Liverpool edge Chelsea on penalties to set up Carabao Cup quarter-final against Bournemouth

Fleetwood Town have earned a home Carabao Cup quarter-final against Everton or Newcastle after pulling off a remarkable upset against Arsenal.

The League Two side will again play at Highbury having become the first club from the fourth division to reach the last eight since Colchester United in 2019/20, and await the winner of the final fourth-round tie. It was a tough draw, meanwhile, for League One’s Bradford City, who must travel to the Etihad Stadium to take on holders Manchester City.

Elsewhere, Andoni Iraola faces a reunion with Bournemouth after his Liverpool side overcame Chelsea in a tense penalty shootout. An encounter between Crystal Palace and Sunderland completes the last-eight line-up, with the semi-final places to be settled in the week of 14 December.

Follow all of the latest from the draw with our live blog below:

News.title: Liverpool edge out Chelsea with penalty shootout victory in Carabao Cup
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

As Xabi Alonso can testify, Liverpool and Chelsea have history when it comes to penalties. As a man who won both the Champions League and the FA Cup on spot kicks in his time at Anfield knows, their trophies can come courtesy of a prowess from 12 yards.

And so there was a certain predictability that Alonso’s return to Anfield ended in a shootout, and that Liverpool won it. Chelsea have had five shootouts against them and lost them all, starting in the 2007 Champions League semi-finals, when Alonso was among the Liverpool scorers. Chelsea had lost, too, in the 2019 Super Cup, the 2022 Carabao Cup and the 2022 FA Cup. “Once we reached the penalties there is going to be a sad sight,” said Alonso. There is for Chelsea, anyway.

open image in gallery Xabi Alonso's Anfield return ended in disappointment ( Getty )

An evening with some terrific penalties ended with a terrible one, Wesley Fofana skying Chelsea’s eighth of the shootout, and ninth of the night, into the Kop. That both players who had conceded spot kicks in the first half missed them at the end of the game may have been a coincidence; at least Ryan Gravenberch’s mishaps did not cost Liverpool.

But for Alonso, with Chelsea in a rare season out of Europe, the first chance of silverware is gone. For the third time in six seasons, Liverpool have knocked them out of this tournament. “It is a small setback, probably the least important competition,” said Alonso, but Chelsea have not won a domestic cup since 2018. Meanwhile, Liverpool are taking the hard route towards a third Carabao Cup in six seasons. After facing Spurs and Chelsea, they have got Iraola’s old club in the quarter-finals. “The only thing I wouldn’t want is Bournemouth,” he lamented. “We haven’t been lucky with the draws.”

Yet Liverpool had much else to enjoy, including the fact the ultimately decisive spot kick was converted by Joe Gomez, who has never scored a goal in 12 seasons and 278 games at Anfield.

Alexis Mac Allister, Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola had also found the net from 12 yards; that all bar Gakpo were substitutes may have rewarded Andoni Iraola for his Carabao Cup policy of holding some of his premier players back and introducing them for the closing stages. “When I have done the last subs and I put Alexis and Alex on, it starts to be in your head,” said Iraola. “Those are the best ones probably that you can put.”

Chelsea were at least spared an unwanted action replay when Kostas Tsimikas, who had scored the winning penalty against them at Wembley in 2022, missed the target after Valentin Barco hit the post. There had been no saves in the first 12 penalties, then two in two, Mike Penders parrying Ryan Gravenberch’s effort and Giorgi Mamardashvili stopping from the debutant Emmanuel Emegha.

open image in gallery Morgan Rogers fired Chelsea into the lead from penalty spot ( Getty )

open image in gallery Cody Gakpo levelled with a converted penalty of his own ( PA )

On a night of 18 penalties, the only goals in regulation time also came from 12 yards as they traded penalties, both conceded stupidly and needlessly in swift succession.

Gravenberch had ploughed through Moises Caicedo and Rogers scored; but for Cole Palmer’s sending off against Tottenham, he would have been on spot-kick duties. But then Gakpo, too, is normally further down the queue to take them for Liverpool.

However, he drilled in his spot kick after Fofana handled the ball in his attempts to stop Virgil van Dijk from meeting Tsimikas’ corner. No sooner had Chelsea been gifted a lead than they presented Liverpool with a leveller.

There could have been a winner thereafter. After his traumatic outing against Tottenham, Penders made a brilliant save to repel Ronald Araujo’s header. It was redemptive, too, when he denied Barcola, the rookie showing his considerable talent. “He looked really solid,” said Alonso.

open image in gallery Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders had a fine game including denying Ryan Gravenberch during the penalty shootout ( PA )

open image in gallery Wesley Fofana’s wayward penalty kick decided the game in Liverpool’s favour ( Getty )

At the other end, Mamardashvili denied Marco Palestra a first Chelsea goal when the summer signing was supplied by Rogers. Over the 90 minutes, the scoreline was probably fair. They cancelled each other out.

Alonso can be flexible in his tactics and sought to match up his boyhood friend Iraola’s system. His Chelsea played 4-4-1-1; so, two decades ago, did Rafa Benitez’s Liverpool teams. There were echoes of the past, some of the rancour of the clashes of the 2000s. When the Anfield crowd saluted one of the heroes of 2005, a Spaniard signed by Rafa Benitez, they were singing about Luis Garcia, not Alonso.

Another of Liverpool’s finest midfielders of the 21st century, Henderson, was greeted with boos on his return to Anfield, largely for joining Chelsea but a Champions League-winning captain held his nerve to score his spot kick as the Kop jeered. If Henderson’s move to Stamford Bridge was a surprise, so was his deployment here, in an unexpectedly advanced role as a No 10. Perhaps it made him the deputy for the suspended Palmer. His Liverpool counterpart was James McConnell, another holding midfielder playing just behind a lone striker.

With more defensively-minded personnel in attacking areas, perhaps it was unsurprising there were few chances. There was a shortage of creativity, a surfeit of caution. With Joao Pedro injured and Palmer out, Chelsea only had one of their first-choice front three. Liverpool kept their three biggest buys in reserve, three £100m on a bench that cost more than half a billion pounds. Each came on, and each scored in the shootout while Chelsea ended up with three misses.

News.title: Worker rights pioneer Dolores Huerta wanted others to feel seen
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Dolores Huerta had spent decades advocating for labor rights and marginalized people when she went to a central California college and met a group of farmworkers’ descendants — many of them students who choked back tears over the then-94-year-old taking the time to listen to them.

That was the effect Huerta had on young people, said Ana Padilla, executive director of the Community and Labor Center at the University of California, Merced, which had hosted Huerta for the event.

“It was transformative,” Padilla said. “Something that I heard a lot from students in particular was just how accessible she was. That’s just what made Dolores a natural organizer, just an ability to connect immediately with really anyone.”

The activist and icon who helped improve the lives of laborers in farming and other industries died Wednesday from cancer at 96. She was surrounded by family at her home in Bakersfield, California.

While most people would spend their golden years enjoying retirement, Huerta never stopped fighting. Living up to her famous rallying cry, “Sí, se puede!" (“Yes, it can be done”), the civil rights activist marched alongside protesters, spoke on countless panels and lent her voice to progressive causes well into her 90s. And it wasn't just on issues impacting Latinos but also African Americans, the LGBTQ+ community and women. Not just an organizer, Huerta during every major election encouraged voters and endorsed candidates. She also pushed more Latinos to consider running for office.

Even after Huerta revealed in March that she was among the women and girls who say they were sexually abused by César Chavez, the labor leader she was inextricably linked to in history, admiration for her only strengthened.

Huerta once said she simply wanted encourage younger generations, particularly women, to use their voice.

“I hope that they know they have a place,” Huerta told The Associated Press in August while attending the Los Angeles premiere of the documentary, “American Pachuco.”

“Never be afraid to take the leadership,” she said.

A living Latina legend who continued to show up

From the United Farm Workers union to the Latino Victory Project, many groups said they would not exist if not for Huerta. She co-founded with Chavez the National Farm Workers Association in 1962. It would become the United Farm Workers of America a few years later and then join with the Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee.

The movement fought for better wages and working conditions for agricultural workers such as fair hours and access to bathrooms. Her work has garnered her accolades including the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, in 2012.

Her leadership has made Huerta almost a mythical figure especially in Latino households. Anabelle Sanchez, 20, of Lansing, Michigan, texted her parents when she learned of Huerta's death. Sanchez, who is Mexican American, was a child when her mother taught her about Huerta.

“I've always looked up to her. She was very civically involved throughout her life and just using her voice even when things were scary,” said Sanchez, a Michigan State University political science and public policy major who hopes to emulate Huerta's “strength and her courage.”

“She was a part of everyday life and she would always go to events like pretty much up until her last breath,” Sanchez said. “Always being an advocate, thinking of others who may not have that opportunity. That's just something that will always stay with me about her."

Irasema Coronado, director of Arizona State University's School of Transborder Studies, became friends with Huerta over 20 years ago when they met at a feminist-centered conference on a cruise ship. She remembers Huerta as someone with boundless energy who showed up for people. She recalls Huerta attending a protest in Phoenix and then leaving immediately after to make appearances at demonstrations in New Mexico and Texas.

“She was everywhere," Coronado said. “She never missed an opportunity to be on the right side of something. I never saw her with a script. It was from the heart."

An unapologetic feminist

During the farmworkers movement of the 1960s, Huerta put up with a great deal of sexism being the only woman in the room.

“She was expected to be quiet and stay in the background and instead, she was out in front and demanding change," said Kathy Spillar, executive director of the Feminist Majority Foundation, of which Huerta served on the board.

The two women met at a conference for the National Organization for Women in the late 1980s. Spillar approached Huerta with the idea of launching the foundation.

“It was the only way that the issues Dolores was talking about could be addressed,” Spillar said. “She said, ‘Sign me up. I’m with you.’ And that was the beginning of almost 40 years.”

Spillar met Huerta around the time that a police officer attacked and beat Huerta. On Sept. 14, 1988, while protesting outside an appearance by then-Republican presidential candidate George H.W. Bush in San Francisco, she was beaten with a baton. Huerta was hospitalized with broken ribs, a ruptured spleen and other injuries. She later won an $825,000 settlement from the city.

But, that ordeal also got Huerta thinking about how to help others besides farmworkers, Spillar recalls. Huerta noticed the women caring for her at the hospital as she recovered from the police assault were under-appreciated.

“They all would talk with her about the struggles that they faced,” Spillar said. “And she decided, I think then, that she was going to become very active in the feminist movement.”

A larger-than-life figure who connected with people

Many schools in California bear the name Dolores Huerta. The state also joins Washington, Oregon and New Mexico in marking her legacy on her April 10 birthday.

However, after the revelations about Chavez's abuse, Huerta rejected pledges by some to use her name as a replacement for his on streets, schools and other sites. Instead, those places “should not be renamed after her, but the UFW martyrs, organizers, farmworkers, and families who sacrificed everything to build something bigger than any one person," a spokesperson for Huerta told The San Francisco Standard earlier this year.

Huerta used her influence when it felt needed. That's how the labor center in Merced was officially founded in 2020, Padilla said, after the labor rights pioneer lobbied state lawmakers to fund it.

Talking to students there was among Huerta's favorite things.

“She would want to spend as much time as she could with you and regardless of your standing,” Padilla said. “She treated folks the same.”

___ Associated Press writers Leslie Ambriz in Los Angeles and Fabianna Rincon in New York contributed to this report.

News.title: Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out
News.content:
Unfortunately for Chelsea, Wesley Fofana put his hand up twice. Firstly to concede the first-half penalty for handball that allowed Liverpool to equalise quickly after Chelsea themselves had scored from the spot.

And then secondly to volunteer to take one of the penalties in the shoot-out. The defender had to score to keep Chelsea in it, but he woefully, nervously skied his effort high into a gleeful Kop and it was Liverpool who went through to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

There the reward for Andoni Iraola, the head coach, is a home tie against the club he left in the summer: Bournemouth. The draw has opened up for Liverpool, and they know it, with only Manchester City left of the other big guns. But despite again playing at Anfield, they would have preferred not to face such a dangerous and motivated opponent, who have just reeled off five wins and five clean sheets in a row under Iraola’s replacement, Marco Rose.

This was also a big win. A meaningful win. One that was celebrated as such with Dua Lipa’s One Kiss – an anthem on Jürgen Klopp’s run to Liverpool’s first Champions League Final under him in 2018 – played over the loudspeakers at the end as the players joyfully milled around the pitch.

News.title: Burnham rules out calling early election
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. John Healey has promised to offer households “breathing space” in his maiden Budget today.

The Chancellor insisted the economy has shown “resilience” in the face of the energy shock from the Iran war.

However, he admitted the conflict has pushed up the cost of living, “piling pressure on the families, on businesses, and on our public finances”.

Among the measures the Chancellor is expected to announce are plans to scrap standing charges on household gas bills – saving families up to £50 a year.

Mr Healey said: “We can’t stop these shocks that hit Britain, but we can make Britain more resilient when they do.

“So, this Budget is designed to give households breathing space from some of the everyday costs, provide targeted support for businesses and self-employed people, and to start the long-term action needed to get energy costs down for good.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Healey prepares to slash household gas bills by £50 | Chancellor to scrap standing charges on gas bills and curb Energy Secretary’s power

2) Minimum wage rise will drive up food prices, Healey warned | Manufacturers say they are already struggling to cover soaring production costs

3) Poundland directors quit in stand-off over administration | Board members fear owner wants to steer retailer into insolvency

4) Google attacks UK over ‘unlawful’ AI plans | Search giant fights plans by competition regulator to force it to promote rivals

5) Netherlands to cut 25,000 civil service jobs in AI push | Police and defence will be exempt from plans to trim 15pc of government workforce in next decade

What happened overnight

Ahead of the Budget, oil prices rose after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude exporter, which has renewed concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East.

Brent crude was up 1.7pc to nearly $116 a barrel, maintaining inflationary pressure on the global economy. It traded around $70 before the start of the Iran war.

Meanwhile, Asia stocks rallied amid fresh enthusiasm about AI.

South Korea’s Kospi surged more than 6pc and was on track for its largest one-day gain since July, after chipmaker SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold jump in quarterly profit and said it would return about $75 billion to shareholders this year.

The AI rally faces its next test when technology giants Alphabet and Microsoft report earnings after market close later today, with investors looking for evidence of returns that would justify the hefty cost of the AI build-out.

In Asia, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 1.7pc, with Japan’s Nikkei adding 1.1pc and ⁠China’s CSI300 blue-chip index climbing 0.7pc.

News.title: Government remains tight-lipped on aid spending in Autumn budget
News.content:
The government made no mention of plans to restore aid spending in the Autumn budget and is on track to miss its current aid commitment.

It had been rumoured that a Burnham government planned to reverse the overseas aid cuts made by Sir Keir Starmer, who reduced an already shrunken aid budget from 0.5 to 0.3 per cent of gross national income (GNI) in February 2025.

The current 0.3 per cent allocation is the lowest proportion of national income spent on aid since 1999.

It was expected the reversal would be drawn up as part of a wider shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) under Ed Miliband as foreign secretary, The Telegraph reported in September.

But there was no mention of any timeline for restoring Britain’s overseas development assistance to the legally enshrined 0.7 per cent of gross national income GNI target on Wednesday.

The UK is now also on track to miss its 0.3 per cent aid spending commitment, equivalent to £9.2 billion per year, following a failure to confirm any upwards adjustment to the UK aid budget to account for inflation.

The shortfall is estimated to fall at £410 million this year, an analysis from the Centre for Global Development (CGD) found.

Britain’s aid money is spent across the world in sectors like health, education, disaster relief, and helping to promote democracy.

News.title: Fleetwood knock out Arsenal in one of biggest shocks in League Cup history
News.content:
An unfamiliar opponent at a very familiar sounding venue, Arsenal play Fleetwood Town for the first time this evening at the Lancashire club’s Highbury Stadium.

Fleetwood, 18th in League Two, are the lowest-ranked team remaining in this season’s League Cup, having booked their place in the fourth round thanks to a victory at Sheffield United.

They were playing in English football’s sixth tier in 2009, and so while their stadium may share its name with Arsenal’s former home, the two clubs are worlds apart.

The League Cup is fourth of four competitions on Arsenal’s list of priorities, but Mikel Arteta should be able to rotate extensively while progressing to the quarter-finals. With a trip to Anfield on Sunday, that is a welcome luxury.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres are seasoned internationals in need of minutes and in line to start.

Max Dowman lit up Arsenal’s third-round victory at Ipswich Town, and 17-year-old centre-back Marli Salmon was not far behind him. Young striker and Northern Ireland international Ceadach O’Neill is also expected to be involved, and he may be joined by other academy players.

While attention is fixed on Premier League and Champions League success, Arsenal’s stinging defeat by Manchester City in last season’s final of this competition will not have been forgotten by Arteta or his players.

Matt Lawlor, Fleetwood’s manager, was full of praise for Arsenal in his pre-match press conference: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch. The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.

“We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”

Arteta has told his players that they must keep their standards high, with a lack of concentration or professionalism potentially their worst enemy against fourth-tier opposition.

Arteta said: “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.



“We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that’s why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game.”



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: High temperatures linked to more than 700,000 deaths in 2023, study estimates
News.content:
Record-breaking temperatures killed an estimated 710,00 people globally in 2023, an increase of more than 36 per cent since 2015, according to new research.

A report on climate change and health by the Lancet medical journal shows that since the Paris climate agreement was introduced in 2016 the number of deaths linked to heat has rocketed.

Between 2006 and 2015 the average annual number of deaths attributed to heat stood at around 398,400 but between 2016 and 2023 the number increased to an annual average of 540,800, hitting a high of 710,000 in 2023.

The authors of the Lancet study say that extreme heat, which is linked to cardiovascular problems and is particularly dangerous for older people, pregnant women and those with other health conditions, must be considered a global health emergency. And they warn that the risks from high temperatures have accelerated in recent years.

News.title: Nigeria’s women and girls impacted the most by British and US funding cuts, committee is told
News.content:
UK and US aid funding cuts in Nigeria have impacted the country’s women and girls more than other groups, MPs were told on Tuesday.

Nigeria has been among the hardest-hit countries as many Western governments have slashed overseas development budgets to increase defence spending.

At the International Development Committee’s first hearing on the impact of aid cuts on global health in Africa, MPs were told that UK government cuts had impacted water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) programmes in Nigeria significantly, putting women and girls at risk.

“WASH is one of the lowest-funded areas in UK government support to Nigeria. WASH enables girls to stay in school, enables them to manage their menstruation effectively, enables women to give birth safely, and protects the lives of children under 5,” Evelyn Mere country director of Water Aid Nigeria said.

“The UK government says one of its priorities is that it will educate girls, empower women and make sure their voices are heard. It means that the UK says one thing, but with the aid cuts does another,” she added.

The British Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO) announced earlier this year it would reduce its aid spending in Nigeria by 50.2 per cent over the next three years, from £136 million in 2025 to £68 million by 2029.

Nigeria has also faced substantial funding reductions from the US after the Trump administration shuttered USAID, the government’s foreign assistance arm. This included more than $600 million (£450 million) in health funding.

An FCDO internal impact assessment, published in July 2025, acknowledged that the biggest casualties of African funding cuts would be frontline WASH and women’s health programmes.

“Overall, any reductions to health spending risk an increase in disease burden and ultimately in deaths, impacting in particular those living in poverty, women, children and people with disabilities,” the assessment concluded.

The winger is loved by the Chelsea fans who believe he has that something special in his locker.

Sports.content:
Next

XABI ALONSO left Anfield disappointed after his former club Liverpool got the better of Chelsea in a brilliant penalty shootout, with the decider missed by Wesley Fofana.

A cagey first half was a tale of two penalties, with Moises Caicedo brought down inside the box which saw Morgan Rogers open the scoring after 40 minutes in the absence of Cole Palmer.



But three minutes later, Liverpool struck back via the same means.

A woeful handball from Wesley Fofana following a corner saw Cody Gakpo step up to level the scoring.



Liverpool had the better of the chances throughout the second half, bringing on all of their £100million men in the form of Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola, and Alexander Isak, but they still couldn’t find a winner as the game went to penalties.

It looked as though it was over when Valentin Barco struck the post with Chelsea‘s fourth penalty kick, only for Kostas Tsimikas to sky the ball high over the crossbar to send the game to a sudden death.

Chelsea then missed their chance to win the shootout at 5-5 when Emanuel Emegha was denied by Giorgi Mamardashvili, after Alexander Isak was kept out by Mike Penders moments prior.

It was Wesley Fofana who missed the eventual deciding penalty, with the Reds winning it 6-5 on penalties in the end.

SunSport’s Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield has given his ratings for the Chelsea players…

MIKE PENDERS – 8

There wasn’t a lot he could do to stop a Cody Gakpo equaliser that found the bottom left corner, and he made two brilliant stops – one from point blank range to deny Ronaldo Araujo, and another to keep Bradley Barcola out with half an hour to go.

Confident with the ball at his feet, and made a good stop to deny Alexander Isak to see the Blues win the shootout.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 6

You would imagine Josh Acheampong is one of those better equipped than most to deal with former Cobham wonderkid Rio Ngumoha, and he did so relatively well despite being booked for a foul on him.

Ngumoha is a talent that would cause anyone problems, and he did for Acheampong, who could have also offered more going forwards but was decent in defence.

WESLEY FOFANA – 2

Just two minutes and twelve seconds – that’s all it took for Wesley Fofana to give away a penalty for handball moments after Chelsea had scored one of their own – and it was a really silly handball to give away too.



Didn’t improve massively after that either really, and Chelsea fans will be disappointed to see Maxence Lacroix hobble off because it means Fofana will probably start against Man Utd next time round…

His deciding penalty, skied over the crossbar, put the cherry on the cake for the Frenchman in a disasterclass of a performance.

MAXENCE LACROIX – 6

Chelsea fans and Xabi Alonso would have been very disappointed to see Lacroix replaced before half time with what looked like a hamstring injury, as he limped off at Anfield.



He was decent up until he hobbled off, making plenty of clearances and being strong in the air in particular against a youthful Liverpool front line.

MALO GUSTO – 3

Played a good pass into Caicedo to win the first penalty of the game, but was pretty pathetic aside from that.

A second-half dive could have cost Chelsea, which saw him embarrassingly take off his own boot in protests for a foul and then hooked for Marco Palestra.

All around underwhelming performance from someone who hasn’t played many minutes under Alonso this season.

MOISES CAICEDO – 6

Unsurprisingly, the best of Chelsea’s midfielders, and formed a decent base to the Blues midfield alongside Romeo Lavia, as well as winning the penalty for the opening goal.



He was excellent in keeping possession for the Blues, even if he did so for a little too long at times, and was important in beating the LFC press.

ROMEO LAVIA – 5

One thing about Romeo Lavia is that he will always be ready to put in a performance against Liverpool.

There were a few too many sideways passes, with Chelsea needing him to advance the ball a bit more in the first half given that they played with a midfield three, and he was booked for a silly foul on Ngumoha.

JORDAN HENDERSON – 5

Sections of Anfield booed Jordan Henderson’s every touch, who looked like he wanted to take Morgan Rogers’ penalty against his own former club.

He was a leader in the side, and steady in midfield, but didn’t offer anything exceptional on another Anfield return.



Usually, that would be okay, but the Blues needed more creativity from him in the middle of the park as the most advanced of the Blues’ midfield trio.

PEDRO NETO – 5

Neto started over Estevao who has history against Liverpool, which may not have been the right decision from Xabi Alonso.

He didn’t get an awful lot of support from Acheampong behind him, but needed to do more going forwards with the ball at his feet in a pretty toothless Chelsea front line.



MORGAN ROGERS – 6

Scored the opener from the penalty spot, and it was expertly taken in Cole Palmer’s absence to bury the ball in the top right corner.

But aside from that, he didn’t seem like the Morgan Rogers we have got used to seeing this season without Joao Pedro and his pal Palmer up there with him.

He did improve as the game went on in terms of his creativity and physicality, and should have had an assist if not for the paws of Mamardashvili in the Liverpool goal, who denied substitute Marco Palestra.



DANNY WELBECK – 3

Struggled to get into the game at all in the first half, and didn’t offer much in terms of pressing against a fairly comfortable Liverpool defence for the most part.

Hooked for Emanuel Emegha who made his full Chelsea debut after 67 minutes, having not made much impact at all.

SUBS:

LEVI COLWILL (MAXENCE LACROIX, 45) – 7

Was utterly solid after coming on for the injured Lacroix, and good at playing out from the back too.

Scored a cracking penalty in the shootout too.

EMANUEL EMEGHA (DANNY WELBECK, 67) – 4

All eyes were on Emegha making his long-awaited Chelsea debut in the absence of Joao Pedro, but he wasn’t overly impactful after replacing Danny Welbeck.



Displayed a few decent touches, but nothing that will fill Chelsea fans with much hope, though a half-hour cameo away at Anfield for your debut, with the game level can’t be easy.

Will be utterly disappointed to have missed what could have been the winning penalty at Anfield.

VALENTIN BARCO (MOISES CAICEDO, 67) – 5

It’s credit to him that Chelsea were not significantly worse with him on the pitch instead of Moises Caicedo, as he always remained an option for his teammates and defended with all his might.

Missed his spot kick.

MARCO PALESTRA (MALO GUSTO, 67) – 5

Was almost instantly more impressive than Malo Gusto when he came close to giving his side the lead with a low strike near the end of the game.

Sports.title: Liverpool 1 Chelsea 1 (6-5 pens): Fofana horror show sees Reds secure FIFTH penalty shootout win over Blues
Sports.content:
Next

IT JUST gets better for Andoni Iraola.

But it isn’t getting any easier for Xabi Alonso and Chelsea.



Liverpool chief Iraola knows that getting silverware in his hands will go a long way to convincing the Anfield fans that he is the man with a plan.

And as Liverpool won a penalty shoot out against the Blues for the FIFTH time out of five, it left Alonso’s realistic trophy hopes now relying on the FA Cup.



A night that flickered into life with two spot kicks in three minutes before the break ended up leading to a full quota of them after 90 minutes.

Morgan Rogers had barely finished celebrating his successful conversion before Wesley Fofana’s crazy handball allowed Cody Gakpo to level it up, no chance for Mike Penders.



With neither side able to find a winner in a second half that was only marginally better than the turgid opening period, it went down to the collective and individual test of nerve.

Both sides blinked. Konstantinos Tsimikas spooked over with the chance to win it after Valentin Barco hit the post, before Penders’ save from Ryan Gravenberch counted for nothing as debut-making Emmanuel Emegha took a shocker.

And when Joe Gomez slammed home, Fofana’s nightmare evening saw his effort flying high into the Kop.

Misery for Alonso, who was not the only former Liverpool midfielder returning to Anfield in the blue corner.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Indeed, unlike his manager, Jordan Henderson lifted the Prem trophy in his days as a Red.

Tonight, though, as part of a midfield trio alongside Moises Caicedo and Romeo Lavia, he was pitted against Trey Nyoni – still in nappies when Henderson started his professional career 18 years ago.

It meant Chelsea reverting to a back four, with Malo Gusto pressed into action on the left to help keep Cody Gakpo under lock and key.



Gusto, though, looked the weakest link, especially when he had the ball at his feet.

Fortunately for the Frenchman Liverpool – with the thick end of £400m-worth of talent on the bench as Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola sat huddled against the cold – were equally sloppy.

The only exercise for ref Darren England was to produce yellow cards for two of the Liverpool youngsters, Lewis Koumas for a late foul on Maxence Lacroix and James McConnell for what would have been deemed a deliberate knock-on at Twickenham.

There were brief moments, Virgil van Dijk – in a rare early round start in the competition – turning on the afterburners to thwart Danny Welbeck’s dart through the middle before centre-back partner Ronald Araujo eased Rogers off the ball.

Rio Ngumoha was a bright light on the Liverpool left yet it was beyond underwhelming.



Half-time seemed set to arrive without even a shot worthy of the name before Gravenbech gifted Chelsea the lead.

When Gusto rolled in to Caicedo, there was no need for the Dutchman to make any challenge.

The Chelsea man was going away from goal, with no real threat.

Yet Gravenberch slid in, wildly, sending Caicedo flying and giving whistler England no real option.



After some silliness – Henderson enjoying the role of pantomime villain as he carried the ball 50 yards before passing on responsibilities – Rogers sent Giorgi Mamardashvili the wrong way from the spot.

But within three minutes, Fofana, quite literally, handed Liverpool a way back to parity.

Fofana was one of THREE Chelsea players marking van Dijk from Konstantinos Tsimikas’ outswinger and any of them could have dealt with the delivery.

Instead, brainlessly, Fofana stuck his right hand above his head to paw it away.



Again, only one decision, Gakpo equally as effective from 12 yards as Rogers had been earlier.

It was Gakpo’s 11th Carabao Cup goal in his four seasons in England and seventh in as many Anfield games in the competition.

And when Lacroix then pinged his hamstring as Gakpo drew the first actual save of the match from Mike Penders before the interval, the pendulum seemed to have swung firmly in Liverpool’s direction.



Not so. Indeed, had Rogers’ touch not been horribly heavy when Henderson nodded him clear at the start of the second period, it might have been different.

Soon afterwards, a Rogers strike, parried by Mamardashvili, would surely NOT have counted after the ball struck his right forearm.

Enter the Liverpool big guns, Wirtz and Barcola on and an instant switch in intensity.

Penders stood firm to parry after Araujo ghosted in behind his defence and then plunged low to his left when Barcola’s shot deflected off replacement Levi Colwill.

Two good stops by a man in the spotlight before Alonso gave a belated debut to Emanuel Emegha, who announced himself by barging into Van Dijk.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

They were matched by Mamardashvili, flying low by his right post to thwart substitute Marco Palestra.

While Colwill blocked Wirtz in front of goal, defending that took it all the way. Liverpool stayed stronger.

Sports.content:

GERONIMO!

Manchester City’s Argentine back-up keeper was the hero as he saved the skins of the holders with two stops in the shootout.



Former Marseille man Geronimo Rulli denied Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to give an enthralling tie a gripping ending.

First choice Gianluigi Donnarumma was one of five players given a short break by Enzo Maresca after a difficult couple of weeks for him.



And what must the Italy international have been thinking as he watched his understudy take centre stage?

Whatever the future holds for City in light of the cheating scandal engulfing the club, they are not going anywhere quietly.



And twice they came from behind here to keep their hopes of winning this competition for an eighth time in the modern era alive.

The good news for those at the Etihad is that they will get to watch a rematch in the Prem in just three days’ time.

It was the visitors who took the lead on the half hour as Jack Hinshelwood held the ball up well and laid off to Georginio Rutter whose low cross found Malick Yalcouye.

The Ivorian international managed to stay onside and his shot from close range could only be pushed into the corner by home keeper Rulli.

Normally the VAR would have had a look and it would have been tight for offside – but it was not in operation here and the goal stood.

Yet the home side hit back as Floyd Samba burst into the box and Albion defender Jaouen Hadjam appeared to handle.

The ref waved play on as the loose ball dropped for Phil Foden and the England ace smuggled it across to Mateo Kovacic.

The veteran Croatian still had plenty to do but his low 20-yard shot curled away from the diving Jason Steele and kissed the post on its way in.

City could even have gone in at the break in front but skipper Marc Guehi got his header from Ayyoub Bouaddi’s cross all wrong.



Instead it was the visitors who retook the lead around 90 seconds after the restart with a superbly taken goal.

Maresca had made two changes and maybe his team were still settling as Hadjam’s low cut-back from the left was steered home stylishly by Rutter.

The French forward twice could have put the tie to bed.

He was teed up by Yalcouye but Rulli made a spectacular save to push his effort over, then he danced around City’s back-up keeper only to fire his effort into the side netting from a tight angle.

Fabian Hurzeler‘s men – who knocked United out in the last round – looked set to make it a Manchester double.



But the home side were still in it and went in search of an equaliser with Rayan Cherki and Rico Lewis both going close.



Not surprisingly the French maestro was involved as they did pull level.

His low free-kick from the edge of the box clipped the heels of young Brazilian defender Vitor Reis to completely wrong-foot Jason Steele.

Albion sub Mats Wieffer could have won it late on as he crept onto a corner at the back post but bundled his shot against the post.

Meanwhile City’s record signing Enzo Fernandez just needed to get a toe on Foden’s injury time free-kick to win it – but could not quite get there.

So it went to penalties and the visitors seemed to have the advantage as Kovacic saw his effort saved by Steele.

BRUNO FERNANDES and Michael Carrick have tried to draw a line under their spat at crisis-hit Manchester United.

The Red Devils captain is now in line to feature at Chelsea on Saturday following clear-the-air talks with under-fire boss Carrick — who is fighting to save his job at Old Trafford.



Fernandes, 32, was openly critical of his gaffer’s tactics following the 4-1 Champions League thrashing in Como eight days ago.

Carrick hit back at the Portuguese playmaker by declaring: “If you don’t run forward or back, you aren’t going to win.”



The fragile truce was brokered after Fernandes was dropped and left on the bench for Sunday’s 3-0 home humiliation by Bournemouth.

Carrick claimed the axing was “for football reasons” — even though his skipper was fit and available.

But the punishment backfired as United extended their winless run to eight games in all competitions.

It emerged the club’s head coach and leader had held face-to-face talks at Carrington on Tuesday as the Red Devils confirmed their former midfielder Carrick, 45, is staying on as boss.

The Geordie will be quizzed on the Fernandes controversy when he faces the media today ahead of the lunchtime visit to West London on Halloween.

And the pair have vowed to focus on trying to turn United’s troubled season around — starting at Stamford Bridge.

Then the PFA Player of the Year returned from Italy to discover his Cheshire mansion had been burgled while on United duty.

And despite being benched against the Cherries, Fernandes was among the flops who were booed following the defeat — just seconds after the fans had applauded Carrick down the tunnel.

Sports.title: 'I had a great time at Man Utd – but I joined City to get revenge on them'
Sports.content:
'I had a great time at Man Utd – but I joined City to get revenge on them'

Manchester United and City are bitter rivals but that has not stopped a few players representing both with one former star explaining his reasons for making such a move

View 2 Images Carlos Tevez joined Manchester City with the intention of getting back at Manchester United (Image: (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images))

Carlos Tevez has revealed getting revenge on Manchester United was why he joined Manchester City. The 42-year-old made a permanent switch from West Ham United to Etihad Stadium in 2009 after opting against joining United following a two-year loan spell.

‌



‌



Those two seasons at Old Trafford were very successful as Tevez scored 34 times out of 99 appearances but his minutes decreased towards the end of his second campaign at the club.

‌



Clarity over his long-term future was unclear during that period with Tevez ultimately joining City in the summer despite reports claiming there was an agreement for him to sign for Real Madrid. The Argentine scored 73 goals in 148 games across four years at City but has since shockingly hinted he made that specific move to get one back on United.

‌



Sir Alex Ferguson's three picks to become Man Utd boss as pressure grows on Michael Carrick READ MORE :

When asked by Rio Ferdinand which club he enjoyed more during his appearance on the Rio Ferdinand Presents channel, he said: "Oh, Rio... Look, I feel like I left a lot, uh, at both teams.

"But if you make me choose, let's say, uh, I had a great time at United. The other team, uh, City, for me, was like a revenge for for, how can I put it, uh, I didn't get back what I gave.

‌



A two-year loan switch is relatively unusual in football and was actually prohibited by FIFA in 2022, but Tevez was amongst the few to complete such a transfer.

After producing some impressive performances, he looked certain to join United permanently, though that situation never materialised with Tevez revealing he held discussions with Sir Alex Ferguson about his future but ultimately believed he failed to honour his commitments.

‌



View 2 Images Carlos Tevez felt Sir Alex Ferguson broke Manchester United promises

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said: "They spoke to me. The two year... How do you say «en préstamo»?'Loan' After, if you play well, pay the contract after one year. Fergie told me, 'Carlos, I'm going to pay out your contract and you're going to stay in Manchester'. The team went to a pre-season in Los Angeles.

"I remember this conversation with Fergie. He said 'I'm going to pay for Berbatov but don't worry, I'm going to buy you the thing and we'll do your contract'.

‌



"For me, the Man United fans understand. You remember in the game the fans speaking to Ferguson. 'Fergie sign him. Sign him up, sign him up.'".

"For me it was... It was hard Rio. It was hard because I felt like I'd given my heart to United. And I didn't feel the same. I didn't feel the same because, uh, if you remember, we won the Champions League. We won the league and, and then, to bring down my price, they brought in a player and I carried on the same way for the first months.

‌



"The second months, let's say, of the second year. But by the second, the second month, I didn't want to know any more.

"I think that Ferguson had, from the day we talked in Los Angeles up to six months to keep his word. And he didn't. On the contrary, he started leaving me on the bench. In my head. He started pushing me aside so he could bring down what I was worth. And that's what hurt me the most."

Sports.title: Liverpool dump out Chelsea on penalties as former favourites face up to new realities
Sports.content:
Liverpool dump out Chelsea on penalties as former favourites face up to new realities

LIVERPOOL 1-1 (Pens: 6-5) CHELSEA: The two Premier League heavyweights couldn't be separated after 90 minutes with Wesley Fofana missing the decisive spot kick

View 4 Images Liverpool got the better of Chelsea on penalties

Liverpool knocked Chelsea out of the Carabao Cup on penalties with Wesley Fofana missing the decisive spot kick in sudden death.

‌



‌



Valentin Barco was the first man to miss in the shootout and his miss presented Kostas Tsimikas with the chance to put the Reds through, but he blazed his effort into the Kop. Jordan Henderson would score the tenth penalty on his return to Anfield to send it into sudden death.

‌



Ryan Gravenberch and Emanuel Emegha missed successive penalties, the latter having the chance to send Chelsea into the next round. But it was Chelsea defender Fofana who fired over, leading to huge celebrations at Anfield.

‌



It was a night of spot kicks with Morgan Rogers opening the scoring in front of the travelling fans, but the Chelsea lead would last a matter of minutes before Liverpool themselves were awarded a penalty. Cody Gakpo scoring emphatically just before half-time.

The Reds went into the shootout having lost their last two, which had major consequences. One of those against Crystal Palace in the Community Shield and the other against PSG in the Champions League.

Andoni Iraola made six changes to his team, but gradually drip fed his quality from the bench. Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola all emerging in the second-half.

‌

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The opening goal of the game came courtesy of a penalty, which was awarded following a reckless challenge from Ryan Gravenberch on Moises Caicedo. Ex-Red Jordan Henderson held the ball for long periods as huge jeers rained down from the Anfield crowd, but he handed it off to Rogers, who confidently converted.

Chelsea's lead though only last three minutes as a Wesley Fofana handball from a corner presented Liverpool with the chance to level. Gakpo scoring in front of the Kop.

‌



Bar the two strikes from the spot in was a first-half lacking in goal mouth action, with neither goalkeeper being regularly called into action.

Wirtz began the evening on the bench but with the game still in the balance Iraola turned to the German just before the hour mark. Mike Penders produced a huge save to deny a Ronald Araujo header, with Rogers racing up the opposite side of the pitch seconds later, only to see his effort blocked.

‌



View 4 Images Wesley Fofana fired into the stands in sudden death

The Chelsea record signing was instrumental in creating a change for Marco Palestra, but the full-back's effort was well saved by Giorgi Mamardashvili. Not long after and a huge block from Levi Colwill denied Wirtz from close range, but neither side was able to find the goal that would've decided the game inside 90 minutes.

‌



REDS ON A ROLL

Liverpool have now enjoyed five wins on the bounce dating back to their Manchester City loss with Iraola looking like he's getting on a roll after his summer switch.

In that time the Merseysiders have shown all sides to them - they quashed the Brighton momentum at the weekend, overcame the challenge that is Brentford away and showcased their powers of recovery against Villarreal in the Champions League.

‌



Getting the better of Chelsea is their latest scalp, and even if the Blues are by no means the side of old, they are still a rival who needed to be dispatched if Liverpool wanted to keep alive their hopes of winning the season's first trophy - which they have done.

View 4 Images Morgan Rogers opened the scoring on the night from the spot

‌



Given Iraola's exploits at Bournemouth plenty was expected, but it has been a slower start than he perhaps would've liked. Nothing quite keeps people happy or builds confidence like winning games and Liverpool are getting into good habits.

HENDO'S FROSTY RETURN

He was the man who captained Liverpool to their first ever Premier League title, completing a comeback from a man who was once deemed surplus to requirement to one who would lead one of their greatest teams. And yet Henderson still felt the backlash from those who once chanted his name.

‌



The midfielder returned to English football with Brentford, but few would've thought at his age that a move to a heavyweight club remained on the cards. Still, Chelsea came calling in the summer.

Henderson enjoyed a sensational period at Anfield under Klopp, also winning the Champions League, but his decision to leave for Saudi Arabia back in 2023 certainly didn't sit well with everyone. This was a player who championed certain causes, which weren't even legal in the Middle East, and there was clearly a financial motive behind his move.

‌



View 4 Images Cody Gakpo levelled shortly before half-time

His reception at Liverpool serves as a reminder that no player's legacy is guaranteed by what they do whilst playing for a club. How they choose to leave and where they go next can often prove defining.

‌



REDS IN BLUE

In a different world perhaps Caicedo and Romeo Lavia would both be playing for Liverpool. But in the summer of 2023 both men, who had been on Jurgen Klopp's radar, chose to move to Stamford Bridge.

The Reds actually had a then British-record bid accepted by Brighton as they looked to go after Caicedo, having also been linked with Lavia, then at Southampton, for much of the summer. Caicedo made it known he wanted to move to Chelsea, and eventually got his wish.

‌



Liverpool were denied the chance to pivot to Lavia with Chelsea, in the midst of another major spending spree, signed him too. Injuries have plagued Lavia but he's finally fit and Caicedo has shown that he's been worth the money. The two lined up in midfield together against Liverpool, who had youngster Trey Nyoni and Gravenberch to oppose them.

Caicedo's well-timed run into the box saw him scythed down by Gravenberch, which led to the opening goal, but it wasn't a night where you thought the two midfields were £140m apart.

Sports.content:
Roy Keane denied Man Utd return by Michael Carrick call as role lined up for ex-captain

Roy Keane could've landed back at Manchester United if Ole Gunnar Solskjaer had been named as interim boss, with the Irishman lined up as his assistant

View 2 Images Roy Keane was in line to be Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's assistant if the Norwegian took charge in Manchester (Image: Dave Shopland/Shutterstock)

Roy Keane could've secured a return to Manchester United had they overlooked Michael Carrick at the start of the year.

‌



‌



Carrick was up against Ole Gunnar Solskjaer as the Old Trafford hierarchy looked to fill the void left by Ruben Amorim's departure in January. Carrick had worked under Solskjaer during his stint at the club.

‌



And it was the ex-Middlesbrough boss who got the nod, but had Solskjaer been given the gig then he would've looked to bring in Keane as his assistant, according to The Sun.

‌



During Solskjaer's previous spell in charge of United, he had Mike Phelan his assistant, but remained close with Keane and has made no secret of his admiration for him and his opinions. He previously said: “I keep in touch with Roy and have been at his house for a cup of tea. I always listen to Roy and his opinions. I value them very highly. I know Roy did an interview saying there are many people that claim to be his friends."

‌



Keane managed Sunderland and Ipswich but has also spent time as a No.2, working underneath Martin O’Neill at Ireland and Nottingham Forest and with Paul Lambert at Aston Villa.

The Irishman won seven Premier League titles, four FA Cups and the Champions League in a 12-year spell at Old Trafford, but endured a high-profile exit in late 2005 following a clash with Sir Alex Ferguson. Keane has previously commented that the Scot's presence at the club may hamper any return.

‌



Carrick ultimately won the race to lead United last term and his stunning interim spell saw him land the job on a permanent basis, keeping ex-England coach Steve Holland as his main lieutenant.

View 2 Images Roy Keane and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer have retained a strong bond (Image: Instagram/ Roy Keane)

‌



Keane had been critical of Carrick's appointment when it first happened and said on the Stick To Football podcast: "His wife can always come in [if Carrick doesn't do well], cause she's got a bit of a big mouth sometimes. She's probably doing the team talk."

The comment stemmed from a feud in 2014, when Keane criticised Carrick's performance in a Champions League defeat to Olympiacos.

Carrick's wife Lisa Roughhead posted on Twitter: "Roy Keane what a ****, says anything to provoke a reaction." She later deleted the tweet and posted an apology.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany 'dislocated shoulder' in collapse as doctors rule out heart attack
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany 'dislocated shoulder' in collapse as doctors rule out heart attack

Vincent Kompany collapsed during a Bayern Munich training session and dislocated his shoulder, but doctors have ruled out a possible heart attack

View 2 Images Vincent Kompany's doctors have tested for a possible heart attack with the Belgian dislocating his shoulder last week (Image: 2026 FC Bayern)

Vincent Kompany is thought to have dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed during a Bayern Munich training session five days ago.

Kompany remains in hospital in Munich with doctors seeking to confirm what caused his collapse, which saw the former Manchester City captain quickly airlifted to hospital.

The Belgian's doctors have reportedly been investigating a potential brain issue amid his period of ill health - and that has meant he's been absent from the touchline since taking charge of Bayern's Champions League draw with Arsenal last week.

Bild reports that Kompany has also suffered seizures after falling. They also claim the issue is not thought to be life-threatening and a heart attack or stroke has also been ruled out. The 40-year-old is not expected back in the dugout for several weeks as he continues his recovery.

The club's interim manager Aaron Danks said on Tuesday: "It looks like he's getting better every day. That's positive. But there is no major news regarding his diagnoses or his return to work."

Harry Kane, who has claimed the Ballon d'Or with Kompany as his manager at the Allianz Arena, revealed he had been in contact with the Belgian before his historic night.

The Englishman said: "He actually phoned me, phoned me bright and early at 9am (Monday). I was just out of bed thankfully, so I was able to answer it. But no, he just wanted to wish me all the best, good luck. I asked him how he was doing, he said he feels good, he feels like he's on the mend. I know he's the type of character who just wants to be back with the team already.

View 2 Images It was during training that the Bayern Munich boss collapsed

"He wants to be out on the training field with us, on the bench with us. But it's important that he rests, you know? He's been going through a bit of a tough time with his health recently, and we can hopefully cover it, the staff can cover it.

"Obviously, he's not there, but, you know, it will be massive for me to go back to Munich and see him, all the staff, all my team-mates. I've spoken about how much this [award] is theirs as well as it is mine. So just to celebrate them a little bit will be special."

Whilst being in hospital Kompany is thought to have received a number of visitors including the club's president Herbert Hainer, sporting director Max Eberl, and honorary president Uli Hoeness.

Sports.title: Inside Man Utd's decision to keep Michael Carrick as five reasons for U-turn emerge
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is set to remain as Manchester United manager. For how long that lasts remains to be seen but in the short-term at least, the former midfielder has been given a stay of execution.

Carrick was under huge pressure after a week that had seen the Red Devils thumped by Como and Bournemouth, while there were also high-profile rants from both Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes which hinted at a dressing room damaged beyond repair.

The writing appeared to be on the wall, with United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox heading to Carrington on Monday for crisis talks. But Carrick actually ended up remaining in situ and will be given time to turn the tide, starting with this weekend’s clash against Chelsea.

The United hierarchy will now face the increasingly challenging task of owning the narrative and persuading critics, their decision was made with sound reasoning. Here are the factors that ultimately decided the saga...for now.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Disagreement on replacement

The first - and arguably most troublesome - issue that United chiefs have been attempting to navigate is the fact that they would have to find a replacement for Carrick. And that’s not a task that is expected to be easy despite there being some favourites to claim the job already.

Former Chelsea and Spurs boss Antonio Conte is thought to be open to dialogue but as it stands, United have yet to make an approach.

‌



Another high-profile option is Julian Nagelsmann, the former Bayern Munich coach now available after his spell with the German national team. He is thought to be favoured by United director of recruitment Christopher Vivell but his opinion is expected to be trumped by that of Jason Wilcox.

Eddie Howe is also among the names mentioned and would have had some serious backing had both Dan Ashworth and Sir Dave Brailsford still been at Old Trafford. As it is, the pair have moved on so Howe might not be among the frontrunners after all.

View 3 Images Howe has been mentioned as a potential Carrick replacement (Image: Getty Images)

Compensation packages and Carrick cost

Sticking with Carrick’s potential successor, United also have another headache to navigate and that’s any compensation package they would have to pay out. Should Carrick be sacked, he would be entitled to a severance package given he signed a two-year deal to become the club’s permanent manager in the summer.

‌



It will also represent the third time in as many years that United have prematurely axed their managers, following payouts to Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, who were sacked in 2024 and 2025 respectively.

The payments wouldn't end there either, with the price of acquiring a new man in the dugout likely to be a costly one.

Howe would come at a price due to the terms of his exit from Newcastle and could see United pay out around £6m for his services. Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler also has admirers in Manchester but has already been discounted due to the significant compensation package that the German would command to leave the Amex.

View 3 Images Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada decided to leave Carrick in charge (Image: Getty Images)

‌



International break on the horizon

Timing is also seemingly a big consideration for United chiefs. The Red Devils have three games to play before the second international break of the season, with this weekend’s clash with Chelsea being the first of those.

Italian giants Roma are then their next Champions League opponents, while a testing showdown with Villa follows that before domestic action comes to a pause.

Should United believe a change is the correct course of action, the international break could be a good time in which to do that. That invariably depends on the results that the club get between now and then but it is certainly something to keep an eye on.

Players still onside

One aspect that also appears to be keeping Carrick in a job is the players themselves. Despite his high-profile falling out with Bruno Fernandes, the pair appear to have cleared the air and the Portuguese midfielder is available for this weekend’s game.

‌



Carrick also made sure to hold talks with both players and staff after it became clear that he would still remain in charge. And he made it clear that he wanted everyone on the same page, with winning games at the top of everyone's agenda.

Meanwhile an unnamed player is quoted by BBC Sport as saying: "The feeling is that we all want to put it right. Players, staff, everyone."

So it’s clear that Carrick still has backers in the dressing room, as well as the boardroom. United chiefs and players will be keeping their fingers crossed that was the right decision.

‌

Sports.title: Man Utd told Michael Carrick answers 'no' to two key questions in brutal reality check
Sports.content:
Man Utd told Michael Carrick answers 'no' to two key questions in brutal reality check

Michael Carrick is a man under pressure at Manchester United and a former Chelsea star admits the warning signs regarding his lack of experience were always there

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has presided over a poor start to the season (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been reminded that Michael Carrick was never a top manager when he arrived - nor did he have experience of a club at the top level.

‌



‌



The Red Devils have won just two of their 12 games this season which has seen serious questions asked of Carrick. Many expected him to be sacked in the aftermath of the Bournemouth loss on Sunday, but he has been retained and will remain in charge this weekend.

‌



Carrick's only major job saw him lead Middlesbrough in the Championship but he was handed the reigns at Old Trafford last January, with the original plan for him to manage them until the end of the season.

‌



A stunning interim spell, which saw him record wins over Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool and Aston Villa, had United up to third and he was handed the job full-time - but plenty felt there was still a serious risk and John Obi Mikel has issued some stark reminders.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said on The Obi One Podcast: "The fans are not stupid. The come week in, week out, see what goes on, and they know exactly where the problem lies. Is Michael Carrick a top manager? No. Did he manage at the top level before getting the United job? No.

"But we all knew that it was going to be a learning process. He did a wonderful job last season, got them back into the Champions League for the first time in a long time. Collectively, these Manchester United players are not good enough. They were dreadful to watch, awful to watch. It was a disaster."

‌



Carrick retains the backing of the fans, who sang his name at the weekend despite the dire performance, with their anger very much directed at the players and the hierarchy.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's only major experience had been his stint at Middlebrough (Image: George Wood, Getty Images)

‌



Whilst United have stuck by Carrick for now there are plans being made for the possibility of them changing their manager yet again. Eddie Howe, out of work after leaving Newcastle, and Julian Nagelsmann are two of the frontrunners.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery, Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler and Antonio Conte are three of the other names on the shortlist.

Article continues below

Carrick is understood to have held clear the air talks with Bruno Fernandes, who called out the United boss in the aftermath of their loss at Como. The Portugal star had been left on the bench at the weekend but could well return for Saturday's game at Chelsea.

Sports.title: Spanish Cup matches postponed after tragic train crash leaves at least 64 dead
Sports.content:
Spanish Cup matches postponed after tragic train crash leaves at least 64 dead

Spain has been left devastated after a fatal train crash in the Andalusia region of the country with the nation’s football organisers having taken the decision to postpone Wednesday evening’s fixtures

View 2 Images 24 Copa del Rey matches have been postponed (Image: Getty Images)

The Spanish Football Federation have postponed 24 Copa del Rey games in the aftermath of a devastating train crash in the country.

‌



‌



At least 64 people have died and countless more left with injuries after a high-speed train collided with the back of another in the Toledo region of Spain on Wednesday morning.

‌



A massive rescue effort is now underway to retrieve survivors and treat the wounded. And it has now been confirmed that all of the Spanish cup games set to take place on Wednesday have now been called off.

‌



A statement read: "As a sign of respect and solidarity with all the victims of the tragic train accident that occurred early this Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, the RFEF has suspended all 24 matches of the first round of the Spanish Championship-Copa del Rey originally scheduled for this afternoon and evening, as well as all other matches in competitions organised by the RFEF.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"The RFEF will announce the revised tournament schedule and the final times for the postponed matches in the coming days.

"The great Spanish football family remains united in grief at the tragedy, offering its support to the authorities to help the victims of this devastating accident."

‌



In all, there were 24 fixtures concluded on Wednesday, with top-flight sides such as Real Betis, Valencia and Celta Vigo all among those previously set to be in action.

View 2 Images An ongoing rescue effort is currently underway following Wednesday's train crash (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid are set to enter the competition in December but all have released statements on Wednesday in the aftermath of the crash.

So far, there has been no word on if the rest of the Spanish Cup games across the week will be affected, while this weekend’s La Liga fixtures are currently set to go ahead as planned.

‌



Meanwhile, president of the Andalusian Regional Government, Juanma Moreno, has confirmed three days of official mourning across Andalusia.

In a post on Twitter, he said: "We declare three days of official mourning in Andalusia, from 14:00 today until 14:00 next Saturday, October 31. We are devastated. All of Andalusia stands with the victims of this new railway accident."

Sports.title: Rangers score late to snatch draw on McInnes' Hearts return
Sports.content:
Report as Rangers score late to draw 2-2 with Hearts; Kevin Kelsy opened the scoring for Rangers; goals from Claudio Braga and Calvin Miller gave Hearts the lead; Olwethu Makhanya headed in to rescue a point with Dujon Sterling missing a brilliant chance to snatch a win

Rangers snatched a point on Derek McInnes' Tynecastle return as Hearts held onto their formidable unbeaten home record.

The Gers boss was loudly booed by the home support as he emerged from the tunnel for his first match back in Gorgie since leaving for Ibrox in June, just weeks after the Edinburgh side were pipped to the Premiership title.

But his team silenced a pumped-up home crowd when Kevin Kelsy scored a 16th-minute opener following a lapse from Laurent Mendy.

The hosts emerged with renewed impetus after the break and drew level three minutes into the second half when Caludio Braga rushed in to force the ball over the line from close range.

With Rangers rattled, Hearts went ahead in the 57th minute. Tomas Magnusson nicked possession off Kim Minsu and sent Braga racing down the left. The Portuguese drove into the box and his angled shot broke off Manny Fernandez into the path of Calvin Miller, who drilled home a low finish from seven yards out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hearts capitalised on Rangers mistake to break quickly and Calvin Miller swept home their second at the far post

McInnes sent on Bouanani for Gassama, and the Algerian winger helped give the visitors an increased threat in attack before he delivered the free-kick from the left which was headed home by Olwethu Makhanya with stoppage time approaching.

Dujon Sterling had a brilliant chance to be Rangers' hero in the dying seconds, only to chest the ball straight to Hearts 'keeper Beau Reus.

Rangers remain four points behind Celtic, who drew with Dundee United, and four above Hearts, who are unbeaten in 26 league games at home.

The key moments from Tynecastle Park

2: CHANCE! Kerjota sends in a cross and Fagan-Walcott is just inches from getting his head to it.

11: CHANCE! Minsu sends in a cross as Rangers start to find a way into the game, Raskin gets to it but Hearts clear.

16: GOAL RANGERS! Rangers jump on slack Hearts play. Naderi slips a pass to Kelsy to finish past Reus.

26: SAVE! Kerjota has a shot blocked with Miller's follow-up saved by Pandur.

27: CHANCE! A rash challenge from Fernandez sees Hearts with a free-kick in a dangerous area. Miller whips it in, but Mendy heads over the bar.

48: GOAL HEARTS! Rangers are punished for conceding another free-kick and Braga is the one to get it over the line.

57: GOAL HEARTS! Braga drives into the Rangers box and his deflected strike falls to Miller to smash in.

68: SAVE! Kelsy's header reaches Bouanani, who curls an effort towards goal. It's saved by Reus.

76: SAVE! Pandur is called into action again as Braga is given so much space to shoot from distance.

79: SAVE! Neil whips a shot to the far post, which is stopped by Reus.

83: WIDE! Hearts break but Williams sends fires wide from distance. What a chance to wrap things up.

89: GOAL RANGERS! Makhanya heads in from Bouanini's free-kick to pull level heading into stoppage time.

90+4: CHANCE! Curtis sends in the cross to Sterling who looks certain to knock in a winning goal only to hand Reus a simple save.

'Rangers have stolen a point'

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd at Tynecastle Park:

"Rangers will actually be delighted to leave here with a point tonight.

"Hearts, the amount of games they've had, running on empty, the amount of injuries they've got, they were the better team tonight and that would be worrying.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kris Boyd believes Rangers will be delighted to leave Tynecastle with a draw after being outplayed for long spells by Hearts.

"Rangers will leave here with a point and I'd be absolutely delighted that they've got that point.

"I saw a team out there tonight, Hearts, that have got a style of play. There's nothing wrong with it, but when it doesn't work, you're going to be criticised.

"You see that team that was going long, trying to play for second balls, get up on that. When it doesn't work, it looks so disjointed. Towards the end Rangers got that equaliser and then they had the chance to win it, but they didn't deserve that tonight.

"They wouldn't have deserved the three points. Hearts were by far the team who you felt as if were in control of the game, looked as if they were a team that had been coached in terms of patterns of play, especially the second half.

Image: Olwethu Makhanya scored a late equaliser for Rangers

"Rangers really struggled to deal with Hearts. Emmanuel Fernandez, he looked so at unease with the Hearts attacking players. The amount of times that he caused problems for his own team-mates, again.

"I'll say it, Rangers have stolen a point here tonight. They've stolen a point because, especially that second half, it's got to be better."

Vrancken: 'We lost two points'

Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was a really good performance against a really good side on full strength.

"Actually, we lost two points. I think we had to win here.

"I'm pleased with the reaction because the moments they got was through a mistake of us.

"The first goal was a mistake for us. The performance afterwards makes up for a lot of things there.

"We were good in organisation. We were good at the ball. We were winning second balls, duels.

"We know they were aggressive or they want to be aggressive man but we played through their pressure.

"I'm really happy with the performance today. A pity that we couldn't take the three points."

McInnes: 'Winner would have been unjust'

Rangers manager Derek McInnes speaking to Sky Sports:

"I think we deserve our point.

"If we'd scored a winner there, possibly it would have been unjust.

"I liked how my team kept going, but there was a lot about tonight that I thought we looked very naive at times.

"We've got a young team and this ground can do that to you at times. Sometimes you've just got to stem the tide and sometimes you've just got to stay in the game and do the basics really well.

"I thought the game was a bit topsy-turvy. For us, there was loads we can do better."

Genuine handshake?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Derek McInnes got a noisy reception on his return to Tynecastle and there was almost a flare-up on the final whistle after his handshake riled Hearts manager Wouter Vrancken.

There appeared to be some tension between Vrancken and McInnes at full-time, with both telling Sky Sports what happened...

"I think you have to be like a genuine handshake among colleagues for me. Win, draw, lose," said the Hearts head coach.

"At the end everybody fights for his own team, works hard for his own team and in their way of working so I think it's normal and this is also how it has to be but at the end it has to be a genuine handshake.

Asked if he thought McInnes' handshake was genuine, he added: "I don't think so but afterwards we spoke so I think it's okay."

McInnes had less to say: "I was just telling him how fortunate it is to have such a good squad that I left him," he said. "All good."

What the result means and next fixtures...
