Sports.title: Kompany discharged from hospital after collapsing at training
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital, says board member for ​sports Max Eberl; the former Man City defender collapsed during a second-team training session on Friday; Kompany had missed some duties earlier in the week due to a viral infection

Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has ‌been discharged from hospital following his collapse in training last week ‌due to a meningeal irritation, board member for ​sports Max Eberl said on Wednesday.

Kompany was taken to hospital last week after collapsing at Bayern's training ground during ‌a second-team training session.

He missed out on media duties ahead of Bayern's Champions League match against Arsenal due to a viral infection, but did make it to the dugout for the 2-2 draw.

"Given the circumstances, he's doing ⁠well," Eberl told broadcaster ARD ⁠ahead of the German Cup game against Magdeburg, who Bayern beat 6-1. "He ‌was discharged from the hospital today [Wednesday]. That is the biggest and best news for all of ‌us.

"It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication and I am certain that he will ⁠very soon be back on the ​touchline, operating at 100 per cent."

No date has ​been set for Kompany's return, with ​Eberl saying the Belgian would resume his ⁠duties only after receiving medical clearance, something that was reiterated by his assistant, Aaron Danks.

Speaking after the win against Magdeburg, he said: "I still don't feel like there is any timeline on it [when Kompany is back]. It's obviously a really positive step in his road to recovery.

"He gets to settle back at home now, be closer to his family, be closer to his home comforts but it's still really important that he takes his rest and he recovers. So there is no timescale on it. Nothing that I've been told and I've been informed.

"Our doctors will continue to work closely with Vince and at the right moment, he will be back with us once he is fit and healthy to do that and we look forward to that day.

"But in the meantime, we just continue to push forward as a group with the players and staff and keep working hard.

"I haven't spoken to him for a couple of days now so I still think not much has changed in terms of our working relationship at the moment.

"His health is our number one priority and for us he is still in recovery mode so we want him to get back to full health, full fitness and then join us.

"Over the coming days, weeks, I don't know, things will start to move forward and we can start to engage in more of these conversations.

"But there has been no timescale on that at the moment. It is just purely about his health, his recovery and him taking the time that he needs."

Danks has taken charge of the ⁠team and was ​on the bench for their 3-1 win ​at Freiburg at the weekend. Bundesliga leaders Bayern face title rivals Borussia Dortmund on Saturday.

Sports.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties to reach last eight
Sports.content:
Wesley Fofana missed the decisive spot kick as Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties to set up a Carabao Cup quarter-final against Andoni Iraola's former side Bournemouth.

Fofana, whose handball gifted Liverpool their equaliser from the spot in normal time, scooped his penalty into the Kop after Giorgi Mamardashvili had denied Chelsea debutant Emmanuel Emegha.

Valentin Barco, another substitute, also missed his spot kick, sending his effort onto the post, but Ryan Gravenberch was thwarted by Mike Penders and Kostas Tsimikas fired over to keep a dramatic shoot-out going before Joe Gomez capitalised on Emegha's miss and Fofana fired over.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Rogers put Chelsea in front after Ryan Gravenberch's foul

The goals also came from the spot in normal time, with Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo converting within three minutes of each other as a cagey first half burst into life before the break.

Both penalties were needlessly conceded, with Gravenberch first fouling Moises Caicedo when he was running away from goal, and Fofana then bizarrely raising his hand to touch a Tzimikas corner.

There were chances for both sides to win it in the second half, with Penders saving from substitute Bradley Barcola and Ronald Araujo, and Mamardashvili denying Rogers and Chelsea substitute Marco Palestra. But the two sides could not be separated.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wesley Fofana gifted Liverpool a penalty just minutes after Chelsea's opener

While Chelsea named a strong starting line-up, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola included four youngsters in Trey Nyoni, Rio Ngumoha, James McConnell and Lewis Koumas, and the visitors were unable to make their greater experience count.

The victory makes it five in a row in all competitions for Liverpool. For Chelsea, it's a second consecutive defeat after their Premier League loss to Spurs. The Blues also lost defender Maxence Lacroix to an apparent hamstring injury in the first half.

For Alonso and Chelsea midfielder Jordan Henderson, it all added up to an unhappy Anfield return. Chelsea have now lost five straight penalty shootouts against Liverpool.

Iraola praises Liverpool's youngsters

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola to Sky Sports:

"I think it was quite a level game. Very competitive, not a lot of chances for both teams. There were moments for us, moments for them.

"We are really happy with the performances of a lot of the players and obviously happy to finish on the right end of the penalty shoot-out because it gave us the chance to be in the draw.

On Liverpool's young starters: "I think they did a good job. I think they deserved the right to play because they were also very good against Spurs in the last round. We told them, they are first-team players and we are confident if they have to play.

"They showed us they had a very good level and they helped us a lot."

On Liverpool's winning run: "It's three in a row at home which is very important. We were struggling a little bit at home. Now we have the confidence of winning three in a row and now we have the biggest one against Arsenal on Sunday."

Alonso: It was a proper cup game

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso to Sky Sports:

"That's it with penalties, someone will go home feeling it was harsh to go out. But we saw a proper cup game, intense and really close. Then penalties are open for everything.

"We performed with enough level to compete at Anfield. After scoring the first goal we unluckily conceded the penalty. The game was really close from both sides.

"It was a solid performance. We didn't concede many chances so he didn't have to work a lot but he [Mike Penders] was quite stable and solid. That was very important.

"I saw a team competing and showing a good level. This is the least important competition for us and now the focus is on the Premier League."

Sports.title: History-maker Russo scores hat-trick as Arsenal dismiss Benfica
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo became the highest-ever English goalscorer in Women's Champions League history with a hat-trick against Benfica as Arsenal won 3-0 in their league phase match.

The Gunners No 9 matched Fran Kirby's record (21) with her first-half opener - a low, diagonal effort that beat goalkeeper Lena Pauels.

Her next - a glancing header from Steph Catley's corner - made her the outright record holder, before adding another from the penalty spot after Caitlin Foord was fouled by Catarina Amado, taking her to 23 goals.

"She is everything," Arsenal boss Renee Slegers told Disney+ after the game. "It's hard to know where to start. She is such a humble, nice human being, cares for everything and everyone, does everything to the fullest.

"She trains, does meetings, prepares, recovers. Everything is 100 pre cent and she brings so much quality. There is so much to say about Alessia and it's a privilege for me to work with her.

"To have a player that's world class in the way she plays, the way she attacks, the way she defends, does everything for the team and being this person, it's amazing.

"The whole team is amazing, we have so many good personalities in the group. We care for each other, and Alessia leads the way and she was captaining the team today."

Russo scored the hat-trick in front of England boss Sarina Wiegman - who would also have been impressed by Georgia Stanway. She was also named as captain for the second time in her career.

Perhaps the only blemish on Russo's otherwise brilliant evening was being flagged offside in the build-up to Foord's late fourth, which was ruled out.

Image: Alessia Russo was captain for Arsenal on Wednesday evening

The striker's own form mirrors that of Arsenal, who have won back-to-back games for the first time this season, alleviating the pressure after another poor start.

The result sends them second in the Champions League table - with their next European fixture a huge game at Barcelona on November 12, who they beat to win the title in 2025.

Russo: The derby win would've meant nothing without a win here

Arsenal hat-trick goalscorer Alessia Russo speaking to Disney+:

"It feels really nice. I love playing in the Champions League, especially with Arsenal with what we're building.

"The win was really important after building some momentum against Spurs. It's always loud here at Borehamwood, we love playing here and an important three points.

"We said that the North London derby wouldn't have meant anything if we didn't back it up tonight, so it was really important. Now hopefully we can build going forward.

"You could see how many shots on target we had. We've been really building, focusing on people feeling confident on stepping up and shooting from outside the box.

"Their 'keeper made some great saves and on another night, it might have been even more so a great performance."

Slegers reveals what was different against Benfica

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers to Disney+: "It's been tough for us, haven't got the results and the performances until now.

"The north London derby was really good for us and we said we wanted to back it up. I'm really proud of the players because they did that today. We created a lot of chances, a lot of shots and Alessia's hat-trick.

"There was another way of creating today, our discipline in the press and getting the opportunities going forward. That was a big one for us."

Sports.title: Nketiah steers Palace past Fulham to boost boss Sage
Sports.content:
Eddie Nketiah steered Crystal Palace into the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup as they won 1-0 at Fulham.

The striker scored in the first half of their fourth-round tie at Craven Cottage, to help ease the pressure on under-fire boss Pierre Sage.

Fulham dominated the first half and missed a slew of chances, only to see Palace take the lead with their first shot of the game on 37 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Nketiah puts Crystal Palace ahead against Fulham with a deft finish

Oscar Mingueza burst down the right and crossed for Nketiah to flick in with a deft touch.

Fulham then continued to push after the break, with Alex Iwobi going closest as he forced a point-blank save from Dean Henderson from a corner.

They had another big chance to level in stoppage-time, but Henderson was on hand again to palm away Gonzalo Garcia's header.

The key moments from Craven Cottage

Image: Eddie Nketiah celebrates scoring for Crystal Palace

16: BIG CHANCE! Tete miscues his header at the back post completely unmarked. Fulham should be ahead.

18: SAVE! Fulham have ANOTHER huge chance to score but Robinson's tame effort is saved by Henderson.

37: GOAL! PALACE LEAD OUT OF NOWHERE! Pierre Sage's side are in front with their first shot of the game. Nketiah steers in Mingueza's cross from the right with a deft touch. That is just his 10th touch of the game. That must have been Palace's first attack.

68: FULHAM HAVE TO SCORE! Castagne's flick at the front post helps the cross find Iwobi but his effort is straight at Henderson. The Palace goalkeeper kept that one out with his legs from the close-range effort.

87: HUGE CHANCE! Kamada should wrap the game up for Palace but he sends the shot wide from inside the box.

Arbeloa: Same story against Palace again

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa:

"I'm disappointed. It was a similar game to the one we played some weeks ago [against Palace in the league]. We controlled the game, had the chances and, in the end, they took their chance. One shot, one goal, and they were defending all the time.

"It didn't work. We need to do better against a team like this that defends in a low block. We need to move the ball quicker, look for the wide areas, put in more crosses and do better with the final pass.

"It's another day and the same story, so we need to improve.

"They were not jumping and pressing us. They were defending the space.

"It's not easy against a team that defends with so many players in a tight space. Because of that, you need to move the ball quicker, make more runs in behind, try to put in more crosses and use the wide areas.

"You have to do it for 90 minutes, one time and another time. You need to be patient but aggressive at the same time. We have to do better."

Sage: I know what kind of player Nketiah can be

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage:

"I know what kind of player he is and what kind of player he could be. I spoke with him last week, and the message is what he said. He is right.

"His potential is higher than his performances at the moment. We have to reduce this gap because he needs it, the team needs it and his skills need it.

"In this situation, the fact that he does not play too much and that there is pressure when he does play because he needs to score can be bad for a player. But when he makes that switch, he is able to do very important things for us."

Sage also reserved special praise for goalkeeper Dean Henderson, who made his first appearance since the Premier League win at Fulham at the start of September.

"He is a wonderful goalkeeper. He showed it again today. He is an important captain and an important person. I am very happy for him to come back.

"Dean is a big part of this success and this defensive success. The confidence in him is immense and very important too."

Sports.title: Sunderland's first-half blitz sends them past Brentford into quarters
Sports.content:
Three goals in 13 first-half minutes saw Sunderland blitz past Brentford and into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals with a 3-2 win at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats owed much to 21-year-old Jocelin Ta Bi for his trio of assists to turn the game on its head after Brentford had dominated the early stages - and hit the post, bar and saw a shot cleared off the line in one move at 0-0.

Ta Bi, who joined Sunderland in January but had only featured four times since, was a livewire on the right flank in that first 45 minutes and thought he had opened his account for the club with a low drive that beat Hakon Valdimarsson, only for Chemsdine Talbi to tap home on the line and claim the goal.

Bi's second assist was more intentional after dancing into the box from out wide and pulling the ball back for Timur Tutierov, who sidefooted home a quick second only three minutes later.

Another 10 after that, it was three when Bi's excellent cross picked out Malick Fofana at the far post, and the unmarked Belgian powered a header home.

Callum Wilson gave Brentford hope just before the break when he bundled an effort home from close range before being booed for his Newcastle connections, but the Bees failed to build on that effort and took until the 94th minute for Igor Thiago to turn home Mathias Jensen's effort - by which time, it was too late.

Le Bris hopes win can prove 'powerful' to kick-start season

Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris:

"We know we have a nice challenge this season with the Europa League, the Carabao Cup and the league with a young squad.

"The process is not a straight line. The win can be really powerful because we had to show character and we delivered.

"Jocelin [Ta Bi] is the perfect example. He came from another country, he is so talented. He was brave…and to deliver those three key passes.

"This is the second season in the Premier League with the Europa League, so it is difficult. There is always a fine margin.

"It doesn't disturb the whole process. We have to stay consistent and this was a good step today."

Andrews rues poor goals conceded

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews:

"We were very ambitious in this competition to go as far as we could.

"We approached it in a very diligent way, playing Sunderland recently we know what they are about. We can't concede goals like that in a short space of time, defend like that and expect a good outcome.

"The game is about both boxes. Granted there were some players who haven't played for a while, but we pride ourselves in how we defend as a team.

"It was a crazy game but we have to look at ourselves, how we conceded those goals. You can't describe those 12 minutes of madness. I had full faith in the team, we see them every day in training and unfortunately those minutes have cost us."

What's next?

Sports.title: Man City dump Brighton out of Carabao Cup after shoot-out victory
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup holders Manchester City needed penalties to progress past Brighton and into the quarter-finals after battling from behind to draw the game 2-2 at the Etihad.

Enzo Maresca's side never led on the night but scored four of their five penalties to win the deciding shoot-out 4-3, with Rayan Cherki striking the winner and Geronimo Rulli denying both Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk.

Brighton, the better side for the majority, will consider themselves unlucky to be dumped out of a competition Fabian Hurzeler had earlier professed to want to win. But City stuck to task and eventually prevailed on penalties - Hurzeler gets his chance to enact revenge when the two sides meet again in the Premier League on Saturday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Malick Yalcouye strikes to put Brighton ahead

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Precision from Mateo Kovacic brings Manchester City level

The visitors hit the front twice in the game, the opener struck by an impressive Malick Yalcouye, rounding off a slick Brighton move. There was some surprise in the stadium that the linesman's flag stayed down given Yalcouye's position on the last line, but the midfielder was given the benefit of the doubt with VAR not in operation.

Manchester City, aggrieved by the perceived injustice, tried to up the tempo and eventually got their reward when Mateo Kovacic guided his strike inside the post to equalise. But City's build-up was slow and predictable, without many of their regular starters after Maresca granted five key players a rest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brighton retake the lead less than 90 seconds after the restart

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Vitor Reis or Rayan Cherki?! Deflected free-kick brings Man City level

Just 90 seconds into the second period, City were undone again, Georginio Rutter's first-time finish from Jaouen Hadjam's pull-back giving Brighton the advantage - a lead their brave performance deserved.

As the game became stretched late on, City seemed to get more ragged. But such is the talent in their ranks, it was not long before another leveller unearthed itself.

Rayan Cherki's free-kick took a wicked deflection off Vitor Reis to wrong-foot Jason Steele and set up a grandstand finish, where both sides had chances to win it, but ended up leaving it to the lottery of penalties.

City narrowly avoided the fate that befell fellow Premier League heavyweights Arsenal on Tuesday, eliminated by fourth-tier Fleetwood Town, and have a meeting with League One outfit Bradford City in December as their prize.

The key moments from the Etihad...

Image: Geronimo Rulli celebrates with Jeremy Doku after saving two penalties to beat Brighton

24: PENALTY CLAIM! Rico Lewis is upended by Yalcouye in the box but referee Andy Madley waves away any suggestion of a foul.

29: CLOSE! Pascal Gross fizzes a low shot just past the far post.

30: GOAL! Yalcouye's instinctive finish beats Rulli but the goal carries more than a suspicion of offside.

40: GOAL! A precision strike from Kovacic from the edge of the area brings City level.

47: GOAL! City are caught sleeping after the restart as Rutter sends Hadjam's lay-off soaring past Rulli.

73: GOAL! Cherki's free-kick takes a cruel deflection off the boot of Reis and gives Steele no chance of saving.

90: PENALTIES! Kovacic is the first to miss, before Ayari and Dunk are also denied and Rulli gets to finish the evening as his side's spot-kick hero.

Maresca happy with rotation of squad

Man City boss Enzo Maresca:

"Brighton are in a brilliant moment. They score many goals every game so we knew it was going to be tough. We could have done better defensively. But we only started three months ago with this project.

"We have many things we can do better. The game was chaotic but overall we controlled it quite good.

"Brighton always go front foot, man to man. It will be exactly the same on Saturday.

"This is a different competition, but the ambition has to be the same. We need to do our business, that is winning games. At the moment we're doing that."

On the rotation: "I was happy with the way we planned the game, the rotation. I was very happy with the ones that played."

Hurzeler: Man City were lucky

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler:

"We had enough chances to win this game. The goals we conceded are very unlucky, that's football, they had the luck on their side.

"We will analyse this game and we have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge - that's what we will try to do."

On staying in Manchester before facing City again: "We'll see if it's an advantage. We will try to make the best out of it, no excuses. We will come back full of energy and we go on Saturday."

Sports.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties yet again to secure Carabao Cup progress
Sports.content:
Chelsea must have been resigned to their fate as soon as the shootout arrived at Anfield. Four times they had faced Liverpool on penalties previously and four times they had lost. Number five was confirmed when Wesley Fofana’s wild effort sailed high into the Kop and sent Andoni Iraola’s side into a Carabao Cup quarter-final against his old club Bournemouth.

Fofana was not the only culprit as Chelsea’s catalogue of penalty misery against Liverpool gained a new chapter alongside the 2007 Champions League semi-final, the 2019 Uefa Super Cup final and the FA and League Cup finals of 2022.

Emmanuel Emegha had the chance to win it for Xabi Alonso’s side in sudden death but was denied superbly by Giorgi Mamardashvili. Liverpool fluffed their lines with victory in sight too, Kostas Tsimikas blazing over and ruining the chance to reprise his match-winning role at Wembley four years ago. Ryan Gravenberch and Valentin Barco also failed to convert.

It fell to Joe Gomez of all people to edge Liverpool ahead with the first shootout penalty of his Anfield career. The long-serving defender, who has never scored for Liverpool, found the top corner of Mike Penders’s goal in convincing style. Fofana could not repeat the trick and finally, after Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo had both scored penalties in normal time, the two adversaries were separated. It was another painful result for Alonso, fresh from the home defeat against Tottenham on Saturday, although the Chelsea display was an improvement.

The Chelsea manager said: “For sure it is not the outcome we wanted or expected but once you go to penalties there has to be a sad side. We played with courage, the game was close with not many chances for both sides. It is a small setback because it is probably the least important competition for us. As soon as we leave Anfield our focus will be on a very important game [against Manchester United] on Saturday.”

If, as Alonso claimed, the Carabao Cup is not a priority for Chelsea this season then his decision to again overlook the merits of Estêvão, who was left kicking his heels on the bench all evening, was mystifying. With João Pedro injured and Cole Palmer suspended Chelsea started with Danny Welbeck in attack and the former Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson operating in an advanced midfield role. Liverpool contained them relatively comfortably.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola embraces his goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili. Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty Images

The Premier League rivals served up a fast-paced, committed cup tie that was lacking goalmouth incident before they exchanged penalties in the space of four minutes. Chelsea were awarded the first when Moisés Caicedo was released inside the Liverpool area by a cleverly disguised pass from Malo Gusto and clipped from behind by Gravenberch. The boos for Henderson intensified as he carried the ball to the spot with a wry smile on his face and handed it to Rogers, who sent Mamardashvili the wrong way with an emphatic penalty kick.

Liverpool soon had a spot-kick of their own when Caicedo and Fofana challenged Virgil van Dijk at a Tsimikas corner and the ball struck the Chelsea defender’s raised hand. Gakpo converted confidently into the bottom corner. The referee, Darren England, called both penalties instantly and correctly, showing officials do not always have to rely on video assistance. The game benefited as a spectacle from the absence of a video assistant referee, although Iraola might well have disagreed had Rogers scored after appearing to control Pedro Neto’s chip with his arm. Mamardashvili’s save meant that controversy was avoided.

Penders, keen to atone for his costly error against Spurs, took centre stage for Chelsea when saving a flying header from Ronald Araújo at close range. The Liverpool defender had been supplied by a fine cross from Gomez and, with two defenders pushed forwards, Rogers almost punished them on the counterattack. Gomez, however, worked tirelessly to chase back and block the forward’s eventual shot. Penders also saved impressively from Bradley Barcola when the France international cut inside from the right and his low shot was deflected towards the bottom corner.

Rogers was involved in several promising openings for Chelsea as Alonso’s team – improved more than Liverpool by their substitutes – finished strongly. Marco Palestra had the best of them when released by the England forward’s perfectly weighted pass but Mamardashvili produced an excellent save low to his right. Wirtz also had a late chance to seal victory but his attempt from Gakpo’s knock-down struck Levi Colwill and was eventually cleared. And so to penalties, and a familiar feeling for the side from Stamford Bridge.

Iraola said: “I’m pleased for the players because they put in a big effort tonight. I can feel [togetherness within the squad] and I’m happy to feel it because it is very important. The players are feeling support from the crowd and now we have another big one on Sunday [against Arsenal] so let’s try to finish this four in a row in the best way.”

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Slegers hails ‘role model’ Russo after historic hat-trick sinks Benfica
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo wrote herself into the history books once more as she became the highest English goalscorer in the Women’s Champions League. Her hat-trick gave Arsenal a vital 3-0 win against Benfica to send the Gunners up to second in the league phase table.

“I’m so happy. I think we’ve found a nice dynamic as well with the last two games,” Russo’s manager, Renée Slegers, said. “She’s one of the leaders and she does it her way. She cares for everyone around her and connects well with her teammates. She leads the way as a role model, doing the right things consistently.”

It was a statement performance from the 27-year-old who has shaken off the early-season cobwebs. Her three goals at Meadow Park on Wednesday took her tally up to 10 in her past seven appearances for club and country, hitting a rich vein of form just when Arsenal have needed her most.

It is safe to say Arsenal’s season has yet to fully burst into life. Struggles in front of goal and unforced errors have defined the opening two months but the gritty north London derby win on Saturday did feel like it could be a springboard for momentum.

There was no less pressure coming into this Champions League match against Benfica, another must-win game with Arsenal’s European form mirroring their domestic struggles. A last-ditch win against HB Køge and a heartbreaking draw against Paris FC (in which they surrendered a two‑goal lead) left them fifth in the league phase table before kick-off, with Barcelona and OL Lyonnes looming.

Slegers made three changes to freshen things up. Ona Batlle returned to her more natural right‑back role while the summer signings Élisa De Almeida and Géraldine Reuteler made their full debuts.

Ivan Baptista’s Benfica arrived in confident form on the back of consecutive wins domestically. Slegers was keen to highlight their strong identity pre-match, having had first‑hand experience of their resilience in last year’s league phase. So it proved once more in a first half in which Arsenal dominated, but struggled to break through against a well-structured opposition.

View image in fullscreen The Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, has eased pressure on herself with back-to-back wins over Spurs and Benfica. Photograph: David Cliff/EPA

It was the visitors, in fact, who had the best opportunity of the first half hour. Frøya Dorsin was left beating the turf in frustration after spurning a glorious opportunity to catch out a stranded Misa Rodríguez with a lob. It was a moment that jolted Arsenal into life as they upped the tempo and began to rain pressure on Benfica’s goal. First Olivia Smith set up Russo for a low shot that went narrowly wide before Smith herself forced Lena Pauels into a fine save.

Arsenal found their breakthrough just before half-time when Russo produced a sublime finish after a well‑worked move down the left.

It was like a switch had flipped for Arsenal after the break as they exuded confidence, zipping the ball around the turf with increasing ease. Smith looked more and more comfortable in her central role while Caitlin Foord came alive down the left, the latter denied a clear shot by a superb last-ditch challenge.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The conductor behind them all was Russo as she pressed and stretched the play to her tune. The captain on the night was at the heart of things once more as the hosts doubled their lead, rising high to glance home a corner. She completed her hat-trick shortly afterwards, converting from the spot after Foord was brought down by Catarina Amado.

Quick Guide Roundup: Chelsea roll past Roma, Bayern and Real draw Show Chelsea maintained their strong start to this year’s Women’s Champions League campaign as second-half goals from Ellie Carpenter [pictured, centre] and Kadeisha Buchanan secured a 2-0 win over Roma at Plough Lane. After a goalless first half, substitute Carpenter combined with Wieke Kaptein to open the scoring in the 51st minute. The Australian made a powerful run, found Kaptein and then met her cross from the right with a low shot which took a deflection off Roma defender Winonah Heatley before going in. Central defender Buchanan wrapped up the win in the 89th minute, heading home to ensure a second win in three European matches for Sonia Bompastor’s unbeaten team. Roma were left to rue chances missed by Maya Doms and Alayah Pilgrim as they extended their scoreless Champions League start to three games. 'I’m pleased with the fact we scored really early in the second half. We could probably have killed the game a little bit earlier,' said the Chelsea head coach, Sonia Bompastor. 'It’s important for us in these games to be able to be clinical and ruthless as early as possible. But we find different ways to impose ourselves in the game and to score goals. So it’s good.' Bayern Munich fought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 against Real Madrid and preserve their unbeaten home record in the pre-knockout phase. Last season’s semi-finalists have now not lost any of their 17 home games in the group stage or league phase thanks to Momoko Tanikawa's second-half equaliser. Athenea del Castillo pounced from Linda Caicedo’s cross in the seventh minute, before Lineth Beerensteyn headed in from close range to double Madrid’s lead midway through the first half. Edna Imade nodded in to reduce the deficit on the half-hour and Tanikawa levelled soon after the restart, before Sophie Proost hit the post for Bayern in stoppage time. Eight-time champions Lyonnes cruised to an emphatic 6-0 home victory over Internazionale, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto scoring twice before Lily Yohannes made it three on the hour mark. Vicki Bècho came off the bench shortly after and hit a hat-trick as the French giants went top of the table on goal difference. Swiss side Servette claimed a historic maiden Champions League win at the ninth attempt as they brushed aside OH Leuven 5-1 in Geneva. Paola Hernández and Gloria Marinelli both struck twice to leave the Belgian champions winless so far in this season’s league phase. Press Association Photograph: Andrew Redington/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It was a finish that marked the 200th goal of Slegers’s tenure and one that further eases the pressure on the head coach. With every minute that passed the hosts looked increasingly like themselves and could have added more to their tally.

“It looks like there is something off our shoulders,” Slegers said. “We were playing like us tonight and I am so happy. The players enjoyed themselves – they connected, they expressed themselves and they played with intensity. We backed the last performance up. We need to do it again at the weekend.”

There will no doubt be sterner tests to come in Europe, more immediately away to Barcelona in a fortnight’s time, but this was a victory that signified something more important than just climbing up the Champions League table.

Sports.title: Rulli’s heroics earn Manchester City shootout success against Brighton
Sports.content:
After Jérémy Doku’s second-half substitute appearance transformed Manchester City into a high-octane proposition, the smart money was on the momentum continuing into a victorious penalty shootout.

So it proved as Enzo Maresca’s men triumphed 4-3, Gerónimo Rulli the hero: his save from Lewis Dunk’s fifth spot-kick was decisive, the Argentinean also having repelled Yasin Ayari’s fourth effort.

While Jason Steele kept out Mateo Kovacic’s attempt, City progressed after Brighton twice took the lead – via Malick Yalcouyé and Georginio Rutter – before being pegged back by Kovacic and Vitor Reis.

Maresca was left beaming: “Since I’m here we never practised penalties,” said the City manager. “It always happens that the one that scored in the 90 minutes [Kovacic] misses the penalty. I am very happy.”

Of Doku, he said: “He made an impact. This is the reason they are there. Jérémy and the rest – to try to do their best, if they start from the beginning or if they come in from the bench try to make an impact.”

The tie might have gone either way, so the lottery of penalties felt apt to decide who went through before Saturday’s rematch back here in the league. City will now play League One Bradford in the quarter-finals.

“I watched all [Brighton’s] Premier League games and since the first day they always go front foot, man to man, so they’re going to be exactly the same on Saturday,” Maresca said.

His opposite number spoke of vengeance. “We lost in a shootout. We had enough chances to win the game – they had the luck today. We have to reset. We have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge,” said Fabian Hürzeler.

Quick Guide Carabao Cup quarter-final draw Show Fleetwood v Everton or Newcastle Manchester City v Bradford City Crystal Palace v Sunderland Liverpool v Bournemouth Ties will take place during the week commencing 14 December Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Brighton will stay up in the area. “Not sleeping in your own bed is not an advantage,” said the manager. “But we’ll go there with full energy and ready to go on Saturday.”

When Yalcouyé opened the scoring there was the proverbial hint of offside about the forward as his shot pinged off Rulli and in.

With no video assistant referee in the Carabao Cup the goal stood, though it was soon cancelled out by Kovacic: Phil Foden fed him and, from the edge of the penalty area, he threaded the ball beyond Steele low into the left corner.

View image in fullscreen Georginio Rutter fires Brighton into a second-half lead. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

For the second half Maresca introduced Rayan Aït-Nouri and Ryan McAidoo for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Floyd Samba. Instantly, though, City conceded: Brighton slipped through the lines with ease, and Jaouen Hadjam’s cross was slid in by Rutter.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The forward’s grin went wide in celebration and the Seagulls were heading through, while City were going out. Aït-Nouri, skipping down the left, tried to do something about this, but his ball over was aimless.

At least there was pace in this foray, which those in blue sometimes lacked. But, also, Maresca’s team had become sloppy – a long-range Rayan Cherki pass that ended in Steele’s gloves was emblematic.

Olivier Boscagli’s corner that dipped viciously close to Rulli’s goalline was far more dangerous, so just after the hour Maresca introduced a first big gun – Doku, for Allan – this coming after Rutter ran in and went close to a second, underlining Brighton’s ascendancy.

When Doku played Aït-Nouri in through the left, it was a rare City attack and showed the value of having the Belgian now able to affect the game.

At this point, though, the decision to allow his star quintet the night off was backfiring for Maresca. City lacked control and were toothless. Doku, again, cut through Brighton but there were no runners to prosper from his delivery infield.

Hürzeler’s men tried to squeeze time and snaffle the ball whenever City attempted to move them about, but then came a first passage in which City camped in Brighton territory. Suddenly, those in green were having to answer questions. Foden’s burst that drew a free-kick from Rutter near the 18-yard line presaged one they could not answer. Cherki blasted at goal, Reis stuck out a boot, Steele was wrongfooted, and it was 2-2. Doku had lit up City, his presence terrorising Brighton’s defence and turning the tie.

“They are in a brilliant moment, scoring goals, many goals every game and winning, so we knew it was a tough game in terms of defending in the right way,” Maresca said. “We could have probably done something better defensively, but we started just three months ago [together]. The game was chaotic but we controlled it quite good.”

Sports.title: European football: Bayern ease to Cup victory after Kompany leaves hospital
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich sailed to a 6-1 win over second-tier Magdeburg in the DFB-Pokal after their head coach, Vincent Kompany, was discharged from hospital earlier on Wednesday.

Kompany’s assistant, Aaron Danks, was in the dugout for Bayern for the last-32 tie, while Harry Kane was rested. The Ballon d’Or winner received a guard of honour from his teammates before kick-off in front of 75,000 fans at the Allianz Arena.

Bayern had no difficulty without their star striker, with Michael Olise opening the scoring and adding a second-half penalty. Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies, Nathaniel Brown and teenager David Santos Daiber also got on the scoresheet, with Mateusz Zukowski striking for the visitors.

The German Cup holders received good news pre-match, with Kompany able to return home five days after collapsing at training on Friday. The Bayern Munich sporting director, Max Eberl, revealed that the Belgian had been suffering from meningeal irritation.

“We have identified the cause: it is a case of meningeal irritation, which is what triggered the incident last Friday,” Eberl said. “He has now been allowed to go home, where he can continue his rehabilitation … [which] means rest and medication. I am very, very confident that he will be back on the touchline at 100% very soon.”

Olise tapped in from an excellent Saibari assist after 10 minutes but the unfancied visitors levelled five minutes later through Zukowski. Olise then set up Saibari midway through the opening half and added a third from the spot early in the second half before smiling and pointing to Kane, Bayern’s regular penalty taker, on the bench.

View image in fullscreen Michael Olise scored from the penalty spot in Harry Kane’s absence. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

The teenage forward Lennart Karl set up goals for Davies and Brown, before Santos Daiber added more gloss to the victory with a stoppage-time goal. “We’re also winning for him of course,” Brown said of Kompany. “It’s really good that he’s back home now. He should get some rest, but hopefully we’ll see him again soon.”

“We’re very pleased that [Vincent] is getting better,” said Danks, who will continue to lead the team while Kompany recovers. “But he needs to rest, spend time with his family and continue to get better. He’s doing better and is on the road to recovery. We’ll simply try to do our best and prepare for the game on Saturday.”

Elsewhere, Bayer Leverkusen came from two goals down to win 5-2 against 2. Bundesliga promotion-chasers Nuremberg, with defender Edmond Tapsoba netting twice and Patrik Schick, Jonas Hofmann and Lucas Vázquez also on target.

Deniz Undav’s 90th-minute strike earned Stuttgart a 1-0 win over 10-man Paderborn, while Freiburg also won in stoppage time. The Japan forward Keisuke Goto scored twice in the final 15 minutes to turn a 2-1 deficit into a 3-2 victory over Wolfsburg.

Second-tier Dynamo Dresden upset Schalke 2-0, and Holstein Kiel eliminated Hoffenheim 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw to reach the last 16.

There was a huge upset across the border in Poland, as defending league champions Lech Poznan were beaten 1-0 by fourth-tier Siarka Tarnobrzeg in a Cup tie that kicked off at 12.30pm on Wednesday.

Lech held Sunderland to a 1-1 draw in the Europa League last week and beat Legia Warsaw on Sunday to go top of the Polish top-flight – but they were brought down to earth by Arkadiusz Kasia’s second-half header.

Inter sink Venezia, Milan beaten by Bologna

Internazionale returned to the Serie A summit with a nervy 2-0 win at bottom side Venezia, while Bologna won 4-2 at San Siro to inflict a first league defeat of the season on Milan.

Champions Inter drew level with Lazio on 25 points at the top before a hotly anticipated Milan derby on Saturday. Ruben Amorim’s side lost their unbeaten streak after Alphadjo Cisse’s double was not enough to avoid defeat, as Samuel Mbangula’s hat-trick sealed a 4-2 win for the visitors.

Venezia have picked up just three points all season, but earned them with a shock win over Napoli on new coach Davide Nicola’s debut. Another shock result looked possible on Wednesday until they were undone by two late own goals, with Matías Moreno and Redouane Halhal diverting crosses into their own net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

At San Siro, a lengthy injury list restricted Amorim’s options, and the Milan coach also left Christian Pulisic and Luka Modric on the bench. Mbangula, making his full debut for Bologna, swept home the opener inside eight minutes, but the visitors were soon pegged back when an Arthur Theate error gifted Cissé a simple finish.

View image in fullscreen Bologna’s Samuel Mbangula is surrounded by teammates and coaches after scoring his third goal against Milan. Photograph: Spada/LaPresse/Shutterstock

The teenager struck again in the 27th minute, volleying home a Fikayo Tomori cross, but the game was turned on its head once again in the space of two second-half minutes. Davide Bartesaghi turned a free-kick into his own net before Mbangula struck again just after the hour mark. The 22-year-old sealed victory four minutes from time, beating Mike Maignan after a breakaway.

Juventus’s shaky start continued with a 2-0 defeat away to Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck early before Tommaso Baldanzi doubled Genoa’s lead in the 28th minute. Luciano Spalletti’s inconsistent side have not won back-to-back league games since the opening two weeks of the season, and face Napoli next.

With head coach Massimiliano Allegri suspended after being sent off during the 3-3 draw with Roma, Napoli enjoyed their biggest win of the season, winning 4-1 at Monza to go sixth in the table, above Juve on goal difference.

Rasmus Højlund’s early opener was cancelled out by Gustavo Varela’s header just before the break, but Napoli pulled away in the second half as Matteo Politano, Rafa Marín and substitute Kevin De Bruyne all scored. Elsewhere, Adrián Bernabé saw his penalty saved as struggling Parma and Udinese played out a 0-0 draw.

Copa del Rey games postponed after rail crash

All 24 Copa del Rey matches scheduled for Wednesday evening have been postponed as a mark of respect following the devastating rail incident in Spain.

A high-speed train crashed into the rear of another train on Wednesday morning and derailed two cars in the province of Toledo, with at least 68 people killed.

La Liga clubs Alavés, Celta Vigo, Levante, Real Betis and Valencia were due to get their domestic cup campaigns under way, but all of Wednesday’s fixtures will now be played at later dates.

Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atlético Madrid are not due to enter until the last 32 in December, but all three issued statements expressing sadness and deepest condolences.

Sports.title: Nketiah takes Crystal Palace past Fulham and earns Sage breathing space
Sports.content:
“Can we play you every week?” chanted the Crystal Palace fans as they celebrated a fifth victory over Fulham on their own patch in the space of 18 months. Eddie Nketiah’s first-half goal against the run of play eased some of the growing pressure on Pierre Sage as Palace booked a third consecutive appearance in the quarter-finals of this competition.

The good news for Sage is that Arsenal – who beat them on both of those occasions – have already been eliminated. However, he knows that Saturday’s game at Tottenham will have much more bearing on whether he is still around by the time Palace’s Carabao Cup campaign resumes against Sunderland in mid-December.

For Álvaro Arbeloa, this was a disappointing setback after a couple of weeks of progress. Fulham have not beaten Palace at Craven Cottage since January 2005 – a run of 10 matches – and will not get a better chance after Sage made 10 changes, including the inspired return of their captain, Dean Henderson, in goal. His save in stoppage time from Gonzalo García proved crucial and there were boos for Fulham at the final whistle. Arbeloa will be relieved that at least he does not have to face Palace again this season.

Sage left the pitch blowing kisses in the direction of his wife in the stands, but praised the travelling supporters for helping his team get over the line. “I like the fans, but I love my wife,” he said. “All the fans are really behind us – they are happy when the team is like this. The connection is better when we fight on the pitch.”

Fortunes have contrasted significantly for these two sides since Palace’s 3-2 win here at the start of September. Successive 1-0 victories against Hull and Coventry in the Premier League took some of the heat off Arbeloa but he was disappointed that a rotated side, which still contained several key players, could not take their chances – an issue becoming a recurring theme under the Spaniard. “It’s the same story – we need to learn to be more clinical,” said Arbeloa. “It’s a really frustrating night for everyone.”

Quick Guide Carabao Cup quarter-final draw Show Fleetwood v Everton or Newcastle Manchester City v Bradford City Crystal Palace v Sunderland Liverpool v Bournemouth Ties will take place during the week commencing 14 December Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Sage had no choice but to rotate his side heavily after their exertions last week, which included travelling to Istanbul for a draw with Beskitas in the Europa League before losing to Newcastle at home three days later. No doubt with an eye on Saturday’s trip to north London that could define the Frenchman’s future, Chris Richards was the only player to retain his place. There has been talk of a protest before Palace’s next home game against Liverpool over rising ticket prices and what some supporters have described as the club’s strategy “which prioritises tourists instead of regular match-going fans” by playing loud music before kick-off and half-time. The fans who packed the away section were in full voice throughout, even as their second-string struggled against opponents who were clearly brimming with confidence.

View image in fullscreen Pierre Sage, who has been under scrutiny following some poor results, applauds the Crystal Palace fans after the match. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Fulham went close twice in the space of 60 seconds when Kenny Tete headed wide from a corner before Henderson – after month on the sidelines – saved well with his feet from Antonee Robinson at the far post. Joachim Andersen should have done better with the next chance from another corner soon after, but the Denmark defender could not hit the target against his former club.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With Cheick Doucouré making his first senior appearance in midfield since January 2025 after a litany of injury problems, Palace looked rusty all over the pitch and did not manage a single touch in Fulham’s box during the first half-hour, amassing just 22% of possession. But they still managed to take the lead when Óscar Mingueza found space down the right flank and delivered an inch-perfect cross for Nketiah to volley in expertly. After all their dominance, Fulham’s supporters could hardly believe their eyes.

Palace should have been punished when Honest Ahanor gave the ball away on the edge of his area but Rodrigo Muniz’s shot was weak. Arbeloa turned to his bench and there were huge cheers for Josh King’s arrival. But Jefferson Lerma and Henderson somehow managed to clear Iwobi’s header off the line as Fulham finally created a chance their pressure merited.

The Palace substitutes Daichi Kamada and Dwight McNeil could have sealed the victory with late chances as Fulham pushed forward in desperation for an equaliser. Their supporters could not hide their frustration at full-time as Palace’s sang about another possible trip to Wembley. What a difference a few days make.

Sports.title: Howe, Nagelsmann, Pochettino: can anyone end Manchester United’s doom loop?
Sports.content:
In January 2014 the 13th series of Celebrity Big Brother aired in the UK, the show so popular that its run time was extended by five days before a public vote anointed Jim Davidson the winner. Then, two years later when Brexit happened, people wondered where their tolerant country had gone, lamenting the ephemeral spirit of London 2012 as though the 2011 riots were some kind of fever dream, not a desperate response to decades of structural and institutional racism exacerbated by the cruelty of unnecessary austerity.

The truth is that if security is quickly upended, it was built on quicksand to begin with. Which brings us to Manchester United, easing effortlessly from an uplifting third-place finish to some of the worst football in their history.

It is entirely possible that Alex Ferguson made a deal with the devil to the effect that United would be great until he retired and hilariously dreadful thereafter. But assuming not, his l’état, c’est moi mentality was busy setting up the post-him fall even at the height of the success – itself a consequence of what had gone before.

A day after the Munich air disaster, Louis Edwards – later a seller of condemned meat to schools – joined the board, eventually assuming control thanks to a dodgy rights issue. He bequeathed the club to Martin – his substellar son – who floated it for personal gain, turning an institution that sought to win, entertain and unify into a business legally compelled to return value to shareholders.

This left United vulnerable to acquisition by anyone and, when Ferguson fell out with two directors – a horse, a horse, his kingdom for a horse’s ejaculate – they sold to the Glazers, who loaded the purchase price and accordant interest obligation on to the club, with government and football authorities waving through a move since outlawed. Ferguson, meanwhile, must have feared exactly what the takeover would entail and known that without his support the banks might not have lent the money, while the chief executive David Gill admitted opposition to it but stayed in his role anyway, and so the pillaging began.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United fans let their feelings know about Malcolm Glazer’s proposed takeover of the club in May 2005. Photograph: John Peters/Manchester United/Getty Images

The English game then exploded, with investment in United left available only to those of wealth so extreme it necessarily casts aspersions over their character – such as arch polluter and anti‑immigration zealot, Jim Ratcliffe. Proclaiming inaccurate and divisive rhetoric contrary to the inclusive, cosmopolitan spirit of Manchester and United, jobs were culled and fights picked with fans, Old Trafford’s most desirable seats socially cleansed so the club could sell them to day-trippers for astronomical prices, with longstanding supporters banned after trumped-up charges of touting – a deeply principled stance the club fails to apply to itself.

Not untypically for a billionaire, Ratcliffe seemingly believes that correct opinions reflect exchequer not expertise, giving himself final say on footballing decisions. And rather than the “best in class” executives he promised, his United operate according to what political analysts call the “Boris principle”, no‑marks in thrall to their own self‑image given jobs for which they lack the ability and character, the consequent chaos being effective sabotage.

So the patterns continue: Champions League qualification is missed, insufficient funds are released; a new unsuitable manager spends heavily on players below requisite standard; Champions League qualification is achieved via unsustainably reactive style; the manager is denied necessary funds amounting to less than the bounty of Champions League qualification; the manager imposes a proactive style without the necessary materials; the manager is belatedly fired for a fee far exceeding that saved by cutting jobs; a new unsuitable manager, with entirely different requirements to his predecessor, is appointed; executive accountability is absent.

View image in fullscreen Eddie Howe is the preferred choice of director of football Jason Wilcox if there is a change of manager at Old Trafford. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

It is thus no surprise that Michael Carrick remains unfired, despite exuding the vibe of a man who’s mentally fired himself. Perhaps it’s a stay of execution, but more likely there’s bizarre hope of a turnaround, partly to save paying him off, partly because the relevant executives can’t achieve consensus on a replacement, and partly because surely even Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox accept that, following another catastrophe, after dismissing Carrick they are honour-bound to dismiss themselves.

Except they and United don’t work like that.

So, just as they failed Carrick by not recruiting properly; failing to add experience to his coaching team; failing to replace outgoing fitness and set-piece coaches and failing to interrogate details of his new game-model, they are now failing him by having him continue in a job that is too much for him, destroying a season that remains salvageable. Meantime, the Glazers’ dividends continue unabated.

As such, the question isn’t so much who should be United’s next manager as can anyone manage United? Increasingly, it looks like the answer is – to quote Don Logan in Sexy Beast – “No”.

There are immediate on‑pitch issues: the team are unfit and their collective mentality weak; after years being lied to, the captain has finally broken; and the players hate the suits, the package toxic. Those are the minor problems.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Roughly, football management comprises five aspects: coaching, tactics, talent ID, pastoral care and presence. And, though no manager excels in every department, at this version of United surely they must. Moreover, given this is no job for a novice, track record is also important – and it might be here that Unai Emery’s candidature falls down, his brilliance in transforming mid‑ranking clubs undermined by failures at two high-profile basket cases.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino has recently signed a contract extension which puts him in charge of the USA men’s team until 2030. Photograph: Kirby Lee/Imagn Images/Reuters

Which brings us to pastoral care and presence. In the postwar era, only Erik ten Hag has won a trophy at United without tangible charisma, the size of the club now demanding it more than ever. This is not a quality associated with Eddie Howe, while Antonio Conte does not scream pastoral care and, brilliant though his career has been, he failed miserably at Spurs, the only environment he has inhabited that is remotely similar to United.

Should United miss Champions League qualification, financial strictures will make an elite coach and tactician essential. But in any event, football has changed such that the alchemic art of combining players and personalities no longer guarantees success.

Which leaves us with talent ID, player quality and intelligence being the best coaching and tactics there are. Of the 78 players purchased post-Ferguson, only Bruno Fernandes and perhaps Zlatan Ibrahimovic could be classed as cast-iron successes, so the next man – assuming United don’t target Emma Hayes, who embodies more of the right stuff than almost anyone else – must have a keen nose. Even Jürgen Klopp, the other manager who fulfils these criteria – and of all the damage Ed Woodward wreaked on United, turning him off was most costly – benefited from a department which delivered the greatest run of transfers ever.

View image in fullscreen Germany’s coach at the 2026 World Cup, Julian Nagelsmann, speaks to his squad. He is believed to be admired by Manchester United’s executives. Photograph: Pilar Olivares/Reuters

Which leaves Mauricio Pochettino, who built something at Tottenham despite the environment, and Julian Nagelsmann. But had Pochettino not signed a new contract with the USA men’s team, the sense is that, as when Mourinho arrived at Old Trafford after years of speculation, he’s past his magical best, while Nagelsmann may be the free-thinking genius of his own imagination, just as he may be an emperor’s new clothes bluffer.

All of which is to say that failure has many fathers and, once ingrained, is not easily eradicated. Yet just as society has too much going for it to ever move quite beyond the pale, so too does Manchester United. Even the longest journey starts with one step; but does anyone have the nous to ensure it’s taken in the correct direction?

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: McInnes booed in Rangers draw at Hearts, Celtic held at home
Sports.content:
Olwethu Makhanya scored a late equaliser as Rangers earned a 2-2 draw with Hearts on the much-hyped Tynecastle return for Derek McInnes.

The Rangers manager was booed loudly by the home support as he emerged from the tunnel for his first match back since leaving for Ibrox in June, just weeks after the Edinburgh side were pipped to the Scottish Premiership title.

However, his team silenced a pumped-up home crowd when Kevin Kelsy scored a 16th-minute opener after a lapse from Laurent Mendy.

Hearts turned the game round with goals from Cláudio Braga and Calvin Miller early in the second half. But Makhanya’s 89th-minute header ensured the match ended all square, keeping second-placed Rangers four points behind Celtic and four above Hearts.

Celtic showed their mettle as they fought back to grab a 2-2 draw with Dundee United at Parkhead.

The Colombian striker Camilo Durán put Martin O’Neill’s team ahead in the 18th minute with his 11th goal of the season. But the Australian forward Zac Sapsford levelled in the 28th minute with a header before the defender Neil Farrugia put the visitors in front three minutes later with his first goal for the club.

Celtic piled forward in the second half and the defender Liam Scales equalised with a 64th-minute header. O’Neill said: “We cannot control anything that’s happening elsewhere. The disappointment and the frustration comes from not winning a home game.

“That’s really it. But considering the trials and tribulations over the last number of weeks, yeah, I’m not totally dissatisfied. We conceded some poor goals, but we fought back and I just thought we were going to win it. But in the end we could have lost it too, on the break. I thought Dundee United were very dangerous and they played very well in the game.”

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Liam Scales rises highest to make it 2-2 against Dundee United. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

Stephen Robinson, the Aberdeen manager, admitted his side were not good enough in the 1-0 defeat by Falkirk, but refused to shout and scream at his players in the aftermath.

Ben Brauhaus, on as a substitute, scored the only goal of the game, side-footing into the bottom-left corner from the centre of the box after 73 minutes.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Robinson, though, felt his side should have scored from at least one of their chances before then, saying: “Not good enough. We got what we deserved. We had four chances we should score. We had four great chances from inside the penalty spot, and we should score.

“All four are very, very easy chances. We don’t do that, they take their one chance, and that’s why you don’t win football matches.”

Ash Hay piled more pressure on the Kilmarnock manager, Neil McCann, after scoring a late double to earn Dundee a 3-1 win at Dens Park. His strikes, in the 83rd minute and the fifth minute of added time, gave his side the win after Joe Hugill’s 75th-minute penalty.

Hibernian moved off the bottom of the table as they drew 1-1 at St Mirren to secure Marink Reedijk’s first point as manager. Marko Ivezic put Hibs ahead but Jason Kerr’s own goal denied them a third league win this season.

Motherwell ended a six-match losing run but they were denied a victory as Josh Campbell’s 93rd-minute equaliser for St Johnstone earned them a 2-2 draw. Taylor Steven had given the home side the lead before Ibrahim Said and Tawanda Maswanhise turned the scoreline around. However, Campbell’s late header sealed a point.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup roundup: Bournemouth thrash Villa, Sunderland salvo stings Bees
Sports.content:
Bournemouth continued their impressive run of results by thumping Aston Villa 3-0 to reach the Carabao Cup quarter-finals for the first time in eight seasons, while Sunderland scored three times in 10 minutes at the Stadium of Light to leave Brentford too much to do as the home side won 3-2.

The winger Amine Adli fired home in the seventh minute at the Vitality Stadium to set Marco Rose’s in-form side on course for a fifth consecutive win in all competitions. Lewis Cook, the Cherries captain, added a fortuitous second early in the second period before the striker Álvaro Rodríguez sealed another 3-0 success after similar wins against Milan and Manchester United.

Villa – five-time League Cup winners – were second best for most of a fruitless trip to the south coast as they endured a first defeat in eight games. Taylor Harwood-Bellis and the substitutes Alejandro Garnacho and Alysson had the visitors’ best chances in Dorset but Bournemouth registered a fifth clean sheet in a row to ease into the last eight.

Both sides made wholesale changes for the fourth-round tie. Adli – one of eight players brought in by Rose, the Bournemouth head coach, finished a fine team move to open the scoring.

After James Tavernier unlocked the visitors’ defence with a delightful ball over the top, the full-back Julio Soler delivered a lofted cross from the left, allowing the Morocco international Adli to fire into the top-right corner from six yards out.

Villa’s unfamiliar lineup struggled to create in the opening stages and only a smart stop from the goalkeeper Marco Bizot prevented Ben Gannon-Doak extending Bournemouth’s lead.

George Hemmings flashed wide as Unai Emery’s team eventually threatened before the 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo was denied by a smothering save from the home goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio.

Bournemouth doubled their lead six minutes into the second half. Villa initially survived when Bizot superbly tipped on to the crossbar and behind to thwart the Cherries right-back Juanlu at the end of a marauding run.

However, Cook took the resulting left-wing corner short and, after receiving the ball back from Gannon-Doak, caught out Bizet with a low in-swinging cross which crept in at the near post.

Quick Guide Carabao Cup quarter-final draw Show Fleetwood v Everton or Newcastle Manchester City v Bradford City Crystal Palace v Sunderland Liverpool v Bournemouth Ties will take place during the week commencing 14 December Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The Villa midfielder João Gomes saw an opportunity to halve the deficit saved by Di Gregorio, while the defender Harwood-Bellis went close with a header.

Hopes of a comeback ended in the 69th minute when Rodríguez burst into the penalty box and lashed his second goal of the season into the bottom-right corner after Tyler Adams intercepted a loose pass.

Garnacho was denied a consolation by Di Gregorio after racing clear before his fellow replacement Alysson headed a golden chance wide as Bournemouth’s defence held out to make it a hat-trick of 3-0 wins. They now travel to Liverpool in the quarter-finals.

Sunderland held on to beat Brentford 3-2, with Chemsdine Talbi, Timur Tutierov and Malick Fofana on target – and the winger Jocelin Ta Bi had a hand in all three goals for Régis Le Bris’s much-changed team.

Callum Wilson pulled one back within three minutes, tapping in off the bar from four yards out, after Vitaly Janelt’s scuffed shot had fallen to him.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Igor Thiago set up a thrilling finish when the goalkeeper Melker Ellborg failed to deal with his header in the fourth minute of five added on at the end of the contest. However, the Black Cats held on to book a place in the last eight of the competition for the first time in five years – when they were a League One team.

View image in fullscreen Malick Fofana of Sunderland (right) celebrates with Dayann Methalie after scoring his team’s third goal. Photograph: Ian Horrocks/Sunderland AFC/Getty Images

Brentford started strongly and after the visiting captain, Nathan Collins, directed a free header into the arms of Ellborg, Malick Diouf’s cross was turned into the side-netting by Thiago. Jannik Schuster’s header shortly after crashed against the bar before the rebound saw Michael Kayode direct an effort against the foot of the post.

Ellborg also made a stunning flying save to turn Mamadou Sangaré’s volley over the bar, before Sunderland made them pay for those wasted chances.

Although Thiago went close to levelling, Ta Bi brilliantly created the second at the other end by beating his man and putting a chance on a plate for Tutierov to convert.

With six minutes remaining of the first half, the excellent Ta Bi crossed to the back post for Fofana to head into the roof of the net and make it 3-0.

Brentford responded quickly. Three minutes before the break Wilson pulled a goal back and the striker went close to adding a second before the half-time whistle. After the restart, Janelt’s long-range effort brushed the side-netting and Dango Ouattara headed wide at the far post as Brentford looked to close the gap further.

Although Thiago’s header from Mathias Jensen’s delivery eventually squirmed under Ellborg to give Sunderland a late scare, there was to be no equaliser, and the hosts next travel to Crystal Palace.

Sports.title: Jordan Henderson smirks as he trolls Anfield boo-boys on return with Chelsea - and argues with ex-Liverpool team-mate Virgil van Dijk
Sports.content:
Jordan Henderson laughed off his haters on his return to Anfield on Wednesday night. Liverpool legend Henderson, 36, played the full 90 minutes of the Carabao Cup last-16 tie as Chelsea lost 6-5 on penalties, although the veteran did score his spot kick. It capped what must have been a strange night for the midfielder as he went back to the club where he made 492 appearances and won eight trophies over a 12-year period. Henderson left to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq in the summer of 2023. Despite his long service, Henderson received a vociferous reception as a Chelsea player, with the home faithful booing him every time he touched the ball. And, after the Blues were awarded a penalty in the first half when Ryan Gravenberch fouled Moises Caicedo, that atmosphere escalated further. Henderson picked up the ball and walked towards the penalty spot as if he was going to take the spot kick. Hendo smirking at Liverpool fans in a Chelsea shirt. Never thought we'd see the daypic.twitter.com/Fac2gSbe5x — Dom✨ (@footy_road) October 28, 2026 Jordan Henderson was seen smirking after receiving a hostile reception from Liverpool fans The former Liverpool captain also argued with his former team-mate Virgil van Dijk at one point As he did so, Henderson was loudly jeered and he allowed himself a wry smile and laugh as he looked back towards the crowd. Henderson ultimately handed the ball over to Morgan Rogers, who made no mistake from the spot. The hostile reception may have been in part motivated by the midfielder's desire to contest several decisions with Liverpool's players and referee Darren England, along with the fact he is now representing Chelsea. At one point early in the first half, both Henderson and his former team-mate Virgil van Dijk fought their case in one discussion with England. As they walked away, the pair shouted at each other from afar in what must have been a strange sight for Liverpool supporters to witness. Henderson did later appear to applaud the crowd after the game when he was also seen laughing and joking with van Dijk. Meanwhile, at the end of last season, Henderson, who has similarly played for Ajax and Brentford in recent years, returned to Anfield for the first time with the Bees. On that occasion, he received a warm reception and then a standing ovation when he was substituted in the second half. Speaking after that game, he wrote on social media: 'I'd like to thank the Liverpool fans for the reception they gave me yesterday. 'It meant a lot to me going back to Anfield and being able to say thank you for everything you gave me in my 12 years at the club. It's a feeling that I'll never forget. 'To be able to be there to see my two brothers, Mo [Salah] and Robbo [Andy Robertson], say goodbye and get the send-off they deserve was also special. 'We spent some amazing times together that I will cherish forever. I wish you both all the very best in your next chapters.'
