Mauldin added that reliable electricity and secure communities were necessary for businesses to establish factories, deploy fibre-optic networks and operate efficient supply chains.

The summit brought together government officials, business leaders, policymakers and development partners to examine investment opportunities, infrastructure development and strategies for accelerating Nigeria’s economic growth.

World.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea in League Cup shoot-out, Man City survive scare
World.content:
Chelsea’s French defender #03 Wesley Fofana fails to score from the penalty spot during the English League Cup fourth round football match between Liverpool and Chelsea at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Liverpool beat Chelsea in a dramatic penalty shoot-out to reach the League Cup quarter-finals, while holders Manchester City survived a scare against Brighton on Wednesday.

In a clash between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso, it was the Liverpool manager who took the bragging rights in the last-16 tie at Anfield.

A 1-1 draw in normal time set the stage for the shoot-out as Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers netted from the spot, only for Cody Gakpo to equalise with a penalty of his own just before half-time.

Chelsea’s Valentin Barco hit the post in the shoot-out before Liverpool’s Kostas Tsimikas wasted a chance to win it when he blazed over.

Ryan Gravenberch was denied by Chelsea keeper Mike Penders, but Giorgi Mamardashvili saved Emmanuel Emegha’s kick to keep Liverpool alive.

After Joe Gomez scored for Liverpool, Blues defender Wesley Fofana miscued into the Kop as the hosts advanced.

It was former Liverpool midfielder Alonso’s third defeat in his three visits to Anfield as a manager following losses with Bayer Leverkusen in 2024 and Real Madrid in 2025.

In their debut campaigns at Liverpool, Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot both reached the League Cup final and Iraola is on course to follow in their footsteps with the 10-time winners of the competition.

Alonso made just four changes to the Chelsea side that lost 2-0 at home to Tottenham on Saturday, while Iraola made seven changes from Liverpool’s 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday.

Rogers put Chelsea in front with a 40th-minute penalty after Gravenberch clattered into Moises Caicedo.

But Liverpool were level three minutes later with a penalty of their own as Gakpo converted from the spot following Fofana’s handball.

At the Etihad Stadium, City were pushed to the brink by Brighton in a 2-2 draw before winning on penalties.

City boss Enzo Maresca made nine changes after Saturday’s loss at Aston Villa — which ended the leaders’ 100 percent start to the Premier League campaign.

– Rulli stars for City –

Erling Haaland, Ruben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Gianluigi Donnarumma were among the City stars rested.

Brighton went in front after 30 minutes when Malick Yalcouye steered Georginio Rutter’s shot past Geronimo Rulli from five yards.

Mateo Kovacic hauled City level 20 minutes later with a fine finish that curled into the far corner from 25 yards.

Rutter restored Brighton’s lead two minutes after half-time, slotting home from Jaouen Hadjam’s cut-back.

Vitor Reis deflected in Rayan Cherki’s 72nd-minute free-kick to equalise for City.

Kovacic’s penalty was saved by Jason Steele in the shoot-out, but Rulli denied Brighton’s Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight.

The sides meet again in the Premier League at the Etihad on Saturday.

Bournemouth extended their blistering run with a 3-0 win against Aston Villa at the Vitality Stadium.

The Cherries beat AC Milan 3-0 in the Europa League last week and followed that up with a 3-0 win at Manchester United in the Premier League on Sunday.

Marco Rose’s men dispatched Villa in equally emphatic fashion as goals from Amine Adli, Lewis Cook and Alvaro Rodriguez made it five successive wins in all competitions.

Crystal Palace eased the pressure on under-fire boss Pierre Sage with a 1-0 win at Fulham.

Eddie Nketiah struck in the 37th minute to give struggling Palace their first win in five games in all competitions.

Sunderland enjoyed a welcome respite from their Premier League struggles with a 3-2 victory against Brentford at the Stadium of Light.

Sitting bottom of the Premier League, Sunderland swatted aside the Bees with goals from Chemsdine Talbi, Tymur Tutierov and Malick Fofana.

Callum Wilson and Igor Thiago netted too late to save Brentford.

Fourth-tier Fleetwood reached the quarter-finals with a stunning penalty shoot-out victory over Premier League champions Arsenal on Tuesday.

Everton host Newcastle in the last game of the fourth round on Thursday.

AFP

World.title: Ballon d’Or winner Kane watches as Bayern cruise into German Cup last 16
World.content:
Bayern Munich’s English forward #09 Harry Kane (L) and Bayern Munich’s French defender #23 Sacha Boey warm up during the German Cup (DFB-Pokal) football match between FC Bayern Munich and 1. FC Magdeburg in Munich, southern Germany on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP) / DFB REGULATIONS PROHIBIT ANY USE OF PHOTOGRAPHS AS IMAGE SEQUENCES AND QUASI-VIDEO.

Newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was left on the bench as Bayern Munich sailed to a 6-1 win over second-tier Magdeburg in the German Cup last 32 on Wednesday.

Bayern had no difficulty without their star striker, with Michael Olise grabbing a double and Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies, Nathaniel Brown and teenager David Santos Daiber also getting on the scoresheet.

Kane received a guard of honour from his Bayern teammates before kick-off as the 75,000 fans at the Allianz Arena saluted the Ballon d’Or winner, two days after his triumph in London.

Bayern got some more good news pre-match, with coach Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital, five days after collapsing at training on Friday.

“We’re also winning for him of course,” Brown said of Kompany. “It’s really good that he’s back home now. He should get some rest, but hopefully we’ll see him again soon.”

Olise tapped in an excellent Saibari assist from close range after 10 minutes but the unfancied visitors levelled five minutes later through Mateusz Zukowski.

Olise returned the favour by setting up Saibari midway through the opening half and added a third from the spot early in the second half before smiling and pointing to Kane, Bayern’s regular penalty taker, on the bench.

Teenage forward Lennart Karl set up goals for Davies and Brown before Santos Daiber added more gloss to the victory with a stoppage-time goal.

Kane remained on the bench for the entire match, with Saturday’s home Bundesliga clash with Borussia Dortmund in mind.

Bayer Leverkusen came from two goals down to win 5-2 against Nuremberg, with defender Edmond Tapsoba netting twice and Patrik Schick, Jonas Hofmann and Lucas Vazquez scoring goals.

Earlier on Wednesday, Germany forward Deniz Undav’s 90th-minute strike took Stuttgart to a 1-0 win at 10-man Paderborn.

Stuttgart, finalists in 2025, had a one-man advantage after Laurin Curda’s 37th-minute red card but could not break down a stubborn Paderborn.

After striker Ermedin Demirovic had two efforts saved, Undav took matters into his own hands and turned in a Chris Fuehrich cross with extra time looming.

“The win is what matters most,” Undav said. “I honestly don’t care whether I’m the one who scores, and that’s the truth. We won, we’re through to the next round — on we go.”

Japan forward Keisuke Goto scored twice in the final 15 minutes to overturn a 2-1 deficit as Freiburg won 3-2 at home against Wolfsburg.

Goto’s Japan teammate Kento Shiogai also bagged a brace, while Freiburg’s Igor Matanovic opened the scoring.

Elsewhere, second-division sides Dynamo Dresden and Hertha Berlin both won 2-0 against Schalke and Jeddeloh respectively, while Kaiserslautern eliminated Hannover.

AFP

World.title: Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to US
World.content:
Flavio Bolsonaro steps off a plane after arriving at Opa Locka Executive Airport in Miami, Florida on October 28, 2026. Brazil’s defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro stepped out of a private plane in Florida today, AFP witnessed, despite a court order banning him from leaving his country. His plane touched down at Opa-Locka Executive Airport outside Miami after flying from Argentina with a stopover in Ecuador, as speculation had swirled for days over his whereabouts. (Photo by Ricardo Arduengo / AFP)

Brazil’s defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country’s rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile.

Bolsonaro’s defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday.

“I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Bolsonaro said in the statement published on his X account, slamming “electoral fraud.”

“I will lead the opposition from here,” he said. In a subsequent statement, he revised his claim, saying he is the “leader,” rather than “president.”

Bolsonaro, 45, touched down earlier Wednesday in a private jet at Opa-Locka Executive Airport near Miami.

President Donald Trump’s hard-right administration has strong links to Bolsonaro and his father Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brazil after attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.

Trump reiterated his stand that Brazil’s election was “very strange” but told reporters he “won’t get involved” in Flavio Bolsonaro’s claim to the presidency.

Details of how Bolsonaro, accompanied by his wife and daughters, made it to US soil are still emerging.

He is under investigation in his home country over alleged corruption and money laundering. With his current parliamentary immunity about to expire, he was ordered to surrender his passports but left anyway, reaching the United States via Argentina and Ecuador.

A police source told AFP that Bolsonaro’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, but the senator has also held Italian nationality since 2023, according to Italian documents seen by AFP.

The US Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that the Bolsonaro family members were inspected and cleared “with applicable immigration laws and procedures.”

The travel ban was issued by powerful Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who led the case against Flavio Bolsonaro’s father and is a controversial figure hated by the Brazilian right.

Flavio Bolsonaro had vowed to seek the justice’s impeachment if he were elected — which up until Lula’s comeback in the runoff had looked increasingly likely.

– ‘Shameful’ act –

Lula, who won the election with 51.8 percent of Sunday’s vote, called Flavio Bolsonaro’s departure a “shameful” act.

“A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide,” he said in Brasilia during his 81st birthday celebration on Tuesday.

But Brazil police issued a statement Wednesday saying that he was not considered a fugitive.

There was controversy in neighboring Argentina, where opposition lawmakers demanded to know how Bolsonaro had managed to transit through the country.

While Argentinian authorities said he was carrying valid travel documents, officials have requested chief of cabinet Diego Santilli to provide details to parliament, according to opposition lawmaker Agustin Rossi.

– Fraud cases –

The most high-profile fraud case against Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil centers on the unreleased biopic “Dark Horse” starring US actor Jim Caviezel as Flavio’s father Jair.

In May, the outlet Intercept Brasil revealed audio recordings in which Flavio Bolsonaro negotiated approximately $24 million to finance the film with banker Daniel Vorcaro, who is jailed over one of Brazil’s biggest-ever fraud cases.

Before the leak, Flavio Bolsonaro had denied knowing Vorcaro, or that he had financed the movie.

In July, the Supreme Court ordered a probe into the financing of the film, and whether it involved corruption, money laundering or the illegal movement of currency.

Flavio Bolsonaro acknowledged Vorcaro had funded the film, but insisted it was a private business deal that was “completely legal.”

In another probe, police are investigating whether Flavio Bolsonaro laundered money and moved funds out of the country in collaboration with his close friend, the lawyer Willer Tomaz.

Flavio’s father Jair Bolsonaro also never conceded defeat after losing to Lula and left the country on the eve of his rival’s inauguration, before returning to Brazil three months later.

AFP

World.title: No ministers paid billions for appointments, APC insists
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

The All Progressives Congress, APC, Wednesday, denied claims that ministers pay billions of Naira to secure appointments, saying comments made by its Presidential Campaign Council spokesperson, Alwan Hassan, referred to historical practices rather than the current administration.

Hassan had alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and subsequently seek to recover the money.

Speaking during an interview on Arise TV, Hassan said: “The way Asiwaju is hands-on on the expenditure of our revenue is fantastic and I love it. A lot of ministers pay billions and billions, and, you know, to get themselves appointed. The first thing they think of is how to recoup that money.”

Reacting to the statement, which has generated backlash, National Publicity Secretary of APC, Felix Morka, questioned how ministers who allegedly paid billions to secure appointments would recover such sums within Nigeria’s budgetary framework.

Speaking on Primetime, an Arise TV programme, Morka said Hassan had explained that his remarks were not directed at the current administration but were made in a historical context.

His words: “What he was referring to was not really about this administration, but he was speaking in historical context. What he said left a lot of ambiguity, some have suggested that he was speaking about appointments. He was clear as well when he said that what he was describing predated APC. As a citizen listening to him, I thought he was simply conflating systems. When he came back and said it predated the APC, that suggested to me that his frame of thought was really located, not in the present, but really in the past.

“When you are a public commentator, sometimes you generalise without really specifically drawing those lines of distinction between moments. If I say there’s corruption in Nigeria, I’m not necessarily saying that this government is corrupt. am not here to sort of overanalyse or justify comments. I think that, in due time, he alone will have to come tell what he had in his mind. But from talking to him, what I understood, after the fact, was that he was simply speaking historically, to say that ministers generally in our country have had this really terrible record of engaging in that behaviour.

“If ministers are paying billions to get appointed, how exactly, within what we know to be Nigeria’s budgetary frame, do you recoup the billions you paid to get appointed? I don’t think that is really something that, personally, I am willing to even imagine. He made a comment in historical context, as he explained it. In other democracies, lobbying for appointments is not something unusual. In the United States, there are firms that are contracted to lobby for individuals to get appointed to office. Those are usual things that happen in the background.prior to appointments.

“I think the concern here is that when lobbying becomes monetised, where people pay money to operators or to individuals with influence to procure appointments, that I think is what is really wrong.”

World.title: 2027: Kwankwaso warns INEC over alleged AI-generated images in voter register
World.content:
Kwankwaso

‎

‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

‎

‎Former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has warned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) that alleged irregularities in the preliminary voter register could undermine the credibility of the 2027 general elections.

‎

‎Kwankwaso raised the concern in a statement posted on his official Facebook page, following reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other questionable records in the register.

‎

‎He warned that failure to properly investigate the allegations could weaken public confidence in Nigeria’s electoral system ahead of the elections.

‎

‎According to him, the development raises serious questions about the integrity of the voter registration process and the measures put in place by INEC to prevent electoral manipulation.

‎

‎”With the 2027 elections approaching, INEC must provide Nigerians with clear and convincing answers,” he said.

‎

‎Kwankwaso questioned how the suspicious photographs found their way into the register, whether the individuals involved were genuinely registered and if their identities were properly verified.

‎

‎While welcoming INEC’s decision to investigate the allegations, the former governor insisted that Nigerians deserved more than assurances from the electoral body.

‎

‎He called for a thorough, transparent and independent investigation, saying the findings must be made public and anyone found responsible held accountable under the law.

‎

‎Kwankwaso also demanded a comprehensive independent audit of the preliminary voter register to identify questionable entries, duplicate registrations and possible artificial identities.

‎

‎He, however, stressed that the exercise must not deny eligible Nigerians their constitutional right to vote.

‎

‎”Our democracy cannot afford any compromise in the integrity of the voter register. Every eligible Nigerian must have the right to vote, and every vote must count,” he said.

‎

‎The former governor further warned against the use of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, to manipulate the electoral process.

‎

‎”Nobody should be allowed to exploit technology, including artificial intelligence, to undermine our electoral system,” he added.

‎

‎Kwankwaso maintained that the credibility of the 2027 general elections would depend largely on the accuracy and integrity of the voter register.

‎

‎”The credibility of the 2027 elections begins with a credible voter register, and INEC must get its act together,” he declared

World.title: Atiku challenges Tinubu to prove he’s in Makkah
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide daily proof of his presence in Makkah for Umrah, alleging that the planned pilgrimage could be a smokescreen for a trip to France.

Atiku said Nigerians deserved to know the President’s actual destination, daily engagements and the purpose of the trip, raising questions about a reported $20 billion loan request involving a French business partner.

In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said intelligence available to him suggested that Tinubu might make only a brief appearance in Makkah before proceeding to France.

He called on the Presidency to release clear, current and date-stamped photographs and videos each day showing Tinubu at the Kaaba and performing the rites of Umrah.

“Nigerians deserve verifiable proof of the President’s presence in Makkah and a transparent account of his daily activities in the Holy Land,” he said.

Atiku also questioned whether the trip was connected to the President’s health and the reported $20 billion loan request, urging the Presidency to address the concerns and disclose the full itinerary.

The former vice president said he and other Nigerians would join Tinubu in prayers for the country’s peace and progress, but warned against invoking religion without sincerity.

“No one should invoke the name of Almighty Allah in vain,” he said, insisting that a spiritual mission undertaken on behalf of the nation must be treated with seriousness and transparency.

He maintained that Nigerians were entitled to know how the trip was being funded and demanded verifiable evidence of the President’s whereabouts and activities.

World.title: FG Defends $21.7bn Loan, Says Funds Meant for Productive Ventures
World.content:
Targets single-digit inflation by end of 2027, budget ready December

•Okays East, West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW

•Okays East, West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW Moves to fortify airports against Ebola, other pathogens

•Approves N594.49bn for eight road projects nationwide

•Makinde: Tinubu, APC mortgaging Nigeria’s future

Deji Elumoye and Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The federal government yesterday defended its proposed $21.7 billion external borrowing plan, insisting that the funds would finance productive investments in infrastructure and other critical sectors to stimulate economic growth, strengthen national productivity and improve living standards.



The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said the proposed financing should be assessed based on the assets to be created and the economic returns expected, rather than simply as an addition to the country’s debt burden.



Oyedele spoke after the Federal Executive Council (FEC) meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the State House, Abuja, amid criticism of the borrowing plan by former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, as well as the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election, Peter Obi.



Oyedele maintained that the proposal was a financing plan and did not mean the federal government had already borrowed the money or would necessarily draw down the entire amount.



“Altogether, if you convert the euro amount and add it to the dollar amount, it will come up to $21.7 billion. First and foremost, this is a plan. It doesn’t mean that we have borrowed. It doesn’t even mean that we borrow all of it. So it’s a plan. The average lifespan of the projects under this plan is five years. This qualifies as investment. This is investment, not borrowing,” Oyedele pointed out.



The proposed financing comprises $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion for projects and programmes covering transportation, security, healthcare, agriculture, energy, digital infrastructure, education and social protection.



The government said transportation infrastructure accounts for approximately $10.6 billion, including major projects such as the Sokoto-Badagry and Lagos-Calabar highways and the Kano-Kaduna rail project.



Oyedele said the government was pursuing financing from multilateral and bilateral development partners, alongside other sources, to implement the projects.

Besides, about $7.9 billion is expected from multilateral and bilateral partners, with the World Bank among the major institutions providing support. Oyedele said a $5 billion World Bank component would attract concessional financing at an average interest rate of about 2.1 per cent, while some social-sector loans would carry interest rates of around 2 per cent.



He said the government was prioritising favourable financing terms to reduce borrowing costs and ensure that the projects delivered lasting economic benefits.

Government Targets Single-digit Inflation Rate



The minister also disclosed that the federal government was targeting single-digit inflation by the end of 2027, as it intensifies efforts to stabilise prices and sustain economic growth.



He said inflation had declined to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year, after peaking at about 34 per cent.



According to him, FEC resolved to intensify efforts to bring down prices, particularly food prices, while sustaining investments in infrastructure, human capital development and job creation.



Oyedele disclosed that Nigeria’s foreign reserves had risen above $55 billion, the highest level in 18 years, while net reserves had increased to more than $45 billion from less than $1 billion three years ago. He put economic growth at 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, compared with 2.74 per cent in May 2023.

The minister added that the tax-to-GDP ratio had risen from about seven per cent in 2023 to 12.5 per cent by the end of 2025, while the debt-service-to-revenue ratio had declined from 97 per cent to below 60 per cent.



Oyedele also defended the removal of petrol subsidy, arguing that the previous arrangement placed an unsustainable burden on public finances and constrained the government’s ability to invest in infrastructure and essential services.



He said Nigeria had increased petrol prices about 3,050 times in 50 years without resolving the underlying subsidy problem, adding that the government had introduced interventions to cushion the impact of economic reforms on vulnerable Nigerians.



According to him, more than 10 million households had received over N600 billion in cash transfers, while the Nigerian Education Loan Fund had disbursed N372.6 billion to more than 1.5 million students.



He added that more than 800,000 micro, small and medium-sized enterprises had benefited from subsidised loans at single-digit interest rates.

The minister further said low-income earners making up to N100,000 monthly were exempt from personal income tax, while businesses with annual turnover of up to N100 million were exempt from corporate income tax, value-added tax and withholding tax under the relevant tax reforms.



He also disclosed that the Nigerian capital market had grown from about N30 trillion to more than N160 trillion, expressing optimism about the naira’s outlook on the strength of improved foreign reserves and other economic fundamentals.

Uzoka-Anite: 2027 Budget Ready by December



The federal government also said it was working towards presenting the 2027 budget before the end of the year to allow the National Assembly sufficient time to consider the proposed fiscal framework ahead of the next financial year.



The Minister of State for Budget, Doris Uzoka-Anite, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the FEC meeting.



“We are working on the 2027 budget, and our intention is to present it before the end of the year,” she said.



Further details of the proposed budget, including its overall size, revenue projections, deficit estimates and allocations to key sectors, are expected to emerge as preparations progress.

FG Begins Procurement for East, West Super Grids



Similarly, the federal government has approved the commencement of procurement for the proposed East and West Super Grids as part of efforts to expand electricity transmission capacity from about 5,000 megawatts to 19,000MW within two years.

The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, who disclosed this after the FEC meeting, said the projects would strengthen the national grid and enable more electricity to be transmitted to consumers.



He said the government had also approved three major interventions to reinforce transmission infrastructure around Abuja and Lagos, while accelerating efforts to clear more than 300 containers of electricity equipment stranded at the nation’s ports.

The first approval covers the construction of a 33kV double-circuit underground and overhead line linked to the Katampe Transmission Substation, which serves the North-Central region.



The second involves the design, manufacture and supply of three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV power transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation, a critical facility supplying the Lagos axis.



The third project entails the reconstruction and upgrade of the 35.6-kilometre Itumola-Mapasin-Shagamu 132kV single-circuit transmission line to a double-circuit line to accommodate rising electricity demand along the Lagos-Shagamu corridor.



Tegbe said the projects formed part of the government’s broader strategy to improve transmission infrastructure, stabilise electricity supply and maximise the use of existing power-sector assets.



He disclosed that the ministry had commenced a nationwide technical audit of electricity infrastructure, dividing the country into three major energy zones: Lagos and its surrounding industrial corridor; the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano axis; and the Enugu-Onitsha-Benin axis.



According to him, the audit, which began four weeks ago, would identify ageing and weak infrastructure requiring replacement or rehabilitation to improve the reliability of the national grid.



The minister also restated that the government had paid N1.23 trillion out of the N3.3 trillion owed to gas suppliers and other stakeholders, adding that the outstanding liabilities had contributed to difficulties in ensuring adequate gas supply to power generation companies.



He said the government was working to improve the operational efficiency of the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) and the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) particularly in coordinating grid management and infrastructure development.



Tegbe explained that separating system operations from transmission infrastructure management was intended to improve efficiency, response times and coordination across the electricity network.



He added that the government was reviewing options for greater private-sector participation in electricity asset management to improve performance and ensure better utilisation of existing infrastructure.



On the super grids, Tegbe said the projects would strengthen transmission links across the northern and southern parts of the country, connecting Sokoto through Abuja and other locations to parts of the South.



He said Tinubu had approved the commencement of the procurement process, describing the initiative as a significant step towards building a more resilient electricity network capable of supporting future demand.



Tegbe also announced that construction had commenced on a new National Control Centre (NCC) in Osogbo to replace the existing facility, which he said was built 64 years ago. The new centre is expected to strengthen the monitoring and management of the national grid.

He further disclosed that the government was energising completed transmission substations in Kano, Katsina, Bauchi and Gombe, among other locations, to bring idle infrastructure into service.



The minister said the government was also expanding access to electricity through solar mini-grids, particularly in institutions and locations facing transmission constraints.



According to him, at least 14 federal universities had received installed and energised solar mini-grids, with capacities ranging from one megawatt to five megawatts. Another 11 universities were being supported through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund, bringing the number of institutions covered by the programme to nearly 30.



He stated that five teaching hospitals were also benefiting from solar power installations being implemented in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health.

On the backlog of electricity equipment stranded at the ports, Tegbe described the situation as unacceptable, saying some containers had reportedly remained uncleared for between 14 and 20 years.



He said the president had directed the ministry to work with the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) and the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) to clear more than 300 containers containing electricity equipment.



Tegbe attributed the prolonged delay to the failure of previous administrations to settle outstanding charges and complete the necessary clearance processes.

FEC Approves N45.8bn Disease Surveillance System



In the same vein, FEC has approved N45.8 billion for a biosecurity and disease surveillance system at five international airports to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to detect Ebola and other dangerous pathogens at its borders.



The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Ali Pate, disclosed this after the meeting, saying the project would be implemented under a 20-year public-private partnership concession awarded to BioHealth Consortium following the council’s approval of its full business case.

Pate described the initiative as a major investment in Nigeria’s health and economic security, warning that infectious disease outbreaks could disrupt economic activities and threaten public safety.



“Over the last two weeks, I think you realise the significance of enhancing biosecurity at our points of entry. Since COVID, we have known that there are significant vulnerabilities in terms of public health threats crossing borders and the need for coordinated, technology-driven systems for early warning, detection and response to emerging infectious disease threats,” he stressed.



The surveillance system will be deployed at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos; Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja; Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano; Port Harcourt International Airport; and Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu.



According to Pate, more than 18 million passengers pass through Nigeria’s airports annually, making effective surveillance at points of entry critical to national health security.



Under the concession arrangement, the private-sector partner will design, finance, build, operate and maintain the facilities throughout the concession period, while the federal government will provide policy, institutional and regulatory oversight.



The assets will revert to the federal government at the end of the concession in line with the agreement reviewed and endorsed by the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC).



He said the project will incorporate wastewater surveillance to detect pathogens associated with aircraft, air and surface sampling equipment, and technologies for monitoring cargo and baggage.



It will also establish a National Surveillance Operations Centre to coordinate real-time monitoring, integrate data, track incidents and support rapid responses to suspected outbreaks.



The facilities will include modern laboratories for rapid diagnostics at points of entry, with their operations integrated with those of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, Port Health Services, the Nigeria Customs Service (BCS), the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC).



Pate said the project was partly informed by lessons from Nigeria’s recent response to the Ebola threat.



He disclosed that Nigeria had maintained surveillance and containment measures before confirming an imported Ebola case in October. The patient had recovered after receiving treatment in Nigeria and was continuing to improve in her home country, he added.



The minister, however, warned that the threat remained, given the continued spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo and the possibility of other infectious diseases entering Nigeria.

Umahi: Eight Road Projects Worth N594.49bn Get Nod



FEC has also approved eight road projects worth N594.49 billion across the country, while Nigeria and four other West African countries are pursuing financing from the African Development Bank (AfDB) for their respective sections of the proposed 1,028-kilometre Lagos-Abidjan highway.

The Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, disclosed this after the meeting, saying the approved projects had contract sums ranging from N11.33 billion to N209 billion, alongside remedial works on deteriorated sections of the East-West Road.



He listed the projects to include the 18-kilometre Amaseri Road, from Ishagu to Otakot on the Enugu Expressway, awarded at N20.257 billion.

The council also approved N11.33 billion for the third phase of the Umuahia-Bende-Afikpo Road in Abia State, with about five kilometres remaining under the federal government’s scope.



Umahi explained that the project had previously been funded under the NNPC tax-credit scheme, but work stalled after the funding arrangement was discontinued.



The project was subsequently rescoped, while the Abia State Government undertook to construct the remaining 43 kilometres, he said.

In Kogi State, the council approved N160 billion for the reconstruction of the 95-kilometre E2K-Okey-Ampa-Otopa Road. It also approved N209 billion for the 81.1-kilometre Ado-Ekiti-Ijan-Ilumoba-Ikole Road in Ekiti State, including a bridge. The contract was awarded to CBC.



Other approvals include N28.218 billion for the 17-kilometre Sokoto-Illela Road, Route A1, awarded to Kespeko Global Limited, and N62 billion for a 30-kilometre road linking Adamawa and Taraba states, with five bridges. The latter contract was awarded to WeChina Nigeria Limited.



The council further approved N89.2 billion for the 47-kilometre Bichi Ring Road, including a flyover, and N14.486 billion for the eight-kilometre Dikko-Maje link road connecting to the Suleja-Minna Road. The respective contractors are Lara Lake and MW Resources Limited.



On the East-West Road, Umahi said the council considered remedial works on sections that had deteriorated partly because the road was constructed years ago and now lies below flood level.



He said ministers from Nigeria, Benin Republic, Togo, Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire would meet on Friday to discuss financing arrangements for the regional highway, with him chairing the meeting.



Under the proposed arrangement, the AfDB would provide funding to participating countries to develop their respective sections of the transnational corridor, although the financing remains subject to the outcome of the discussions and the bank’s arrangements.



Nigeria’s section, stretching from Tincan Island in Lagos to the Seme border with Benin Republic, covers 79 kilometres. The other sections comprise 89 kilometres in Togo, 576 kilometres in Ghana, 155 kilometres in Côte d’Ivoire and 128 kilometres in Benin Republic.

Makinde: Tinubu, APC Mortgaging Nigeria’s Future



Meanwhile, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has condemned the continued resort to foreign borrowing by Tinubu, cautioning that he’s deliberately mortgaging the sovereignty and future of the nation.



In a statement by the Director Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediuwa, the group vehemently rejected the latest loan 80 days to a crucial election that it said will ultimately remove him from office in May, 2027.



‘’We are deeply concerned that these loans are repeatedly justified under the omnibus of funding infrastructure, critical projects and budget deficits, yet Nigerians cannot point to commensurate projects or has this successive borrowing been able to adequately fund Tinubu’s three overlapping budget cycles, raising the question as to where monies have gone.



‘’This malignant debt cancer and insatiable appetite for foreign loans have reached alarming proportions that every well-meaning Nigerian should fear for the nation’s future as Tinubu’s government relentlessly accumulates domestic and external debts with neither commensurate development, transparent utilisation nor a credible repayment plan,’’ the campaign office said.



Ihediuwa said that this new request has reinforced the fear that Tinubu is burying Nigeria by installment.



‘’In June 2023, President Tinubu secured a $750 million World Bank loan under the Power Sector Recovery Performance programme to improve electricity supply nationwide. Ironically, Nigerians continue to endure crippling darkness, to the extent that the Aso Rock Villa is powered by a solar plant.



‘’That same month, another $500 million was borrowed for institutional strengthening and women’s empowerment. Where is the money, how many women have benefited, and where is the impact?



‘’In July 2023, the President secured another $800 million for Conditional Cash Transfers, followed by a further $700 million in September.

‘’In June 2024 President Tinubu borrowed $2.25 Billion for “Reforms for Economic Stabilization to Enable Transformation and Accelerating Stabilisation and Resilient Growth”. Today, the economy is not only atrophied, it is also neither transformed nor stabilised.



‘’In 2025, President Tinubu borrowed another $1.57 billion for healthcare, education and human-capital development, alongside another $500 million from the African Development Bank later that year.



‘’In 2025, the Senate approved an extensive borrowing plan involving $21.19 billion, €4 billion and ¥15 billion. Included was $3 billion earmarked for the Eastern Railway Corridor linking Port Harcourt to Maiduguri. Yet the corridor remains a question mark for Nigerians awaiting tangible progress as it remains as moribund as ever.



‘’In April 2026, the Senate approved $6 billion for modernizing our ports alongside another $1.5 billion for early-childhood development and household prosperity. What a bitter irony of a beautiful caption in Nigeria where millions of households struggle to afford food, while battling a devastating out-of-school-children crisis. And now comes another colossal borrowing request of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion,’’ the group recalled.



The Makinde/Daura campaign cautioned that Tinubu is steering Nigeria towards the fate of Egypt under Khedive Isma’il (1863-1880) whose dependence on foreign loans and extravagant spending drove Egypt into bankruptcy with devastating consequences on the sovereignty of that nation.



He said that it was unfortunate that at his age, Tinubu is leaving a legacy of ‘debt and enslavement’ rather than productive investments, prosperity, and economic stability.

World.title: TUC Rejects FG’s N70,000 Transport Allowance, Demands Salary Increase
World.content:
Atiku mocks relief initiative, says it can only buy 50 litres of fuel

Chuks Okocha and Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) yesterday objected to the federal government’s proposed N70,000 transport allowance to civil servants, saying temporary wage awards are not sustainable and far-reaching.



The objection came as former Vice President and presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, described the N70,000 monthly transport support for public service workers as a desperate last-minute attempt to contain public anger.



The federal government had approved a monthly transport allowance of N70,000 for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, to cushion the effects of rising living costs. The approval was announced in a memorandum of understanding (MoU) issued at the end of a conciliation meeting between government representatives and leaders of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday. The MoU was signed by Tanimu Yakubu, Director-General of the budget office; Joe Ajaero, NLC President; Garba Abdul, Permanent Secretary of the Service Welfare Office in the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation; and Muhammad Dingyadi, Minister of Labour and Employment.



However, TUC demanded immediate salary increase for workers and implementation of agreement reached with Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU).

TUC said its position was taken at its National Administrative Council meeting on October 8 in Abuja, where it sent a demand letter to the federal government through the office of Secretary to Government of the Federation.



A statement signed by TUC President, Festus Osifo, said the union would await the outcome of a meeting with the federal government to decide on the next steps to take.



The congress said the letter was in furtherance of an earlier press briefing on the economic hardship facing workers and proposed measures to address it.

On salary increase, TUC said its position was clear that the federal government should review and increase the salaries of workers. It said the government did not require any minimum wage negotiation before increasing pay, as there was no maximum wage law in the country.



It stated that some states had raised minimum wage above N100,000, adding that the federal government could raise the pay of its lowest workers to N300,000, from the current N70,000, and apply consequential adjustment.



“While it is good to negotiate minimum wage, which will affect other cadre of workers, FGN must raise wage level immediately as there are no law or historical practices stopping it from doing so,” TUC stated.



Following the letter, the TUC leadership held consultative meetings with government officials, including Secretary to Government of Federation, where its position was canvassed.



It said the proposal of wage award was mentioned, but it was vehemently rejected for several reasons.



According to TUC, temporary wage awards are not sustainable and far-reaching. The congress cited the wage award agreed on October 2, 2023, which was to be implemented until the minimum wage was agreed in 2024, but was never implemented holistically, with some workers still owed one or two months while others never received it.



TUC stated, “How do we go back to same wage award that never benefited all workers? How can workers be expected to trust fresh promises when previous obligations remain outstanding?”



It also cited irregularity in the payment of the 2023 wage award, where those who got up to four months of N40,000 never got it monthly but at intervals, while over 80 per cent of states and the informal sector never implemented any wage award.



“From the foregoing, we further reiterate our demand for pay raise for all government workers, as salary is only consistent and far-reaching pay that workers could rely upon,” TUC said.



It stressed that negotiations of a new national minimum wage must not become an excuse for postponing urgent pay increment.



On cost-of-living relief, TUC said economic crisis affected not only federal workers but also state and local government workers, as well as pensioners, private sector and informal economy workers. It called on government at all levels to implement measurable interventions to reduce the cost of essential goods, ensure timely payment of salaries and pensions, and revitalise the productive sector.



On JOHESU, Osifo said he led the organised labour team that included the JOHESU leadership to resolve the industrial action that lasted several months.

He said after several meetings at the Federal Ministry of Health, a final conciliatory meeting was held at Ministry of Labour and Employment, where a communique was agreed.



The signing led to suspension of the industrial action in good faith, but TUC said the government did not keep its side.



Under the terms of settlement, it was agreed that all outstanding issues relating to CONHESS adjustment shall be conclusively addressed without further delay, but seven months later, adjustment remained unimplemented, Osifo said.



“This continued failure to honour explicit commitment violates principle of good faith, undermines confidence in collective bargaining, and is absolutely unacceptable,” the TUC said.



It demanded immediate implementation of CONHESS adjustment, clear timetable, budgetary provisions, and resolution of outstanding matters.

TUC said its position was unequivocal that workers were demanding social and economic justice, adding that it would defend workers’ rights without retreat and pursue every legitimate avenue to compel government to honour obligations.



It said it awaited the final outcome of scheduled meetings with the government to decide the next line of action.



Meanwhile, Atiku condemned the N70,000 monthly transport support for public service workers as a desperate attempt by the federal government to contain public anger.



He said it was an admittance that government policies had made life unbearable for millions of citizens.



In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said, “The Tinubu administration is scrambling from one announcement to another, showing its failure to grasp the crisis. The cost-of-living crisis reaches beyond transport: energy, food, rent and other essentials affect every part of daily life.



“Barbers pay more to power their clippers; restaurant owners face higher cooking costs; shopkeepers struggle to keep prices down; school bus operators pay more for fuel; and families still must buy food. Every business and household are affected. Does hardship end at the bus stop?”



The statement said, “If public service workers receive N70,000 monthly for transport from November, what happens to private sector workers, traders, small businesses, transport operators and millions without formal jobs? The public workforce is only a fraction of Nigeria’s population. A temporary allowance for some cannot solve a national crisis.



“The agreement also leaves the effective date for a new minimum wage unresolved. The government must publish payment dates, explain eligibility and say when wage negotiations will produce a decision.”



Atiku said, “Any genuine relief is welcome, but a six-month allowance cannot undo this hardship. At about N1,400 per litre, N70,000 buys roughly 50 litres of petrol. What meaningful difference can 50 litres make over an entire month?



“What Nigerians are witnessing is a government that set the house ablaze with its reckless policies, then pretends to fight the inferno by throwing ice cubes at the flames. A temporary N70,000 allowance cannot extinguish a cost-of-living crisis this government ignited.



“This is the pattern: the fuel discount failed, the 90-day cost of living plan failed before it began, and now comes another temporary payment. The government promised CNG would lower transport costs, but that promise has failed. For Nigerians still paying more to commute, the CNG programme is another scam of promises, while families face the same unaffordable prices.”



The statement added, “These rushed announcements smack of political bribery and corruption. Tinubu has shown no genuine intention of clearing the monumental mess caused by his hasty subsidy removal. He offers temporary payments instead of confronting the consequences.



“Atiku has proposed a practical alternative: a transparently managed production subsidy for fuel refined in Nigeria, delivering relief at the pump. Tinubu must not punish 250 million Nigerians for the corruption and leakages of a few thousand. His arrogance prevents him from reconsidering a cocky decision, while families and businesses pay the price.



“N70,000 may help with transport, but it cannot explain why work, food and running a business have become unaffordable. Nigerians need lasting relief, decent wages and an economy that rewards honest work. When will life become affordable again?”



Atiku said his campaign would pursue practical measures to lower living costs, raise household incomes, and restore dignity to work.

World.title: Akpabio: 30 States Have Endorsed Constitution Amendment for State Police
World.content:
• Senate President expresses optimism over decentralised policing

•Urges northern youths to mobilise support for Tinubu’s 2027 re-election

• Says economic reforms need time to deliver results

•Warns against paid social media propaganda

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja





President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, on Wednesday disclosed that about 30 state Houses of Assembly had endorsed the proposed constitution amendment to establish state police.

Akpabio expressed optimism that Nigeria could soon adopt a decentralised policing system to strengthen national security.

He spoke when members of Arewa Revival Project, a northern youth organisation with membership across the 19 northern states, visited him at his office in Abuja.

The senate president said the proposed reform would improve the country’s capacity to tackle insecurity by bringing policing closer to communities.

He expressed confidence that the constitution amendment process was nearing completion, adding that the establishment of state police would complement existing security structures and enhance efforts to address the country’s security challenges.

He urged the youth to intensify grassroots mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, stating that continuity in government would allow the administration’s economic reforms and security policies to produce the desired results.

Akpabio also called on the Nigerian youth to rise above what he described as paid social media propaganda against the administration. He said the president had taken significant steps to diversify the economy, reform the tax system, and address longstanding structural problems.

He explained, “As I speak with you now, for the first time in the history of Nigeria, it may not take us a month before we have a state police system, a decentralised policing in the country, because about 30 states have endorsed the amendment to the Nigerian constitution to bring about state police system, which will further increase the security of the nation.”

The senate president expressed optimism that Nigeria would overcome its security challenges, urging the youth to remain confident in the country’s future while supporting efforts to restore peace and stability.

He stated, “I always tell them that the devil that you see today, you will soon see them no more. Very soon, we shall overcome the insecurity that we face today. So, feel confident as you go round campaigning.”

Akpabio maintained that decentralised policing would further strengthen national security, particularly by improving the ability of law enforcement agencies to respond to threats within their respective communities.

He urged the Arewa youths to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election, saying the administration needs time to consolidate its policies.

He said the president had taken steps to move Nigeria away from its longstanding dependence on crude oil revenues and introduce reforms intended to reposition the economy.

He said, “I expect the Nigerian youth to rise above social media propaganda because this president has managed to take us out of a mono-economy, an economy that was dependent only on crude oil.

“He has brought innovations to bear through the tax reform system, through tinkering with anachronistic laws.”

Akpabio stated that the administration’s performance had earned it the support of the National Assembly, declaring that lawmakers have endorsed Tinubu for a second term.

He said, “No president has achieved the level of development that he has done in this country today since independence. The naysayers will not want to say so, but I am very proud and members of the National Assembly are very proud.

“We hold our heads very high and say, yes, we have given him a pass mark and that we have endorsed him to come for a second term in office.”

Akpabio said Nigeria’s continued survival amid economic and security difficulties reflected the president’s willingness to confront the challenges facing the country.

“I give glory to God that Nigeria is still surviving, and surviving because we have a president who thinks and somebody who wants to face challenges, and he is facing the challenges,” he said.

He urged the youth to support continuity in government, stating that changing the administration before its policies fully matures could undermine the progress made so far.

He stated, “You don’t change a winning team. He is doing so well. Allow his policies to crystallise. This is not somebody who is coming to experiment. He is already doing it.”

Akpabio also emphasised the importance of youth participation in national development, saying government policies should create a stable foundation for future generations.

He said, “Whatever we are doing today, we are doing it to stabilise your future and ensure the survival of Nigeria. So, it is good that you are seeing it.”

He warned that the youth could face considerable challenges in countering criticism of the administration on social media, alleging that some individuals attacking the president and his supporters online are being paid to do so.

Akpabio alleged, “It is not going to be easy for you because most of those who are attacking the president and attacking these young men on social media are being paid. You are not being paid.”

He advised the youth to organise periodic grassroots engagements to explain government policies and challenge misinformation, rather than attempt to compete continuously with critics on social media.

He said, “You may not be able to have the kind of energy and time with them. But once in a while, gather the youth together and let them see the truth and know the truth.”

The senate president added, “Attacking a government that is working well for them, trying to bring uncertainty, is not the best.”

The visit provided an opportunity for the Arewa Revival Project to express support for Akpabio’s leadership of the National Assembly and recognise what it described as his contributions to national development.

Earlier, Project Coordinator, Arewa Revival Project, Hon. Mustafa Ibrahim, said the organisation considered Akpabio deserving of recognition because of his contributions to nation-building and the achievements recorded under his leadership of the National Assembly.

The group, whose membership spans the 19 northern states, presented the senate president with an award in recognition of his contributions to national development.

World.title: LP Chief, AA Candidate to Sue INEC over Alleged Alteration of Ogun PDP Register
World.content:
•Iyabo Obasanjo: Ogun APC afraid of facing Adebutu

Alex Enumah in Abuja and James Sowole in Abeokuta





The National Vice Chairman of the Labour Party (LP) in the South-west, Dr Arabambi Abayomi, and a governorship candidate under the platform of the Action Alliance (AA), Prof Awofala Awolola, have threatened to sue the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

They said that this is over the alleged unlawful alteration of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) membership register submitted to the commission as part of conditions for the 2027 general elections.

Both Arabambi and Awolola have formally petitioned INEC to preserve the original register and investigate information alleging that an affidavit had been sworn to explain the omission of the name of PDP’s governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, from the document.

The LP chieftain and the AA guber candidate warned that they would challenge any purported retrospective alteration of the register or administrative action, based on an allegedly unlawful substitution of the original document.

While they acknowledged that they were not in possession of the alleged affidavit, the LP chieftain and AA guber candidate called on the electoral umpire to establish whether the affidavit existed and whether it had been submitted to the commission.

Speaking with journalists yesterday in Abuja, the petitioners expressed concern that the reported affidavit might be used to seek recognition of Adebutu as the PDP’s governorship candidate for the 2027 election in Ogun State.

According to them, they had received information suggesting that INEC might publish Adebutu’s name on Thursday, October 29.

They recalled that the PDP conducted its Ogun State governorship primary in Abeokuta on May 24, 2026, adding that the membership register submitted to INEC ahead of the exercise did not contain Adebutu’s name.

They said a Certified True Copy (CTC) of the register issued by INEC on July 20, 2026, reflected the omission, adding that a PDP executive member had sworn to an affidavit explaining the omission as an error by the party.

They attributed the information to a disclosure reportedly made by a member of the PDP’s Ogun State Executive Committee, during a WhatsApp discussion.

The signatories said they had not independently verified the existence or contents of the affidavit. Citing Section 77 of the Electoral Act 2026, they argued that the statutory requirements governing party membership registers should guide INEC’s handling of the matter.

They maintained that an affidavit explaining an omission should not, on its own, be treated as authority to amend a register retrospectively.

They also referred to a Supreme Court judgment delivered on September 24, 2026, in INEC v. Zenith Labour Party, Appeal No. SC/CV/495/2026, which they said was relevant to the statutory requirements governing membership registers.

The politicians asked INEC to establish whether the alleged affidavit had been submitted, when it was received, the official who received it and the purpose for which it was presented.

They further called for an investigation into any credible evidence of improper interference with the commission’s records.

“We are placing the Commission formally on notice that any purported retrospective alteration of the membership register, or administrative recognition founded upon a legally impermissible substitution of the statutory register, will be challenged before a court of competent jurisdiction.

“We reserve the right to invoke all appropriate judicial, administrative and other lawful remedies should credible evidence establish that the relevant statutory records have been unlawfully altered, substituted, manipulated or otherwise compromised.

“The integrity of our democracy and the rule of law must be protected. We will not stand by while the rules are bent for the benefit of one man”, Arabambi said.

Meanwhile, the PDP senatorial candidate for Ogun Central, Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State of desperation and unwillingness to face a fair electoral contest, following the omission of the PDP gubernatorial candidate, Hon. Ladi Adebutu’s name from the list recently published by INEC.

Obasanjo, who represented Ogun Central between 2007 and 2011, made the allegation during an interview with The Arena, an Abeokuta-based multi-topic podcast.

She said the circumstances surrounding Adebutu’s omission suggested that political opponents were more interested in eliminating competition than winning elections through the ballot box.

The former Ogun State Commissioner for Health described the development as a threat to Nigeria’s democracy, warning that allowing powerful political interests to manipulate electoral processes could undermine the country’s democratic system.

Obasanjo explained that she initially dismissed rumours about the omission because the lists of senatorial and House of Representatives candidates had already been published.

However, she said further inquiries into Adebutu’s case raised questions about why his name was missing when other PDP candidates had completed the same processes.

“What is it that Honourable Ladi did differently than what we did? And when I asked that question, I have a scientific mind. The answer was, he did the exact same thing, right? That we all did,” she said. The next question is then why is his name not in the list?”

According to her, the investigation that followed suggested that political opponents had taken steps to influence the situation, which she described as illegal.

She maintained that no satisfactory reason had been given for Adebutu’s omission and expressed confidence that his name would eventually be restored. “His name is going to be back (on the list),” she said.

The PDP candidate argued that the issue went beyond Adebutu or the fortunes of her party, warning that allowing political opponents to remove candidates through questionable means could set a dangerous precedent.

“If this happens, then a democracy will crash because everybody that is a money bag will go to Abuja and give the neutral institution money to remove anybody they think can beat them,” she said.

“And so the idea is that, can one man’s desperation to be governor, can we allow us to kill our democracy?”

Obasanjo urged Nigerians to view the controversy as a broader test of the country’s commitment to democratic principles, noting that the survival of democracy depended on respect for established rules and electoral competition.

“It is not even about Honourable Adebutu, it’s not about PDP, it’s about the democracy Nigeria runs,” she said.

She added that repeatedly violating democratic rules could eventually destroy the system they were designed to protect.

“But every time you keep breaking rules, it eventually leads to the end of that experiment. And you don’t know which rule will break it,” she said.

Obasanjo also dismissed suggestions that the controversy surrounding Adebutu’s name could weaken the PDP’s chances in the state, insisting that the development could instead expose the opposition’s alleged fear of a competitive election.

“No. Our people are firm in what they want to do. I believe Honourable Ladi’s name will be back,” she said.

She added that the development demonstrated what she described as the opposition’s desperation to avoid a fair contest.

Obasanjo expressed confidence that the PDP would perform strongly in Ogun State, citing the party’s historical appeal and what she described as the quality of governance under former Governor Gbenga Daniel, popularly known as OGD.

World.title: African Energy Chamber Honours SLB’s Omorodion in South Africa
World.content:
Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





The African Energy Chamber (AEC), has honoured the Country Director of Schlumberger Nigeria Limited (SLB), Dr Nosa Omorodion, for his more than three-decade contributions to Nigeria and Africa’s energy industry.

The Executive Chairman of AEC, N.Y Ayuk, said the recognition included Omorodion’s role in technology development, local content advancement and the growth of indigenous energy companies.

Omorodion received the Lifetime Achievement Award at African Energy Week (AEW) 2026 in Cape Town, South Africa, in recognition of his impact on the continent’s energy sector.

Ayuk described the award recipient as “a true legend” and “a determined fighter for Africa’s energy future”, noting that his career had helped advance technical expertise, strengthen local capacity and create opportunities for African professionals and businesses.

He said Omorodion’s leadership at SLB and contributions to professional organisations had supported the development of indigenous energy companies, enabling them to improve their operations, develop assets and compete more effectively in the industry.

Ayuk also praised his role in providing guidance to national oil companies during challenging periods, describing his counsel and judgment as valuable to the sector.

Beyond his corporate responsibilities, Omorodion was recognised for championing the development of young Africans through initiatives such as the Tech Graduate Trainee Programme, SLB Young Creators Programme and Nigeria’s first AI Academy.

According to Ayuk, the initiatives have expanded access to technical training, innovation and digital skills, helping prepare young Africans for opportunities in an increasingly technology-driven energy industry.

He also highlighted SLB’s partnership with the ONE Campaign, which supported the installation of solar power systems at healthcare facilities across Nigeria to improve electricity reliability and reduce dependence on diesel generators.

Ayuk said the initiative reflected Omorodion’s belief that energy was not merely a commodity but a critical enabler of healthcare, education, economic opportunity and human dignity.

“He did not make the moment about himself. Instead, he challenged us to focus on the future and on empowering, equipping and developing Africa’s young people,” Ayuk said.

He added that Omorodion’s legacy extended beyond the leadership positions he had occupied to include the professionals he had mentored, the capacity he had helped build and the opportunities he had created for others to succeed.

Ayuk said the recognition was both a tribute to Omorodion’s achievements and a reminder that considerable work remained to strengthen Africa’s energy industry.

“The work is not finished. Communities still need reliable power. Young Africans need opportunity. Indigenous companies are still ready to grow, innovate and lead,” he said.

He added: “Your Lifetime Achievement Award honours the past, but your example points us towards the future.”

Ayuk also described Omorodion as a family man, mentor and builder whose achievements should be measured not only by his personal success but also by the number of people he had helped to advance.

He said Omorodion’s career demonstrated that effective leadership involved preparing others to take on leadership responsibilities and ensuring that institutions and communities were stronger as a result of one’s service.

World.title: Minister: Tinubu’s Reforms Yielding Results, More Gains Expected
World.content:
As PBAT Door-to-Door Movement set to unveil book on Tinubu’s reform agenda

Juliet Akoje in Abuja

The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman Ibrahim, has defended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s economic reforms, describing them as necessary and bold decisions that are beginning to deliver results despite the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians.



Sulaiman-Ibrahim stated this on Tuesday at a national press conference organised ahead of the unveiling of a book examining Tinubu’s reform agenda.

She said the president had chosen to confront the country’s longstanding economic problems rather than transfer the burden to future generations.

The book, titled The Courage to Reform: Architecture of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR – Beyond 2027: Statecraft, Vision for National Renewal, is being promoted by the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement to showcase the administration’s policies and achievements over the past three years.



According to the minister, Tinubu assumed office on May 29, 2023, amid difficult economic circumstances that demanded decisive action to address structural weaknesses in Nigeria’s economy, revenue collection system and public finances.



She explained the petrol subsidy was consuming funds that could otherwise have been invested in essential public services, including education, healthcare and road infrastructure.



She also criticised the existing tax system for placing disproportionate pressure on the people it was meant to protect.



“When Mr. President took the oath of office on 29 May 2023, he inherited hard choices that could no longer wait. A petrol subsidy was draining the resources meant for our schools, our hospitals and our roads and our tax system weighed most heavily on the people it should have protected. He could have passed the problem to the next generation. He chose to confront it,” she said.



While acknowledging the economic hardship triggered by the reforms, Sulaiman-Ibrahim said the government recognised the sacrifices Nigerian households had made.



She, however, maintained that the measures were beginning to produce positive outcomes, citing improvements in external reserves, easing inflationary pressures and renewed investor confidence.



The minister said the government did not take the difficulties experienced by citizens lightly, adding that the sacrifices would ultimately prove worthwhile as the results of the reforms became more evident.

“Those decisions came at a cost and Nigerian families have felt it. No one in this government takes that sacrifice lightly, least of all Mr. President. But I say to you today, with conviction, that the sacrifice is not in vain. The results are beginning to show,” she stated.



She identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), the new tax laws and financial autonomy for local governments as key policies intended to ensure that the gains from the economic reforms reach ordinary Nigerians.



According to her, the student loan scheme is widening access to higher education for students from disadvantaged backgrounds, while the tax reforms are intended to shield low-income earners and small businesses from excessive taxation.

“Under the new tax laws, low-income earners and small businesses are protected, so that those with the least are asked to carry the least. And with financial autonomy for local governments, resources now flow closer to our communities,” she said.

Addressing the implications of the reforms for women and vulnerable households, the minister said the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda had placed social protection and the creation of economic opportunities for women and girls among its priorities.

She explained that her evaluation of government policies was based on their practical impact on women engaged in trading, girls attending school and families living on the margins of society.

She added that the administration remained committed to tackling the difficulties confronting vulnerable Nigerians.

“I judge every reform by one test. Does it reach the woman in the market, the girl in the classroom and the family at the margins? On that test, I can say with pride that our leader and father has kept women at the heart of the Renewed Hope Agenda,” the minister said.

On questions concerning the tangible benefits of the reforms and Nigeria’s increasing borrowing needs, Sulaiman-Ibrahim argued that countries required substantial investments in productive sectors and essential infrastructure to achieve sustainable economic growth.

She maintained that public borrowing was not necessarily a sign of economic failure, noting that developed economies also relied on debt to finance their activities.

She cited the United States as an example of a country that continued to borrow despite having one of the world’s largest economies.

“Show me a country that has developed, that has a strong economy, that is not in debt. I think the most indebted country in the world is the United States of America. And they’re still borrowing,” she said.

The minister further stressed that borrowing should be assessed against the economic value and developmental benefits of the projects financed with the funds.

She acknowledged the importance of responsible debt management, insisting that borrowed resources must be directed towards projects and sectors capable of generating measurable economic returns.

According to her, Nigeria still has significant investment gaps in critical infrastructure and essential systems, making additional resources necessary to address longstanding development challenges.

“One thing I can assure you of is Mr. President will take us to the promised land. He means well for the Nigerian people,” she added.

On the reported increase in the number of out-of-school children in Nigeria from 14 million to 20 million, Sulaiman-Ibrahim acknowledged the seriousness of the challenge but said the government was adopting broader interventions beyond conventional classroom education.

She identified science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education, alongside technical and vocational education and training (TVET), as part of the measures being pursued to expand learning opportunities and equip young people with relevant skills.

The minister also said the administration had increased its attention to early childhood education, skills acquisition and investment in the education sector.

She explained that the government was adopting a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to address educational challenges and improve children’s access to learning.

“Mr. President is a thinking President, so we’re running a thinking government. We’re very deliberate,” she said.

Sulaiman-Ibrahim further urged Nigerians to understand that the benefits of government reforms and policy announcements might not be felt immediately, explaining that implementation often depended on funding arrangements, administrative adjustments and coordination among relevant institutions.

She expressed confidence that the Tinubu administration would fulfil its commitments, while calling on the media to provide citizens with accurate and factual information about the reforms as political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The minister urged journalists to ensure that public discussions about the administration’s policies were guided by verifiable information rather than misinformation as the country approaches the next general election.

“As 2027 approaches, the national debate will grow louder. Let it also grow wiser, and let it rest on facts. I urge you, the press, to carry those facts to every corner of this country,” she said.

The forthcoming book unveiling is expected to feature President Tinubu as the Special Guest of Honour, with Alhaji Aliko Dangote serving as Chief Launcher and Alhaji Abdul Samad Rabiu as Co-Chief Launcher.

High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, is listed as the Chief Host, while the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, will serve as Host.

The Senate President, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, state governors and other prominent political and business leaders are also expected to attend the event.

World.title: NESI Week Deferred Till December to Align with Power Sector Reforms
World.content:
Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





The Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry (NESI) Week, earlier scheduled to hold on November 15, 2026, has been rescheduled to December 13–19 to enable stakeholders to align the programme with the ongoing power sector reforms of President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

The convener of NESI Week, Dr. Obiora Anthony, disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja, explaining that the change would allow the Federal Ministry of Power, investors and other industry stakeholders to harmonise their objectives ahead of the conference.

He said the event, which is designed to bring global players in the electricity industry together under a public-private partnership framework, would focus on strengthening Nigeria’s power infrastructure and improving electricity supply.

“The theme of the conference is: ‘Powering the Future’, where key stakeholders will speak on the electricity and energy ecosystem, for policy dialogue, business engagements, investment, innovations and strategic partnership,” Anthony said.

He added that the revised dates would provide more time for stakeholder coordination and adequate preparation for the programme, while appreciating the continued support of partners and prospective participants.

The week-long event will feature the NESI CEO and Policy Forum, NESI Expo, NESI Innovation Challenge, NESI Energy Future Experience, NESI Games and Awards, the statement added.

The activities are expected to bring together policymakers, industry leaders, investors, innovators and technology providers to discuss developments across the electricity value chain.

Anthony urged sponsors, exhibitors, speakers, media partners and participating institutions to take note of the new dates.
