World.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
World.content:
Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas

toggle caption i David Goldman/AP

The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.

Methane is a major contributor to climate change and is estimated to be 80 times more planet-warming than carbon dioxide in a twenty-year time frame. In 2023, the Biden administration finalized rules that were meant to rein in methane emissions from the oil and gas sector.

President Trump made the announcement while campaigning in Lubbock, Texas, Tuesday, saying his administration's revision, under the Clean Air Act, would save the industry billions in production costs and spur more domestic drilling. The proposal comes as Republicans face a backlash from voters over high gas prices heading into the midterms.

Sponsor Message

"Behind every barrel of oil and every cubic foot of natural gas produced in the U.S. are millions of workers, businesses, and the heartbeat of this nation's economy. The Biden EPA destructively targeted all this," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a press release.

The oil and gas industry, which vigorously opposed the 2023 rules, said EPA's proposed rollback will address some of the challenges companies have faced in trying to comply with the regulations.

"We look forward to working with the Trump administration on a more workable approach that supports American energy production, provides greater regulatory certainty and advances continued emissions reductions," Dustin Meyer, vice president at the American Petroleum Institute, a trade organization for the U.S. oil and gas industry, said in a statement.

But environmentalists say this may end up actually costing the industry more.

"Methane is natural gas, or natural gas is methane," says Jon Goldstein, associate vice president at the Environmental Defense Fund. "And so if you're capturing more natural gas, you're not allowing it to leak out, you're not allowing it to be flared, you have more product that you can sell. And so that offsets a lot of the costs."

"That is harmful to our energy security, and it's harmful to taxpayers that ought to be seeing royalty and tax revenue collected off of this gas that's going to waste," Goldstein adds.

Sponsor Message

One of the regulations the EPA wants to cut is the "Methane Super Emitter Program." Across the U.S., oil and gas pipelines, refineries, and other energy facilities sometimes have huge leaks of methane. But methane is invisible and difficult, not to mention expensive, to detect. The super emitter program is supposed to take effect in January 2027. It would allow the government to delegate monitoring for big methane leaks to certified third parties, including private and nonprofit methane satellite programs.

"The easiest way to think about it is that if the government is alerted to a big leak, then if it's reported by certified third parties, then they could use that information," says Paasha Mahdavi, a political science professor at UC Santa Barbara who studies the oil industry.

"[The government] needs help from other people to say, 'Hey! You're breaking the law!' so they're able to prosecute," Mahdavi adds.

If that program goes away, Mahdavi says it will be harder for the government to spot large leaks of the planet-heating gas from oil and gas facilities. "And we need that because it's really hard to see this stuff," he says.

The EPA's announcement would also loosen regulations on methane leaks coming from low-volume "marginal" oil wells that are considered "marginally economic," meaning they don't make much money.

"People assume marginal well must equal small emissions," Goldstein says. But he says satellites and new technology find that's not true. "These old sort of end-of-life wells nearing the end of their production life are actually responsible for the lion's share of methane pollution from the [oil and gas] production sector," Goldstein says.

The EPA plans to hold at least a 45-day public comment period, including a public hearing, once the proposed rule changes are published in the Federal Register.

World.title: New book revisits the 2023 killing of an unhoused man in crisis on the NYC subway
World.content:
New book revisits the 2023 killing of an unhoused man in crisis on the NYC subway

toggle caption i Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images

On May 1, 2023, an unhoused Black man named Jordan Neely boarded the New York City subway. For years, Neely had drawn crowds with his Michael Jackson impersonation, but on that day he was in crisis, shouting threats and frightening fellow passengers.

A white former Marine named Daniel Penny stepped in, putting Neely into a chokehold for six minutes, killing him. Later, a video of the encounter divided the country. To some, Penny was doing what the police weren't there to do. To others, Neely was a victim, another Black man whose life had been treated as disposable.

Sponsor Message

Journalist Anand Giridharadas spent more than two years investigating what the video couldn't show. He wanted to write a story "that would take us to the heart of America and what it means to live in this country, in this moment." When tragic stories become social media fodder, Giridharadas says, "human beings become caricatures."

In December 2024, Penny was acquitted of criminally negligent homicide after a jury hung on a second degree manslaughter charge and the prosecution dismissed it. Within days of the verdict, Vice President-elect JD Vance invited Penny to the Army-Navy game alongside President-elect Trump. Soon afterward, a Silicon Valley venture capital firm gave him a job.

In his new book, Man in the Mirror: Hope, Struggle, and Belonging in an American City, Giridharadas posits that both men felt let down by the systems that should have protected them.

"I think Jordan Neely had felt abandoned for a very long time, and had reason to feel that way," Giridharadas says. "Daniel Penny would claim that he felt abandoned in terms of law enforcement not being there, and in terms of all the systems that had allowed Jordan Neely to be in that subway car in that condition instead of all of the other conditions that he might have been in had there been a better system of care."

Giridharadas says it's that sense of abandonment that leads people to take matters into their own hands, often with tragic results: "I think it behooves us to think about the condition in which we've left people, this sense of abandonment that we've allowed to be so pervasive that decent people feel like maybe there's no other route for folks besides just DIYing it."

Sponsor Message

Interview highlights

Knopf

On Jordan Neely's criminal record and the city's attempt at rehabilitation

He had a record of interactions with the police that went back more than a decade. But it was very trivial stuff at the beginning. It was essentially the stuff of what it takes to be homeless in New York, jumping turnstiles, sleeping rough. And then in more recent years, it had gotten more serious and he'd committed a couple of violent crimes, assaults, punching a woman in the face, things like that. And he had gone to Rikers. He'd been charged. And then as part of this alternative to incarceration program — and there are programs like this popping up around the country, where folks get an alternative to going to prison that is considered more restorative, more in line with actually helping people who have substance issues or other issues — he gets to avail of one of these programs. Prosecution, defense, they all agree. And he gets sent to this kind of rehab facility in the Bronx instead of prison. And one day, he just walks out of that facility.

And then, in April 2023, just a few weeks before he died, he is [at] Coney Island, one of the terminal points on the subway system, and he's acting erratically on the platform. Outreach workers try to deal with him to no avail. The cops have some interaction with him, but they don't actually realize that it is the guy who is out with a warrant for his arrest because he walked out of this program. And the outreach workers who were there that night don't quite realize that he's a guy that their agency knows very well, just maybe not those individual workers. And he sort of runs off into the night. And a few weeks later, he's dead on the floor of a different subway car.

On Daniel Penny's origins in West Islip, Long Island

These towns in central Long Island have this very complicated relationship [with New York City]. … On the one hand, it's very out of the city, but it's right there. A lot of people commute in every day for work. Some don't. These are towns that were largely populated by white flight in the last several decades. … In many ways, these are towns that are almost like middle-class refugee camps from the squalor and terror of New York City.

Sponsor Message

Maybe even understanding immigrant stories is a more helpful framework for understanding these places. … Immigrants have very complicated relationships with the places they leave. We don't think about that with places that are 45 minutes away from a metropolis, but I actually think that is the way to understand the town in which Daniel Penny grew up. … These are communities where there's often a contempt, often barely concealed, for all the people one wanted to get away from, when one left.

On whether Penny showed remorse

I can't know what's in his heart. I didn't sense that kind of sadness or remorse. And not only did I not necessarily pick that up in that brief conversation we had at his victory party a year and a half after the incident, but one of the things that's striking in both the bodycam video on the scene when they first get there, as well as the interrogation ... is that even in those moments, forget remorse, he doesn't even seem to have curiosity about what may have happened to that guy.

On Penny's MAGA popularity

He sort of gave the impression of a kind of blankness, ideologically. And that was one of the things that then became very strange, that all these people really wanted him to be their symbol and projected onto him all these ideas. And then he, of course, willingly embraced it. He embraced the money that came from it. And then, most dramatically still, at the end of the case, not only was he content to appear with JD Vance and Donald Trump at the Army-Navy game, but shortly thereafter, he got a job offer that gobsmacked many people. This is someone who, I think, has not graduated from college. He was offered a job as a partner at the venture capital firm in Silicon Valley called Andreessen Horowitz. ... He was made partner on their American dynamism team, which is a team that invests in startups that do weapons systems and drones and other things supposedly in the national interest.

Sponsor Message

On the politicization of the case and parallels with Luigi Mangione

I had spent the last year and a half hearing Daniel Penny's people make an argument that was basically like, "The system wasn't there, the system wasn't responsive. Daniel Penny stepped into a void and did what he had to do, took matters into his own hands because of this void." And then in the jury deliberations during that moment was the Mangione assassination of Brian Thompson, of United Health Care. And as that case started to become better known, a similar argument started to develop around Luigi Mangione, this time on the parts of the left instead of parts of right that Luigi Mangione was stepping into this void of a cruel healthcare system and stepping in because so many people were abandoned and he felt abandoned. …

And then Hawk Newsome, Black Lives Matter activist in New York, says, yes ... if they're gonna have vigilantes, we need Black vigilantes. But we also need to make our own schools, we need to have our own media, we have to have our own everything.

And I just thought to myself, gosh, is this the last kind of common thread? The idea that you could hear on the far right, the far left, and elsewhere that we're abandoned, the system's rigged, no one's listening, take matters into your own hands. The sense of, somebody step up. Somebody do something.

Anna Bauman and Thea Chaloner produced and edited this interview for broadcast. Bridget Bentz, Molly Seavy-Nesper and Beth Novey adapted it for the web.

World.title: Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains stubborn
World.content:
Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains stubborn

toggle caption i Andrew Harnik/Getty Images North America

The Federal Reserve opted not to raise interest rates Wednesday, but signaled that it's not retreating from the fight against stubborn inflation.

The central bank renewed its pledge to deliver price stability, a goal that's been made more difficult by a spike in energy prices tied to the U.S. war with Iran.

"Inflation remains elevated," the Fed's rate-setting committee acknowledged in a statement.

At its last policy meeting in September, the Fed raised rates for the first time in more than three years. Since then, data has shown inflation has continued to accelerate, with consumer prices in September up 3.7% from a year ago — a bigger annual increase than the previous month.

Sponsor Message

"It's 'wrong way," says Dan North, a senior economist at the insurance company Allianz Trade. "That inflation line is going up, not down."

The decision not to adjust interest rates comes less than a week before votes are tallied in the midterm election, which may have contributed to the Fed's caution.

"It would be suspicious if there were a hike before the midterm," North said.

Loading...

A December hike is looking likely

After a pause at this week's meeting, Fed policymakers are widely expected to raise their benchmark interest rate at their next meeting in December, in an effort to tamp down demand and bring prices under control.

Two members of the rate-setting committee wanted to move more quickly. Fed governor Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack of the Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank voted to raise rates by a quarter percentage point on Wednesday, while a majority of Fed policymakers opted to stand pat.

The Federal Reserve's benchmark rate — currently 3.75 to 4% — helps to establish the cost of other short-term lending for things like credit cards.

Longer-term interest rates are set by the bond market but can also be influenced by Fed decisions. Mortgage rates climbed to a three-year high of 7.4% earlier this month, before easing slightly. The high cost of home loans has been a drag on the housing market, which has been in a slump for the last four years.

Sponsor Message

AI helps prop up the economy

Other parts of the economy are less sensitive to rising interest rates. The booming investment in artificial intelligence, for example, shows no sign of slowing down, no matter how much the Fed tries to tap on the brakes.

"The A.I. companies don't care what interest rate they have to pay," North says.

The frenzied push to build A.I. data centers is pushing up prices for construction materials and electronic equipment.

Consumer spending has also remained resilient, fueled in part by upper-income shoppers who benefit from the rising stock market.

That's not the case for less wealthy families, whose wages are not keeping pace with the rising cost of living. Average wages rose just 3% for the 12 months ending in September.

"Lower and middle-income Americans are having a real struggle," says Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's Analytics. " Their purchasing power is actually declining. And that's a pretty uncomfortable place to be. And that likely goes to explain to a large degree why people don't feel very good about the economy."

World.title: EU dropping associate membership title for its closer alliance with Canada
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The words "associate membership" were removed from a joint statement expected to be released at this week's Canada-EU summit, according to a draft seen by CBC News.

But while the statement is now expected to use softer language promising closer ties between the 27-member bloc and Canada, the head of the European Union's executive body continued to use the term in a social media post as she landed in Montreal on Wednesday.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen surprised many last month when she announced the EU would begin the process of making Canada its first associate member — a status that does not exist within the bloc — raising concerns among some members and Canadian politicians about what that would look like.

The draft statement now calls for an "ever closer association." It says this deepening relationship, repeatedly dubbed an "alliance for the future" — language previously used by Prime Minister Mark Carney — will be rooted "in a more active foreign and security policy partnership."

A source speaking to CBC News on the condition they not be named says this statement is now finalized by EU member countries, but Canada could still ask for changes.

Another source said some EU countries opposed the term "associate member," particularly Germany who called it a red line.

News that the summit's joint statement won't mention associate membership was first reported by Politico.

WATCH | 'Names or nomenclature' don't matter, says Carney: EU agreement 'names or nomenclature' don't matter, says Carney | Duration closed caption 0:42 Prime Minister Mark Carney says what 'matters' at the EU summit set to take place later this week in Montreal is 'Canada as a whole becoming a more independent, more sovereign nation so we can live our lives as we choose.'

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday before a cabinet meeting, Carney said the title of Canada's relationship to the EU shouldn't matter as long as it delivers for Canadians.

"The good news is it doesn't matter about specific names or nomenclature," he said.

"What matters is the difference that it will make to the lives of Canadians … and Canada as a whole becoming a more independent, more sovereign nation, so we can live our lives as we choose."

'Associate member' ambitions

Touching down in Montreal ahead of the two-day event, von der Leyen continued to use the term "associate member."

"An ocean separates Europe and Canada. Yet we have never felt closer. We have a new ambition: bringing Canada closer to us than ever before, as associate member of the EU," she posted to social media.

"Montreal, we're about to write a new chapter in our shared history."

The summit comes as the Canadian government is looking to to boost trade, investment and strategic partnerships with the EU bloc as part of a plan to reduce economic reliance on the United States under the unpredictable and volatile leadership of U.S. President Donald Trump.

The version of the EU-Canada statement seen by CBC News commits to reinforcing "a predictable trade environment, deepening collaboration in the Arctic, countering foreign information manipulation and interference and continued support for Ukraine."

It also includes commitments to strengthen co-operation on energy security, build up critical mineral supply chains and advance co-operation on artificial intelligence security and safety.

On Thursday, Carney will host a roundtable with business leaders on the margins of the summit. He will then host a dinner in honour of von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa.

World.title: Milwaukee Brewers defeat Tampa Bay Rays to become 1st-time World Series champions
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers playing in the smallest market in the majors are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history.

Hey, Milwaukee: raise a beer and prepare for that parade.

Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings of two-hit ball, rookie Cooper Pratt got two more hits and two RBIs, and the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field.

"It's the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here. I know the city's waited a long, long time for this," Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich said. "We're so happy to bring it home to them. I can't wait to get back there and celebrate."

Members of the Tampa Bay Rays watch during the ninth inning of Game 5 of the World Series, which the team lost to the Brewers. (Kim Klement Neitzel/Imagn Images/Reuters)

World Series MVP William Contreras hit an RBI double and Misiorowski allowed just two hits before leaving the game because of a right calf cramp. He got a standing ovation from the Brew-Crew fans, who took over the section behind Milwaukee's dugout for the last three games.

The 22-year-old Pratt set a Series rookie record with six straight hits before a sacrifice fly in the sixth inning. Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits.

"This is one of the greatest moments of my life. Oh my gosh. It doesn't even feel real," said Pratt, who made his major league debut in June. "This is surreal. It only took four months!"

Milwaukee players Jackson Chourio (right) and Sal Frelick (left) hug after their team won. (Chris O'Meara/The Associated Press)

The World Series title comes in the 58th season for a franchise that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee the following year. The Brewers' only previous trip to the World Series in 1982 ended in heartbreak when they blew a 3-1 lead in the sixth inning of Game 7 and lost 6-3 to the St. Louis Cardinals.

But Pat Murphy's team displayed the resilience of the 67-year-old manager, who survived a heart attack in 2020 and was the NL Manager of the Year in his first two full seasons at the helm in 2024 and 2025.

'They were a team'

"This group of guys right here, the 2026 team, will be remembered forever — and they deserve that because they were a team," Murphy said. "When you talk about this team, you've got to talk about people who care about each other. They're not worried about their own stats. No one cares about that. They care about coming together and winning tonight."

With their flame-throwing, 24-year-old two-time All-Star Misiorowski on the mound, the Brewers rebounded from a heartbreaking, 4-3 extra-inning loss in Game 4 when they were three outs away from a sweep in the 12th before a stellar bullpen finally faltered.

William Contreras of the Milwaukee Brewers reacts after hitting an RBI double in the sixth inning. (Mike Stobe/Getty Images)

"I don't even have words," Misiorowski said. "It's amazing, just watching my guys celebrate. And the city — I know they're going crazy in Milwaukee. It's awesome."

Pitching on four days' rest for only the fifth time in 34 starts this season, including the playoffs, the Miz had his longest outing since throwing 6 1/3 innings against the Cubs on Sept. 8. Leg cramps also forced him out of two outings earlier in the season.

Milwaukee Brewers starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski celebrates the end of the fourth inning. (Ashley Landis/The Associated Press)

Misiorowski, who broke the World Series velocity record with a 103.5 mile-per-hour fastball on the first pitch of the Series last Friday, opened with 12 straight four-seamers between 100.9-103 miles per hour. He topped at 103 twice among his 86 pitches, 58 strikes.

Misiorowski didn't record a strikeout in the first three innings for the first time in his brief career and finished with two, matching his career low. He was fired up after Yandy Diaz missed a cutter to end the fifth. The Miz pumped his fist twice and punched the air walking off the mound.

The NL Cy Young Award favourite allowed one run over five innings to get his first postseason win as a starter in a 3-2 victory in the series opener. He was 2-0 with a 0.84 ERA in the Series.

JoJo Romero got two outs, Abner Uribe recorded two more and closer Trevor Megill pitched the last two innings, allowing an RBI double to Chandler Simpson with two outs in the ninth.

Milwaukee Brewers closer Trevor Megill was on the mound for the final outs of Game 5. (Carmen Mandato/Getty Images)

Megill retired Richie Palacios on a grounder to second to end it, threw his arms in the air and was mobbed by teammates near the mound while Brewers fans celebrated in the stands.

"Milwaukee has waited 44 years, and Milwaukee, you have your world championship," principal owner Mark Attanasio said from the postgame stage on the field.

World.title: 'It feels fantastic,' Scott Gillingham says after winning another term as Winnipeg mayor
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

After winning his second consecutive term as Winnipeg mayor, Scott Gillingham says the city's best days are still to come.

He had 39.8 per cent of the ballots cast, with all polls reporting just before 10 p.m. The second-place candidate, former city councillor and provincial MLA Kevin Klein, received 20.7 per cent of votes.

Software developer Noah Redden finished a close third, with 19.8 per cent of votes, while funeral director Mike Vogiatzakis garnered 9.7 per cent.

Redden saw his support more than triple in a public opinion poll this month, increasing from four per cent in September to 14 per cent, placing him on par with Vogiatzakis.

CBC projected Gillingham's win about an hour after polls closed across Manitoba, at 8 p.m.

"It feels fantastic," Gillingham said as he paraded through a crowd of supporters at his campaign watch party in St. James, shaking hands and receiving high-fives as he made his way toward the stage.

A former city councillor, Gillingham won his first term as mayor in 2022. He squeaked by on election night with 27.5 per cent of the popular vote, repelling a comeback bid by former mayor Glen Murray to win by only 4,391 votes.

Gillingham supporters cheer after he was projected to reclaim the role. (James Turner/CBC)

Gillingham said he knew he had a lot to prove after being elected by such a small margin four years ago.

"Four years have passed. You've seen me do this job. You've seen the decisions that I have made and the work that we have done together, and tonight, you have given me the honour of serving as your mayor once again," the mayor said while addressing his supporters.

"I still believe our city's best days are ahead of us."

Nine new faces will join council after all the votes were counted — the most since Winnipeg's city council was reduced to 15 positions, not including the mayor, before the 1992 election.

Four incumbents — Russ Wyatt (Transcona), Devi Sharma (Old Kildonan), Ross Eadie (Mynarski) and Shawn Dobson (St. James) — lost their seats to Lora Meseman, Greg McFarlane, Natalie Smith and Kelly Ryback, respectively.

WATCH | Gillingham's victory speech: Winnipeg Mayor Scott Gillingham speaks to supporters after re-election win | Duration closed caption 2:46 Scott Gillingham delivered a victory speech to a room full of cheering supporters after he was re-elected as Winnipeg's mayor Wednesday night. He won a higher percentage of the vote than he did four years ago.

Five of the nine new councillors were elected in wards where there was no incumbent candidate. Jeff Palmer won in Fort Rouge-East Fort Garry, while Chris Sigurdson won St. Vital, Ray DuBois took St. Norbert-Seine River, Sara MacArthur took River Heights-Fort Garry and Jasmine Brar won Waverley West.

Evan Duncan (Charleswood-Tuxedo-Westwood), Cindy Gilroy (Daniel McIntyre), Vivian Santos (Point Douglas), Matt Allard (St. Boniface), Emma Durand-Wood (Elmwood-East Kildonan) and Jeff Browaty (North Kildonan) are the six incumbent Winnipeg councillors who retained their seats.

It would have been historic if Gillingham lost the race. The last sitting mayor to suffer an election-night defeat in the city was George Sharpe, who came up short in a narrow loss to Independent MLA Stephen Juba in 1956.

Gillingham and his wife, Marla, celebrate his win. (Michael Fazio/CBC)

A recent public opinion survey suggested that although Gillingham had more support than any other candidate, his early and seemingly insurmountable lead was nearly halved about a week before election day.

Klein, a former city councillor and provincial MLA, phoned Gillingham to concede at his watch party.

"It's very hard to beat an incumbent," Klein said, speaking to supporters as he conceded the election.

WATCH | Klein concedes mayoral race: Kevin Klein makes concession speech as CBC project Scott Gillingham re-elected | Duration closed caption 2:26 Winnipeg mayoral candidate Klein says he's proud of the fact that he stuck to his vision for the city, as CBC projects incumbent Scott Gillingham will win a second term as mayor.

Standing next to his wife, Heather, he said he's proud of how his campaign stayed true to their vision.

"Our vision was not for us. Our vision was for our children, our grandchildren and their grandchildren, and we wanted to build a Winnipeg that they would be proud of."

Scott Gillingham's campaign manager, Luc Lewandoski, said they were encouraged by the results they were seeing throughout the day.

"It really did feel like … all the markers were hitting green — we couldn't ask for a better situation."

Lewandoski said there's bound to be an element of dissatisfaction with an incumbent but that tonight was less about people voting strategically, and more a reflection of people getting on board with Gillingham's message.

"This is a story of growth tonight. This is more people across the city coming on board with Scott Gillingham's message," Lewandoski said.

There were 54 council candidates and more than 90 school trustee candidates in Winnipeg, the city said.

All Winnipeg races were contested this year; in 2022, two councillors won re-election by acclamation.

Mynarski councillor-elect Natalie Smith hugs supporter Andrew Kohan after unseating incumbent Ross Eadie. (James Turner/CBC)

Voter turnout in the city has waxed and waned in Winnipeg's six elections since 2002. The 2022 election that saw Gillingham first elected mayor recorded a 37.5 per cent voter turnout — the lowest since 2006.

Voter turnout was much higher in 2014 , when Brian Bowman was first elected mayor, with 50 per cent of electors casting ballots.

This year, a record number of Winnipeggers took advantage of advance voting to cast their ballot, the city said.

New Thompson mayor

Manitobans outside of Winnipeg also voted for new leaders and councils.

Incumbent mayor Colleen Smook was defeated in Thompson.

Oswald Sawh has secured his first term as the northern Manitoba city's mayor, with all six polls reporting as of 10:15 p.m Wednesday.

Sawh has served several stints as a city councillor since moving to Thompson in 1993. He was first elected in 2002 and served two terms, taking on the role of deputy mayor in both terms.

Smook became the first woman to be elected Thompson's mayor in 2018. She served a term as a city councillor before gaining the mayor's chair.

Two veteran politicians who served with each other on Brandon city council also battled to become mayor of Manitoba's second-largest city.

Incumbent Jeff Fawcett emerged as the winner, with 23 of 28 polls reporting shortly before 11 p.m., CBC projects.

Fawcett was elected Brandon mayor four years ago, after serving on council for three terms. His opponent, Len Isleifson, is also a former city councillor and was MLA for Brandon East from 2016 to 2023.

Advance voting in the Wheat City also set a new record in 2026, with more than triple the number of advance votes cast in 2022, far exceeding any advance poll held in the city in the last 20 years, officials said previously.

Incumbent mayors in several Manitoba communities, including Portage la Prairie, Steinbach, Winkler, Niverville and Selkirk, were acclaimed after no challengers registered to run.

Several places, such as the Municipality of Cartwright-Roblin and the Rural Municipality of Argyle, saw their entire slate of council candidates acclaimed .

Up north, residents in Flin Flon voted for a new mayor after Mayor George Fontaine did not run again. Three names were on the mayoral ballot in Flin Flon.

In The Pas, three candidates are also battling for an open mayor's seat . The northern town has been without a mayor since August, after Andre Murphy stepped down from the job.

Three Manitoba communities — Winnipeg Beach, Victoria Beach and Dunnottar — held elections earlier this year. Only one mayor — Penny McMorris, the incumbent in Victoria Beach — was acclaimed.

World.title: Higher mortgage costs set to depress already ‘bleak’ housing market
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The Bank of Canada just hiked its trendsetting policy rate for the first time in three years, and that means mortgage rates are on the move for some Canadians.

The central bank raised its benchmark rate by a quarter of a point to 2.5 per cent on Wednesday. Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem says more hikes could be coming if inflation — which is largely linked to rising fuel costs — persists in the months ahead.

Canada's major banks are already responding by raising their prime interest rates in step with Wednesday's decision. All five of Canada's major banks raised their prime rates by a quarter point to 4.70 per cent. That's the rate they offer their most credit-worthy customers.

Variable rate mortgages will increase first, as they are directly linked to the issuing bank's prime rate.

Rates for new fixed mortgages are linked to the bond market. When a central bank raises interest rates, newly issued bonds offer higher payouts. As investors demand higher yields, lenders increase mortgage rates to maintain their profit margin.

"In a rising rate environment, choosing whether to go fixed or variable can be really challenging. Variables are lower, and provide flexibility, but future rate increases need to be budgeted for," Clay Jarvis, a mortgage expert at Ratehub.ca, stated in a press release after Wednesday's rate announcement.

"Fixed rates are elevated, but once you qualify your mortgage costs are set. That kind of stability can be worth paying a premium for," he added.

Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem speaks during a news conference on Wednesday in Ottawa, where the central bank's governing council decided to hike interest rates by a quarter per cent. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

Speaking to reporters in Ottawa on Wednesday, Macklem acknowledged that rising interest rates could be uncomfortable for many Canadians and businesses.

"Look, we get it," he said. "It's not going to feel good immediately, but that's how you get inflation back down, and that will feel good for Canadians and Canadian businesses."

Variable rate mortgage holders will feel it most

The Bank of Canada's first rate hike since July 2023 will be immediately felt by variable rate mortgage holders. Toronto-based broker Marcus Tzaferis says that change could be significant.

On a $500,000 mortgage, a rate hike of 25 basis points would add about $70 per month on average to a holder's monthly payments. It might not sound like a lot, but, Tzaferis said, "to a consumer that's already stretched, these 25 basis point incremental increases are going to have an impact."

The central bank also signalled that more rate hikes could be on the horizon — and if the bank hiked rates by another 50 or 75 basis points, Tzaferis said, "you can see how that will affect people's monthly budgets."

Because rate hikes were expected, Tzaferis says he's already been fielding calls from Canadians trying to assess their options.

Barbara Best stands in the kitchen of her Toronto condo on Wednesday. She recently switched from a variable to a fixed rate mortgage and says the price increase is worth it for the peace of mind. (Laura MacNaughton/CBC)

Like Barbara Best. She's had a variable rate mortgage on her Toronto condo since 2022 — the same year the Bank of Canada began a long cycle of rate hikes — but recently renegotiated to a fixed rate months in advance of when her mortgage was up for renewal.

Because fixed rates are currently much higher than variable ones, that means she's paying a lot more each month, but Best says it's worth it.

"It was a jump in payment but it gives me that certainty. It gives me that peace of mind," Best said.

Tzaferis says "now is the time" to shop around for a fixed rate mortgage if holders want to get out of a variable one, or if their mortgage is coming up for renewal soon.

"The kind of most critical thing is for Canadians to start their renewal process early," Tzaferis said. Being aware of what the best rates on the market are and getting the conversation started with an adviser could help consumers make a choice that's right for them, according to Tzaferis.

Hike could pour more cold water on housing market

The hike also stands to worsen the already soft housing market.

Deputy governor Carolyn Rogers said Canada's housing market is already struggling, particularly in Ontario and British Columbia, and the rate increase will add to those pressures.

WATCH | Bank of Canada's housing outlook 'pretty subdued': Bank of Canada's housing outlook 'pretty subdued' — but not just because of rates, official says | Duration closed caption 1:23 Bank of Canada senior deputy governor Carolyn Rogers, speaking after the central bank hiked a key interest rate, said the organization's outlook for housing is 'pretty subdued' for a few reasons, including overall economic uncertainty.

Wednesday's rate hike shrinks the pool of eligible buyers, shifting power from sellers to those who can qualify for the financing needed to make a purchase. Home prices could dip lower.

Earlier this month, the Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA) cut its forecast for 2026 home sales for the third time this year.

Joel Fox, chief operating officer of Toronto-based real estate law platform Ownright, agrees that Wednesday's rate hike will add to the dour mood in the housing market.

"A rate hike likely locks us into year-over-year declines in housing activity for the rest of this year and into next, and I don't see things turning until there's a rate drop," he said in a statement after Wednesday's rate decision.

"The market was already as bleak as we've seen in a long time. The only saving grace is that it's hard to imagine it dropping much further."

World.title: Three face murder charges in death of 12-year-old boy found in rural Alberta
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Three people from Edmonton have been charged in the death of a 12-year-old boy whose remains were found in rural Alberta in August.

The boy has been identified as Fiasal Hussein by police. Cole Morin, 34, and Curtis Brown, 36, have been charged with first-degree murder and kidnapping. Rachel Stuart, 36, has been charged with second-degree murder.

Insp. Wayne Stevenson of the RCMP’s serious crime branch said at a news conference Wednesday in Edmonton that Fiasal "was associated with people involved in criminality" and knew the three accused. Stevenson alleged that Fiasal was lured from his home before being killed.

"He did not deserve that,” said Stevenson. “Whatever challenges or choices may have led to his untimely death, he was still a child with a future ahead of him. This was a cruel and heartbreaking act.”

Stevenson said the investigation began with a 911 call to Athabasca RCMP shortly before 3:30 a.m. on Aug .6. The unknown caller, who police now believe was Fiasal, said he had been kidnapped and was injured.

The call came from the area around Calling Lake, Alta., which is about 200 kilometres north of Edmonton. Spotty reception made it difficult for dispatchers to assess the situation, said Stevenson.

Officers arriving at the scene found a vehicle that had been reported stolen from Edmonton. Stevenson said officers found evidence of an attack, but did not comment on its nature. Hussein’s remains were found at around 9 a.m. during a search of the area. The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner declared the death to be a homicide.

Brown, Morin and Stuart were arrested at residences throughout Edmonton on Oct. 24. All three remain in custody and are scheduled to appear in the Athabasca Court of Justice on Nov. 9.

Police did not elaborate on the relationship between Fiasal and the three accused. They also didn’t provide details on how the boy left his house or how he was killed. Sgt. James McConnell with the RCMP’s major crimes unit said those details are part of the investigation and will be told in court.

“The exact specifics and motive of this homicide are still part of the ongoing investigation,“ said McConnell.

"Parents aren’t supposed to bury their children and that’s what we have in this case.”

World.title: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski addresses jury at his fraud trial for first time, says he's innocent
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski addressed the jury for the first time at his Toronto fraud trial, thanking them, in his brief closing statement Wednesday morning.

"I am the least qualified person here to give a closing statement," Pleterski said in Ontario Superior Court.

"However, that being said, I am innocent of these charges. That is why I pled not guilty. Had I not been forced to represent myself, that would have been proven. That's all I have to say."

Pleterski represented himself at his trial, where he only cross-examined the first of 14 witnesses the Crown called and decided not to call evidence in his defence or to testify himself. When asked by Justice Shaun Nakatsuru whether he had questions for several of the witnesses, he told the court he didn't know what to ask and, in one case, said that he needed a lawyer.

The 27-year-old is accused of fraud over $5,000. At the end of the Crown's case, they dropped a second charge of money laundering against Pleterski. He was charged after a lengthy police investigation in May 2024.

Pleterski was no 'Crypto King': Crown

Before Pleterski addressed the court, Crown prosecutor Akshay Aurora gave his roughly 90-minute closing statement.

"Mr. Pleterski was no 'Crypto King.' Far from it. As it turns out he was no king at all. He was a thief. A thief who stole investor money and used it as he pleased. A thief who stole investor money using calculated lies," Aurora told the jury.

"As you've seen, he burned through that money … he lived his best life, all while his investors pleaded for updates on their money, only to be ignored."

Crown prosecutor Akshay Aurora is shown in this court sketch delivered a roughly 90-minute closing statement at Pleterski's fraud trial on Wednesday. (Pam Davies/CBC)

Aurora provided an overview of the Crown's evidence in his closing statement, emphasizing that none of the investors' funds went into the trading platform, FXChoice, on their investment contracts. Instead, the prosecutor said Pleterski used it to pay back other investors, buy cars, fly on private jets and rack up credit card bills.

"The truth, members of the jury, are in the numbers, and the numbers do not lie," Aurora said.

"The numbers tell us Mr. Pleterski used investor money as if it was his own to fund his lavish lifestyle."

Earlier in Pleterski's trial, a senior forensic accountant who reviewed his financial records testified that investors provided Pleterski with more than $36.3 million and none of those funds were ever sent to FXChoice.

Instead, Albert Ciorma from the Ontario Securities Commission said his forensic audit found Pleterski spent about $5.6 million on luxury vehicles, $4.9 million on credit card bills, $870,000 on travel and private jets and $598,000 on security.

WATCH | Court hears audio recording of self-described 'Crypto King': 'Crypto King' admits $300M account never existed in audio recording played at trial | Duration closed caption 2:24 The Crown closed its case by playing a three-hour audio recording of a meeting between the accused Aiden Pleterski, a lawyer and three investors. The jury heard from a retired police officer who was present at the meeting and gave Pleterski $450,000 to invest.

Pleterski also gave nearly $3.7 million to his parents and took $609,000 in cash advances from a credit card, Ciorma said.

Altogether, those expenses total more than $16.3 million. Pleterski also paid out another $16.1 million to investors from the funds he received, according to Ciorma.

Investor paid back own money

In his closing, Aurora walked jurors through some of the financial summaries Ciorma created of Pleterski's accounts as they related to about half of the dozen investors who testified at trial.

In one case, the Crown showed how investor and witness Sacha Singh provided Pleterski with $1.3 million to invest, how that money made up almost all the funds in the account and that Singh was later paid back $700,000 of his own money from the same account.

Sacha Singh testified remotely by Zoom at Pleterski fraud trial on Oct. 14. (Pam Davies/CBC)

The prosecutor's examples also showed hundreds of thousands of dollars of investor funds being deposited in Pleterski's various accounts, only to be quickly withdrawn to pay other investors, credit card bills and go toward cars and a luxury home.

"None of the money went to MyFXChoice. You've seen it. Each time, Mr. Pleterski just uses the money as if it was his own," said Aurora in reference to these accounts.

Pleterski's investments were all failures

The Crown's closing also highlighted details on Pleterski's limited trading in cryptocurrency and foreign exchange over the course of the alleged fraud between July 2020 and July 2022.

"Every single investment account of Mr. Pleterski's is a failure and only generates losses," said Aurora. "$4,000 is all that comes into his account from any form of cryptocurrency or foreign exchange source."

Over the course of the trial, the jury heard about a purported $311 million fund in a FXChoice account — and how Pleterski provided screenshots and a video of it to concerned investors worried about their money in the spring of 2022.

Earlier this month, the jury in Pleterski's trial was shown this photo of Mitchell Learning holding his own phone with a screenshot the investor testified Pleterski sent him of Pleterski's trading account with a balance of more than $311 million. (Ontario Superior Court of Justice)

It came up in the testimony of several witnesses, alongside the screenshots and videos. Including one of Pleterski's email account, showing the FXChoice account where the money was supposed to be, had been deleted. The jury also heard an audio recording of a meeting with investors where Pleterski admitted the $311 million fund never existed.

'Every dollar was a decision he made'

"Who would delete a $300 million account? You wouldn't even delete a $300 account. It's clear that Mr. Pleterski was deleting that account because his 'investment scheme' was going to be unravelled … that it was going to be exposed," said Aurora in his closing statement.

"At no point, no point in the history of this account, was there $300 million, not even close. The highest this account was at was at $12,000."

The Crown also emphasized Pleterski knew he was deceiving investors from the beginning.

Pleterski, seen here outside the Toronto courthouse where he's standing trial, told the jury Thursday that he's innocent. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

"Mr. Pleterski was the architect of this scheme. He controlled everything," Aurora told the jury.

"Every dollar spent was a decision he made. He was the architect. It would be impossible to say he did not know what he was doing."

As a result, the prosecutor told the jury Pleterski is guilty of fraud over $5,000.

Nakatsuru gave the majority of his instructions to the jury Wednesday.

The judge told the jury he would finish addressing them Thursday morning and then the jury will begin their deliberations.

World.title: Personal data of 40,000 U.S. Homeland Security employees leaked in security breach
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on ‌Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.

DHS said in a statement it was "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively." The agency said it was working to ensure its employees ​were properly protected and would update the public "when more information is ​available.”

The disclosure — which the non-profit data transparency group says draws on information obtained by an entity calling itself "Department of Peace" — is the third major government data leak to have made headlines in the past month.

In ​September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal ⁠Bureau of Investigation (FBI), including sensitive job ⁠details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, ‌the U.S. War Department was hit with a class-action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.

The DHS data includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and other DHS component agencies.

Also included in ⁠the data were job titles and email groups, which, among other details, showed which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work.

WATCH | Canadian arrested in FBI data breach case: Canadian ransomware negotiator arrested in connection to FBI hacking case | Duration closed caption 1:57 Edward Dubrovsky, a Canadian cybersecurity executive who negotiates with ransomware hackers has been arrested in Pennsylvania as authorities investigate a hacking group that claims to have stolen FBI employee information.

In a statement, Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder Emma Best said the hacktivist known as "maia arson crimew" developed a search tool for ‌the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would "replace anonymity with accountability" and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight.

The Department of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data it said that DHS employees "have our information, so it's only fair that ​we have theirs" and that it hoped the data "can be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction."

The Department of Peace in ⁠March claimed responsibility for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors.

Best's statement said the Department of Peace harvested ⁠the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to ⁠a Reuters ⁠query: "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our ​data or systems were compromised."

WATCH | What to do if you get hacked: Caught in a data breach? 3 tips for what to do next | Duration closed caption 1:18 Cybersecurity expert Robert Falzon, Canadian head of engineering at Check Point Software Technologies, shares his top three tips of what students and staff impacted by the Canvas cyber incident should be doing next.

Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the entire data trove but it was able to match ​personal information about six DHS employees named ⁠in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data carried by the dark web intelligence platform District 4 Labs. Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach.

In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees' LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed non-public data about internal DHS ⁠organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or ‌operations.

World.title: Colombia’s opposition announces criminal charges against De la Espriella over ties to drug traffickers
World.content:
Colombia’s opposition leader, senator Ian Cepeda, accused President Abelardo de la Espriella of leading an agrarian counter-reform designed to benefit land-owning clans and convicted drug traffickers.

During a congressional debate, Cepeda claimed that De la Espriella put allies of drug traffickers and paramilitaries in charge of key state institutions responsible for land distribution and asset forfeiture.

The president and his appointees are part of a revolving door system of people who, before being appointed to government positions, defended the interests of drug traffickers and paramilitaries associated with De la Espriella and his businesses, according to the opposition leader.

For example, the president put Diana Patrica Bravo, a former prosecutor and partner at his law firm De la Espriella Lawyers, in charge of The Society of Special Assets (SAE), which controls assets that were seized from drug traffickers.

The leader of the leftist Historic Pact party showed financial statements of one of De la Espriella’s companies, Dominio De la Espriella, that would prove that in between 38% and 40% of its capital deposits came from the family and corporate network of Hugues Rodríguez, a.k.a. Comandante Barbie, a former paramilitary financier who was charged with drug trafficking in the US.

The SAE would control more than 130 properties of Comandante Barbie.

De la Espriella family construction firm, Cosenza S.A.S., made property purchases in the city of Monteria directly with individuals under investigation for money laundering and illicit enrichment, according to Cepeda.

The president’s ex-wife, Yoly Beatriz Illidge, was appointed Superintendent of Notaries, making her “directly responsible for inspecting and monitoring all land entries and records issued by restitution judges throughout the country,” according to Cepeda.

De la Espriella is an associate of drug traffickers, owns assets purchased from drug traffickers, and defends drug traffickers from within the national government. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Last but not least, Agriculture Minister Indalecio Dangond “arrived at this post to execute an agrarian counter-reform at the service of paramilitary land-grabbers, foreign capital, and agro-industrial partners” while blocking investments for small farmers and displacement victims, the opposition leader stated.

Cepeda vowed that he would give the dossier to the United States Department of Justcie and to “Congressmen of the Democratic Party, given that mister De la Espriella is a US citizen.”

The opposition leader additionally promised to file criminal charges against the president and his agriculture minister in Colombia.

World.title: Colombia’s government claims Petro exploited 48 women as president
World.content:
The administration chief of Colombia’s President Abelardo De la Espriella told Congress that former President Gustavo Petro hired at least 48 women who were “trapped and exploited” for presidential parties.

During a hearing, DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios claimed that Petro had 48 women “working in the Presidency, who were unfortunately exploited through temporary work contracts.”

We’re going to prove this to the Colombian people: how, unfortunately, the Casa de Nariño was set up, organized, and designed not for governing, but for partying there every day, bringing women there and engaging in behavior we should not be engaging in—behavior that sets a bad example. DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios

“Forty-eight women are already speaking with us about how, through a contract and an OPS, they were trapped and exploited in order to be with President Petro,” said Rios.

Former DAPRE director Angie Rodriguez, who was sacked by Petro in July, doubled down on her successor’s allegations and asked the former president to prove that the president managed a network of women, including child transvestites.

Were there transvestite children there? Answer me, Mr. President. Were there transvestite children there? I am asking you a question, and I have every right to ask it. Were there? And if there weren’t, uh… prove that what I am saying is a lie. Angie Rodriguez

Last but not least, far-right magazine Semana published an interview with a woman identified as Deicy Jimenez, who claimed she as hired by Petro after meeting him on an adult website.

Jimenez even told Semana’s former presidential candidate Vicky Davila she trafficked drugs for the former president when he was senator.

VD: What happened on the day you say you transported drugs for Petro? DJ: Yes, I was traveling, and he asked me as a favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Were you outside of Bogotá? DJ: Yes. VD: How do you recall that favor Petro asked of you? DJ: He asked me as the favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Did you buy them? DJ: Yes, I bought them somewhere. He gave me money. VD: Did he give it to you in cash or deposit it for you? DJ: In cash. VD: How much money? DJ: Three million pesos. VD: What kind of drugs did you buy? DJ: Cocaine. VD: Where did you buy it? DJ: I bought it from some people. I can’t say (publicly) their names or the location. VD: Is it a gang? DJ: Yes. VD: Did he know you were going to buy the drugs from that gang? DJ: Yes. VD: At that time, was he a senator or the president? DJ: A senator. VD: How did you bring that drug in? DJ: I brought it through the airport. VD: You mean, on a plane? DJ: Yeah. VD: Did you get on a plane with Petro’s drugs? DJ: Yes. VD: How were the drugs packaged? DJ: In bags. VD: Like individual doses? DJ: Yes. VD: And where did you hide the drugs? DJ: In my suitcase.

In a response, Petro denied having hired women for sex and claimed that the far-right attack were the result of authorities’ failure to sustain corruption allegations.

World.title: “Brazil and Colombia need each other,” says De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella recognized the election victory of his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Ignacio Lula, who defeated far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday.

In a post on social media platform X, the Colombian President said that “in the Colombian presidential campaign, President Lula openly supported Ivan Cepeda, and I won. In the Brazilian campaign, I supported Bolsonaro, and Lula won.”

“Neither does Lula decide for Colombians, nor do I decide for Brazilians. THE PEOPLE DECIDE! And when the people speak at the polls, their will is respected because it is sacred,” the president added.

Lula and I have major and profound political and ideological differences, but we agree on one fundamental point: Brazil and Colombia need each other. No other consideration can take precedence over the interests of our nations. Colombia and Brazil are sister nations, facing enormous shared challenges and opportunities.

President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella stressed that “we have much to do and much work to carry out for the benefit of our peoples” an ought to “fight against narco-terrorism and illegal mining, the protection of the Amazon, and the well-being of our citizens.”

Lula was the first leftist candidate and critic of US President Donald Trump to win an election, triggering celebrations among leftists throughout the continent.

De la Espriella, a US citizen, has been among the most fanatic among Trump supporter in trying to align his domestic policies to US foreign policy.

World.title: De la Espriella sacks interior minister after Congress bungles Colombia’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia President Abelardo de la Espriella sacked Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara hours after Congress found a procedural flaw in the passed 2027 budget, which makes the law invalid.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella briefly thanked Lara and announced he would be replaced by the ambassador to the Organization of American States, Alejandro Ordoñez.

The news surprised the interior minister, who suddenly left a congressional debate on a law to facilitate the demobilization of illegal armed groups after receiving a message on his phone.

Lara was apparently held responsible for the blunder of Congress, whose two houses approved the 2027 budget but with conflicting versions of an article on financial risk-coverage mechanisms for the Ministry of Finance.

By the time the error was detected, the budget debate had passed its October 20 deadline, forcing De la Espriella to issue a decree that would convert an older version of the budget bill into law.

The interior minister was the administration’s primary political liaison responsible for managing legislative procedure and whip operations in Congress.

Lara’s job was already under pressure after he failed to convince Congress to cede its presidency to the president’s candidate.

While Ordoñez returns from Washington, Justice Minister Ivan Cancino will assume the role of interior minister.

The incoming interior minister is an ultra conservative Catholic with ties to the Society of St. Pius X, which considers the modernizing reforms of the Catholic Church heresies and errors, and was declared in a schism with the church in June.

In Colombian politics and particularly among the opposition, Ordoñez is mainly remembered as the inspector general who illegally removed former President Gustavo Petro from his post as mayor of Bogota in 2013.

Petro was ultimately reinstated and would become president of the country in 2022.

World.title: Colombia’s Congress approves De la Espriella’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia’s Congress agreed to increase the government’s 2027 budget despite promises by President Abelardo de la Espriella to reduce public spending.

Next year’s budget will be COP634.9 trillion, almost $204 billion, which is 16% more than last year’s budget and 10% higher than the proposal made by former President Gustavo Petro.

According to Finance Minister Miguel Gomez, the budget seeks to bring the State’s finances in line with reality.

The budget was approved in both the Senate and the House of Representatives with the support of De la Espriella’s government coalition.

The Historic Pact, the only leftist opposition party, rejected the budget and boycotted the vote.

On behalf of the national government, I would like to thank you all for your work over the past few months in passing the budget. I would also like to thank the opposition for the strength with which they defended their views. The message that Congress has sent today regarding the government’s economic policy is very important. It is the first step toward putting the country’s economy back on track toward growth, fiscal responsibility, and addressing the nation’s needs. Finance Minister Miguel Gomez

The budget seeks to reimpose the neoliberal model that had been abandoned by Petro and reduce public debt.

According to Green Party representative Jaime Raul Salamanca, who opposed the budget, funding for free higher education was cut in half from COP800 billion ($254 million) to COP400 billion (127 million).

“This cut raises concerns about its potential impact on the continuity and scope of this policy, which has enabled thousands of young people to enroll in public institutions of higher education,” said Salamanca.

The budget also cut the budget for the war crimes tribunal JEP, which could endanger the future of the peace process with the FARC and is opposed by the government.

World.title: De la Espriella announces “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism”
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella announced an “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism” as part of his “cultural counterrevolution.”

During a visit to the Culture Ministry, De la Espriella described wokeism as “an ideological paradigm that aims to transform moral, cultural, and social foundations in the West, perverting values, family tradition, and national identity.”

According to the president, Culture Minister Paola Holguin was a general in the “cultural counterrevolution.”

Culture has an enormous capacity to shape society, and that is why the State has a moral, inescapable, and political duty to prevent cultural spaces from being taken over by social communism, which is atheist and an enemy to the fundamental values upon which the nation of Colombia is built. This is where that cultural counterrevolution will begin. President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella said that Holguin, the daughter of a reported money launderer, would lead the “Culture War” against the “extreme left,” which has “permeated all parts of society, particularly the cultural and academic spheres.”

I want to be clear about this: we are going to wage an open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism, which is nothing more than an ideological movement that aims to transform the moral, cultural, and social foundations of the West, corrupting values, family tradition, and national identity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Earlier in the day, the National Museum removed all references to members of the exterminated Patriotic Union party, slain guerrilla leader and presidential candidate Carlos Pizarro, and the struggle for the rights of Colombia’s LGBT+ community.

References to Colombia’s former guerrilla movements was “terrorism apology, which is “exactly what we have come to confront” in an attempt to “recover pride for Colombian culture.”

Atheists, the Pizarro family and gay rights activists rejected the president’s attempts to remove them from mainstream culture.

World.title: Colombia’s first lady promises transparency over earthquake donations
World.content:
Colombia’s first lady, Ana Lucia Pineda, vowed to reveal how much money she collected and spent in response to the August 10 earthquake that affected hundreds of thousands of people.

Amid mounting public pressure about where the money had gone, Pineda went on the morning program of public television channel Nuestro Caribe to promise that her foundation, Luz y Sonrisas, will take its finances public on Friday.

Carrying a white folder, the wife of President Abelardo de la Espriella stressed that “in the foundation’s accounts rest all, absolutely all of the monies from the donations we received during the ‘Colombia One Single Heart’ campaign” that was announced on August 12.

“A lie is not going to tear down the truth of who I am or what I represent, or how my children recognize me,” said Pineda.

Luz y Sonrisas was one of three NGO’s that were promoted by the De la Espriella government to collect contributions for victims of the earthquake.

Pineda’s foundation was the only one that could receive contributions from abroad.

Earlier in the week, news program Noticias Uno revealed that her foundation that was founded on July 7 lacked the tax exemption that would allow it to accept donations, a process that usually takes months.

In a press statement, tax office DIAN subsequently said that it had granted the tax exemption to the first lady and that she could legally accept financial contributions.

Pineda did not say how much money she had received, but said that she stopped supporting the initial relief efforts “because the humanitarian aid was sufficient, it was huge.”

The first lady vowed she had saved the donations for the reconstruction phase “because I have also taken the initiative to build and return to the victims a house that is durable for the families who lost everything.”

World.title: Colombia’s opposition takes to the street to protest De la Espriella
World.content:
Despite intimidation attempts by the national government and the police, tens of thousands of people took to the streets throughout Colombia to protest the far-right government of President Abelardo De la Espriella.

The protest had been organized by social organizations, labor unions and the country’s largest opposition party, the Historic Pact.

Opposition leader Ivan Cepeda, who joined the protests in Bogota, told a reporter that the government is “exercising a mafia-style rule in the service of the worst elements of Colombian politics—the drug trade.”

Contrary to what De la Espriella is saying, this is not a government that opposes drug trafficking; it is a government that supports the drug trafficking cartels, the paramilitaries, and the ultra-conservative forces that want to destroy people’s rights, the democratic advances made by President Gustavo Petro, and the progress achieved by the popular movement over the past four years. Senator Ivan Cepeda

“That’s why we’re here; we won’t allow people’s rights to be violated or trampled upon,” said the senator.

Hours ahead of the protest, the president signed off on a decree that changed the police response to protests and accused the organizers of being “instigators of evil” who “seek to once again cause chaos.”

Human rights organizations denounced that the security forces put snipers on the roofs of buildings in Bogota and in Cali, a helicopter flew over the heads of the protesters.

The protests sought to test the waters for an even larger “national strike” that is set for November and shut down parts of the country in 2021.

“We are only warming up,” warned Cepeda, who has yet to recognize De la Espriella as Colombia’s legitimate president after losing the elections in July.

World.title: Falklands approves bill on oil pollution emergencies in relation to offshore installations, and responsibilities
World.content:
Falklands approves bill on oil pollution emergencies in relation to offshore installations, and responsibilities

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 15:10 UTC Full article

The Director of Mineral Resources will be the competent authority – “Falkland Islands contingency plan” and “offshore installations” used in the OPRC Regulations.

The Falkland Islands Executive Council has approved a set of Regulations 2026 to amend the Maritime (Oil Pollution Preparedness, Response and Co-operation Convention) Regulations 2019 (“the OPRC Regulations”) to make provision for the preparation and maintenance of oil pollution emergency plans in relation to offshore installations and to require the persons responsible for offshore installations to report oil incidents where oil is discharged into the sea.

Regulations 1 and 2 provide for the title and commencement of the Regulations. Regulation 3 provides that these Regulations amend the OPRC Regulations and the following regulations provide for specific amendments to be made to those Regulations.

Regulation 4 amends regulation 3 of the OPRC Regulations, which sets out the objects of those Regulations, to include making provision for the preparation and maintenance of oil pollution emergency plans in relation to offshore installations.

Regulation 5 amends regulation 4 of the OPRC Regulations which contains definitions of words and phrases used in those Regulations. It adds new definitions for words and phrases used in the 17 amended provisions and replaces the definitions of “competent authority” – with the effect that in relation to ships, ports, harbours and oil handling facilities the Falkland Islands Maritime Authority (FIMA) is the competent authority, but in relation to offshore installations, the Director of Mineral Resources will be the competent authority – “Falkland Islands contingency plan” and “offshore installations” used in the OPRC Regulations.

Regulation 6 amends regulation 6 of the OPRC Regulations which is the application provision, to provide that the OPRC Regulations will apply to offshore installations.

Regulation 7 amends regulation 14 of the OPRC Regulations to require an operator of an oil handling facility to ensure that no activities that pose a risk of an oil pollution incident are undertaken unless the facility has an oil pollution emergency plan approved by the authority.

Regulation 8 inserts a new Part 3A into the OPRC Regulations which makes specific provision for the preparation and maintenance of oil pollution emergency plans in relation to offshore installations.

New regulation 15A requires the responsible person for an offshore installation to prepare and maintain an oil pollution emergency plan for each offshore installation for which they are responsible, although the Director of Mineral Resources may permit joint plans in specified circumstances.

New regulation 15B requires the person preparing an oil pollution emergency plan for an offshore installation to take into account guidance issued by the Director of Mineral Resources and for the plan to comply with the requirements contained in the new Schedule to the OPRC Regulations, which is inserted by regulation 13.

New regulation 15C sets out the procedure for the submission of an oil pollution emergency plan for an offshore installation to the Director of Mineral Resources for approval and the dates by which an application must be submitted.

New regulation 15D provides that an approved oil pollution emergency plan must be reviewed every five years or before then if specified events occur. The Director of Mineral Resources may require an oil pollution emergency plan to be reviewed at any time.

New regulation 15E sets out the consequences if a responsible person for an offshore installation fails to review, submit or amend an oil pollution emergency plan. These are that an oil pollution emergency plan ceases to be approved for an offshore installation and, as a result of new regulation 15G(1), this will mean that no oil or gas operations can be carried out.

New regulation 15F gives the Director of Mineral Resources power to direct, after consultation with a responsible person, that an oil pollution emergency plan be amended if it is not compatible with the Falkland Islands contingency plan or is not appropriate for dealing with oil pollution incidents in the area of the offshore installation.

New regulation 15G sets out the duties imposed on a responsible person for an offshore installation. These include: ensuring that no oil or gas operations are carried out unless the offshore installation is subject to an oil pollution emergency plan approved by the Director of Mineral Resources; maintaining relevant equipment; and undertaking exercises. In the event of an oil pollution incident, the oil pollution emergency plan must be implemented (new regulation 15G(3)).

New regulation 15H imposes duties on the licensee (defined as a person to whom a licence has been granted by the Governor under section 6 of the Offshore Minerals Ordinance 1994) to ensure that where it appoints responsible persons, those persons are capable of satisfactorily carrying out 18 the functions and discharging their duties and that they have access to adequate financial resources to discharge their duties.

New regulation 15I requires a responsible person for an offshore installation who observes or is made aware of any event involving a discharge of oil, or probable discharge of oil, or the presence of oil in the sea to report it to the Director of Mineral Resources. Regulation 9 amends regulation 17 of the OPRC Regulations to set out the steps FIMA and the Director of Mineral Resources must take in response to a report of a discharge etc of oil.

Regulation 10 amends regulation 18 of the OPRC Regulations to now contain provision for the inspection of ships, harbours, ports, oil handling facilities and offshore installations and the powers under which the respective inspectors may operate.

Regulation 11 amends regulation 19 of the OPRC Regulations to introduce offences where a person fails to comply with or perform duties introduced by these Regulations.

Regulation 12 introduces a new regulation 20 in the OPRC Regulations which empowers the Director of Mineral Resources, FIMA and Governor to share information obtained for the purposes of the OPRC Regulations with other agencies.

Regulation 13 inserts a Schedule in the OPRC Regulations that sets out the requirements for an oil pollution emergency plan in respect of offshore installations.

Regulation 14 makes transitional provision. Published by the Attorney General’s Chambers, Stanley, Falkland Islands
