World.title: How do the US midterms work, and why are they so important for Trump's presidency?
World.content:
US voters are electing a new Congress. The results will be decisive for the future of the United States, and a judgment on Donald Trump's second term as president.

On November 3, United States citizens will vote in the midterm elections. These won't decide who gets to sit in the White House; instead, Americans will be voting on who they want to see in the Capitol.

Midterm elections are held every four years, at the exact halfway point between presidential elections. The people of the United States decide who will represent them in the two chambers of the US Congress, the House of Representatives and the Senate. Some states are also voting for their governor. These are the decisions on the ballot paper — but they are not the only thing voters will be taking into account.

J. Miles Coleman, an election analyst at the Center for Politics at the University of Virginia, explained before the last midterms that they were "often a referendum on the president and party currently in power." If the people are content, the party of the leader in the White House does better than if the people are predominantly dissatisfied. President Donald Trump's approval ratings are currently at a record low.

President Donald Trump's approval ratings have sunk to an all-time low: More than 60% of Americans view him negatively Image: Jacquelyn Martin/AP Photo/picture alliance

Who are Americans electing in the midterms?

All the seats in the US House of Representatives are up for election. Its 435 members are elected by eligible voters across the country. Each member represents one electoral district. These are allocated based on population size. As a result, relatively large US states where few people live, such as Wyoming, have only one seat in the House of Representatives. New Jersey, a much smaller state by surface area but with a larger population, has 12. Representatives are elected for a two-year term of office.

US senators, on the other hand, are elected for a six-year term. The Senate, the other chamber of the US Congress, has 100 seats: two for each of the 50 US states, regardless of size. Around one third of these senatorial seats come up for election every two years. This year there are 35, meaning that not every state will be electing a senator in these midterms.

Separately, voters in 36 states will elect their governor, whose term of office is four years in most states. Many decisions in the US are taken at state level, on everything from abortion law to education and electoral procedure. It can therefore make a considerable difference to people's lives whether Democrats or Republicans are the ones making these decisions in their state.

Who currently has a majority in the US Congress?

At present, the Republicans, the party of President Trump, have a majority in both houses of Congress — but its margin is slim.

The House of Representatives currently has 218 Republican deputies, 214 Democrats, and one independent, who usually votes with the Republicans. Two seats are vacant. Observers think it likely that the Democrats will seize the majority in this chamber in the upcoming elections. "It would be a surprise if the Democrats don't at least take the House [of Representatives]," Coleman told the American broadcaster CBS at the end of October.

In the Senate there are currently 53 Republicans, 45 Democrats, and two independent senators who usually vote with the Democrats. When a vote in the Senate is deadlocked 50:50, the US vice president has the deciding vote. This means that currently, Trump's Vice President JD Vance would tip the scales if there were a tie in a Senate vote.

Republicans and Democrats are vying for seats in the two chambers of the US Congress Image: Graeme Sloan/Sipa USA/picture alliance

Why are the midterms so important?

Voter turnout is typically lower for midterms than for presidential elections, but the results will decisively influence US politics for the next few years. Despite the significant executive power delegated to the presidency, the majority of federal political decisions have to be approved by Congress before they can be implemented.

It is therefore considerably easier for Trump to govern the country as he chooses if the Republicans have a majority in both chambers of Congress. If the Democrats win a majority in one or both chambers, it will be more difficult for him to make changes to either domestic or foreign policy.

Which races are crucial?

The Democrats only need to win four more seats in the House of Representatives to gain a majority. They would then have 218 representatives. Out of the 435 races, only a few are still considered toss-ups. These include districts in Iowa, Virginia and Montana.

One senatorial race to watch is the one in Texas. Current polls put Democrat James Talarico level with his Republican rival, Ken Paxton. The Democrats need four more seats in the Senate to win a majority. The possibility that Texas could be one of them is already a sensation. No Democrat has won here at state level since 1994. Talarico now even has the support of some members of the Bush family, the Texas Republican dynasty of former presidents George H.W. Bush and George W. Bush, his son.

Many US voters are undecided, disillusioned or disengaged To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In the gubernatorial elections it is possible that, for the first time in US history, a Black woman could become state governor. In Minnesota, the Democrat Amy Klobuchar and the Black Republican Lisa DeMuth are vying for the position, while in Georgia the Black Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms is up against the Republican Rick Jackson.

DeMuth is unlikely to win in Minnesota: The state generally votes Democrat, and Klobuchar, who has been state senator there for almost two decades, is much better known than her rival. In Georgia, however, the latest polls suggest it's neck-and-neck. Bottoms has a realistic chance of winning.

This article has been translated from German.

World.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
World.content:
A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

Since a ceasefire took effect in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region on October 27, preparations have been underway to evacuate residents trapped there.

Following Russia's occupation of the town in 2022 and the flooding caused by the destruction of the nearby Kakhovka dam in 2023, residents were cut off from the outside world. All access routes to Oleshky, which lies on the Dnipro River, had been mined. Former Oleshky residents who managed to escape and talked to DW described hunger, no access to medicine, and no electricity or water. About 2,000 people are still living in the town.

According to the Save Ukraine Foundation, it has rescued at least 300 civilians from Oleshky over the past six months. DW spoke with lawyer Myroslava Kharchenko, who works for the organization, about preparations for the upcoming evacuation.

DW: A ceasefire is already in effect in Oleshky. Do you know whether any evacuation efforts have begun?

Myroslava Kharchenko: No, we do not have that information yet. What we do know is that the ceasefire came into effect on October 27 at 3 a.m. Kyiv time, which is 4 a.m. in Russia. Mine-clearing operations on the road began at around 8 a.m. What is happening inside Oleshky itself, however, is entirely within the military's remit. Everyone involved in this operation has been asked to maintain strict confidentiality. Any careless remark or action could jeopardize the entire evacuation effort.

What I can see is that information is being actively collected through closed internal local chat groups. Registration lists and application forms are being shared, and people are filling them out themselves. Organizers are contacting those who previously requested evacuation to verify details such as their date of birth and current place of residence. They are also asking people to provide contact information for neighbors or relatives who may be nearby or in the same building, because communications are extremely unreliable.

The organizers are also collecting information about the health conditions of those planning to leave. Among them are people who are ill, have limited mobility, or are recovering from recent injuries, including blast and mine-related wounds. We therefore expect those organizing the evacuation to ensure that medical assistance is available for those who need it.

How exactly is the evacuation expected to take place? Will people be evacuated through Russian-controlled territory or via the Dnipro River? Have any routes already been agreed upon?

As far as we know, a river route would be extremely dangerous. We have not heard any confirmation that such an option has been approved. It therefore appears likely that the evacuation route will pass through the temporarily occupied Ukrainian territory and possibly through Russia before people are able to reach Ukraine. For security reasons, however, none of these details are being made public.

What do you know about the number of people expected to be evacuated?

We are actually very pleased that the evacuation is not expected to take place in a single day. That is important because we hope that those who manage to leave safely during the first stage will serve as an example for others.

People still trapped in Oleshky are extremely afraid. There have already been numerous provocations, and this is not the first attempt to establish such a route or humanitarian corridor.

As a result, there is a great deal of suspicion. Those concerns are based largely on uncertainty, and some people may choose not to leave during the initial phase of the evacuation. Overall, however, we estimate that around 500 people may eventually be evacuated.

Oleshky ceasefire comes into effect in Ukraine war To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

How would you assess the role of Melania Trump in making this evacuation possible?

We are immensely grateful to Melania Trump for drawing attention to the humanitarian catastrophe currently unfolding in Oleshky. What is taking place there is in fact genocide committed by the Russian Federation.

We are thankful for her efforts and hope they will help make this evacuation possible. We will be even more grateful once most people are safely removed from the combat zone and arrive in Ukrainian government-controlled territory.

Myroslava Kharchenko from the Save Ukraine Foundation Image: DW Novosti

When could the physical evacuation of civilians begin?

I can't say how long it will take. What seems clear, however, is that time will be needed to clear mines from the roads leading into the city. We also understand that many streets inside Oleshky are mined, so additional work will be required to make routes within the city safe.

There is a hospital from which people need to be evacuated. Nearby is a morgue where bodies also need to be recovered.

I do not know whether that will be included as part of this humanitarian corridor, but it is undoubtedly important. The bodies need to be identified and the causes of death established. That process will also take time, regardless of how quickly the military is able to work.

It is difficult to make any predictions because, as you can see, everything is being conducted under strict secrecy. Statements from both the Russian and Ukrainian sides have been extremely cautious, and that is clearly justified under the circumstances.

World.title: One year on, families seek justice after election violence
World.content:
One year after Tanzania's deadly post-election violence, families are still seeking answers. A government inquiry recorded 518 deaths. DW research has documented apparent use of excessive force by security forces.

Warning: This article contains descriptions of violence.

For one family member in Mwanza, Tanzania's second-largest city, justice could begin with a simple act: an apology.

Raha, whose name has been changed for safety reasons, said her nephew, who she raised, was killed during protests that erupted following Tanzania's October 2025 general election.

"The government should have asked for forgiveness for what happened. Even just offering condolences," Raha said.

A year later, the family is still waiting for answers about the death of their loved one.

A disputed election, a deadly crackdown

The violence followed an election campaign marked by the exclusion of the main opposition candidate.

Tundu Lissu, leader of the opposition Tanzanian Party for Democracy and Progress, commonly known as Chadema, had been arrested and charged with treason in April 2025 and his party barred from contesting the election.

A polling station is set ablaze as clashes erupt in Dar es Salaam on October 29, 2025 Image: AFP

On election day and in the days that followed, protesters called for political reforms and the resignation of Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan.

A government-appointed commission, chaired by retired Chief Justice Mohamed Chande Othman and commonly referred to as the Chande Commission, found that at least 518 people died from "unnatural causes," many from gunshot wounds, and over 2,000 people were injured.



Othman said the death toll could be higher because some families buried their loved ones without taking their bodies to morgues or reporting to the commission.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) also said the actual number of people killed could be higher .

"It's very clear that it's far more than the 518 people that were presented by the commission," said Oryem Nyeko, HRW's senior Africa researcher.

Police likely acted beyond their guidelines

DW analyzed dozens of videos, interviewed sources, reviewed police guidelines and advocacy research, and obtained a leaked police report.

We could not determine the exact location or publication date of every video, as some of the footage was released later due to internet blackouts or anonymously, for fear of reprisals. However, elements in the footage, our sources, public reports, and an internal police report give strong indications that these videos do reveal pieces of what happened in the days following the election.

The evidence DW has reviewed indicates that police likely acted beyond the scope of their guidelines and training. The material reviewed by DW included cases in which people were killed who were not protesting, where protesters were killed by head wounds, and where protesters were beaten or degraded by people in uniform.

The police's specialized Field Force Unit, identifiable in some footage by its red berets and riot-control equipment, helmets, shields and heavy weapons, appeared repeatedly in the material reviewed by DW.

Separately, the Centre for Information Resilience, an open-source investigation organization, documented incidents in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania's biggest city and commercial capital. In one, the uniformed people are beating civilians with sticks. In another, they are located close to where protesters were shot and killed.



DW also identified incidents in which people who were not protesting appear to have been killed. In Mwanza, videos showed the bodies of young men reportedly killed by people in police uniforms while watching television in a video hall. The case was also cited by Human Rights Watch and flagged by the Chande Commission for further investigation.

Who was responsible?

Tanzania's police guidelines restrict the use of firearms to circumstances where they are absolutely necessary. Yet investigations by DW and human rights organizations documented incidents involving protesters with apparent gunshot wounds to the head and upper body and non-protesters shot while trying to flee or while outside during a government-imposed curfew.

Security analyst Nicodemus Minde said the commission left crucial questions unanswered.

"The Commission did not really tell us who was responsible and why," he said.

The presence of a police unit at an incident does not establish who ordered an operation or whether senior officials authorized unlawful force.

The Tanzanian President has described the unrest as an attempt to overthrow the government.

Police violence reports emerge after Tanzania election row To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

DW confronted the Tanzanian government on the allegations of excessive force by police. The Tanzanian Ministry of Home Affairs declined to comment, saying it would interfere with the legal process.

DW also asked the Tanzanian police for comment. No response had been received by the time of publication.

The Chande Commission recommended further investigation but did not identify security bodies, individual officers or commanders who may have been responsible.

A second inquiry, chaired by retired Justice Shaban Ally Lila, began gathering evidence in August 2026 to further investigate. Its findings are still pending.

'There is no justice'

For the family members of those killed, the inquiries have yet to restore trust.

Zuri, whose name has been changed for safety reasons, said her brother and her son were killed in the post-election violence. She asked why the government had not visited affected families.

"We lost our children; we lost our brothers. Why hasn't the government taken any initiative to at least visit us?" Zuri asked.

"They behave as if nothing happened. Is this justice? There is no justice in Tanzania."

World.title: What would a new Israeli government mean for Arab neighbors? More of the same is expected, with some small positives predicted.
World.content:
A new Israeli government is unlikely to bring big changes on controversial topics like Palestinian statehood and Israeli troops in Lebanon and Syria, experts say. Some small positives may be possible though.

As Israeli politicians begin to try to build a coalition government, after an election that saw no clear winner, response from politicians in surrounding Arab countries has been muted or non-existent.

This may be because, for the time being anyway, it remains unclear as to whether the new Israeli government will continue with "business as usual" under incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or whether a new government headed by Netanyahu's opponents will take what is expected to be a more moderate domestic course.

Whatever the eventual outcome, the consensus is that there is unlikely to be a huge change in Israel's foreign relations with neighboring countries like Syria, Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt, and, further afield, the Gulf states. Nor is it likely to produce very different policies toward Palestinians, which many Arab populations in the region feel strongly about.

Netanyahu opponent Gadi Eisenkot (pictured), head of the Yashar party, appears to have achieved 16% of the vote. But he will need to build a coalition in order to govern Image: Shir Torem/REUTERS

Both Netanyahu and his main opponent Gadi Eisenkot "are two sides of the same coin," Egyptian politician Mostafa Bakry wrote on X after exit polls seemed to indicate an Eisenkot victory (something that's increasingly contested) and Israeli-Arab parties had displaced Netanyahu's far-right allies. "Arab joy at Netanyahu's near-failure to form the government does not mean that what is to come … differs greatly from his predecessor."

"An Eisenkot government would likely be politically fragile, limiting its room for maneuver," Beth Oppenheim, a policy fellow in the Middle East and North Africa program at the European Council on Foreign Relations, wrote in a commentary last week . "The biggest differences from the current government would be at home: It would halt the judicial overhaul, open a state commission of inquiry into October 7th and pass a conscription law."

However, Oppenheim explained, "when it comes to foreign policy, there would not be a fundamental transformation. Netanyahu's post-October 7th security doctrine — pre-empting threats, operating far beyond Israel's borders and holding 'buffer zones' in neighboring territories — has been embraced by nearly all Jewish Israeli parties."

Palestinian Territories: No two-state solution

One of the election campaign posters for Netanyahu's Likud party bore a stark message — "The right or Palestine" — the message being that if voters did not choose Netanyahu and his right-wing allies, his opponents would be too accommodating toward Israel's Arab-led political parties and would be open to the establishment of a Palestinian state.

But observers believe that message is exaggerated, and that the two-state solution is already dead.

"Support for Palestinian statehood has collapsed across most of the Jewish political spectrum, and permanent Israeli control over Palestinians has become normalized," Oppenheim pointed out . With the exception of one party, "all mainstream Jewish parties support, or at least acquiesce in, the settlement enterprise in some form and publicly oppose a Palestinian state on the 1967 lines."

A Likud campaign banner that reads: "The right or Palestine" Image: Jewel Samad/AFP

In August this year, Eisenkot himself said that, "there is no Palestinian state, and no Palestinian state will be established under the government we form."

An Eisenkot-led government would, however, cooperate with more left-wing Israeli parties, which have previously supported a two-state solution. Any new coalition may also need the backing of Israel's Arab-led parties, who are currently thought to have increased their seats in parliament to around 19.

But as Mairav Zonszein, senior Israel analyst at the International Crisis Group, told the news agency Associated Press this week , "At best, [a new government] would be able to slow down the extremely crazy acceleration that we've seen in the last four years of every aspect of Israel's aggression in the occupied territories and inside Israel itself."

A less extreme government would tone down religious messaging, might be less demanding when it came to conditions on disarming Hamas in Gaza, and could potentially move forward with the next stage of the Gaza ceasefire, agreed to in late 2025, but barely implemented. It might also do more to contain settler violence in the West Bank.

A 2025 survey found that around 82% of Israeli Jews support expelling Palestinains from Gaza (pictured) and around 56% believe Arab citizens of Israel should be expelled Image: Bashar Taleb/AFP

"That's because [settler extremism] is a phenomenon that doesn't enjoy the support of the majority of Israelis, damages Israel's international reputation, and suppressing it is feasible," Elizabeth Tsurkov, a senior fellow at the Washington-based think tank, the Middle East Policy Council, explained on social media .

"[A new Israeli government] would keep expanding the settlements and Palestinian statehood would remain taboo," Oppenheim wrote. "Without a diplomatic track with the Palestinians, further flare-ups of violence in the West Bank and Gaza are inevitable, destabilizing the region — and normalization with Saudi Arabia will remain off the table."

Saudi Arabia: Could anti-Netanyahu bloc bring normalization?

After the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel by Hamas and Israel's ensuing military campaign, which has resulted in at least 70,000 Palestinians killed and Gaza devastated, Saudi Arabia's conditions for normalization with Israel have hardened.

The country, hugely influential in the Muslim world, has put out several statements saying there could be no path to normalizing relations with Israel without some progress on Palestinian statehood.

Last week, at a meeting of foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkey and Egypt, the Saudis co-signed a communique in which the four countries said Israel was "the fundamental source of instability in the region and beyond."

Video still from a Houthi attack on a Saudi airport in October, 2026. The Saudi government has reportedly rejected Israeli offers of help to fight Yemen's Houthi militia Image: AFPTV/AFP

But there is some cooperation between the two countries behind the scenes. Analysts say that if a government less hardline than Netanyahu's gets into power in Israel, it will be easier for countries like Saudi Arabia — but also the United Arab Emirates, Jordan and Egypt, which all have varying levels of backchannel cooperation and formal or informal contact with Israel — to admit to this kind of behind-the-scenes diplomacy.

Syria: Security agreement revived?

According to a study published last week by Syrian think tank, Etana, Israeli troops have come as far as 1,160 kilometers (721 miles) into Syria from the two countries' disputed border, occupied Syrian land as far as 400 kilometers from it and carried out 1,996 ground operations in southwest Syria between January and September this year.

Before elections this week there was no chance of any kind of withdrawal from Syria because it would have been seen as "defeat," Ksenia Svetlova, an associate fellow at Chatham House and a former member of the Israeli parliament, told online publication Syria in Transition this month. But if the anti-Netanyahu bloc gets into power, that could change, she suggested.

Israeli troops have destroyed infrastructure and roads in places like Hamidiyah in Quneitra, near the Golan Heights, in Syria Image: Ercin Erturk/Anadolu/picture alliance

"A security agreement with Syria will become more probable, as many potential stakeholders [in a new, more centrist Israeli government] have spoken favorably about it in the past," noted Svetlova, who is also director of the Tel Aviv-based Regional Organization for Peace, Economics and Security, which works on Israeli-Palestinian-Arab partnerships. "However I do expect that it will take time as this government will be constantly attacked by the extreme right."

For months this year, Israel and Syrian diplomats negotiated a security agreement under the US' stewardship. But it came to nothing in late 2026 after Israel apparently refused to withdraw back to boundary lines established under a 1974 disengagement agreement.

Lebanon: More diplomacy wanted

Observers and media commentators in Lebanon say the Lebanese government would prefer to have Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc in power.

Lebanon and Israel are continuing to negotiate an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon, where the Israelis claim they have established a "buffer zone" to facilitate their fight against Lebanese militia group, Hezbollah. The Lebanese argue the Israelis have in fact invaded their country.

And when it comes to negotiations around disarming Hezbollah and withdrawing Israeli troops, there's a perception in Lebanese political circles that Eisenkot would be easier to deal with than Netanyahu and his extremist allies.

The Israeli military has enormous damage in southern Lebanon. At one stage, Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of giving in to the US when he stopped bombing Beirut Image: Zohra Bensemra/REUTERS

This is despite the fact that Eisenkot is widely seen as the inventor of the so-called "Dahiyeh Doctrine," a military strategy that calls for asymmetric warfare in areas like Beirut's southern suburbs, where Hezbollah is based, to pressure both militants and their civilian support base.

A similar strategy is thought to be being implemented in southern Lebanon now, where whole villages continue to be razed by the Israeli military, even as active fighting has subsided.

Lebanese commentators are also optimistic that Eisenkot, former commander of the Israeli army, would have something in common with their own president, Joseph Aoun, who used to head Lebanon's armed forces.

"When Netanyahu was ousted from power between 2021 and 2022 by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid [now members of the camp led by Eisenkot], we were able to negotiate and conclude the maritime agreement," a Lebanese official told Lebanese daily, L'Orient Today , referring to a 2022 deal to share offshore territory.

World.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy irked by US-Russia-China summit
World.content:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy has voiced his concerns about a probable meeting between the leaders of the US, China and Russia next month. Plus, a localized truce appeared to be holding in the town of Oleshky.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that a planned meeting between Russia, China and the United States next month could present the three participants with an opportunity to redraw global spheres of influence.

"We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' with a redistribution of influence," he said in comments to journalists on Wednesday, referring to the 1945 Yalta Conference in Crimea , where Allied powers redrew the world map in the wake of the Second World War.

Putin raised idea of three-way summit with Trump: What to know

The Kremlin has previously indicated that preparations were underway for a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US and Chinese counterparts, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific summit next month.

The Wall Street Journal first broke the news about the three-way summit earlier this month and said that Trump had not agreed to attend the summit at the time.

But the Journal said Trump was open to the proposal — that had been raised by Putin — since he wanted to bring an end to the war in Ukraine.

"What China, Russia and the United States might discuss has not yet been clearly defined," Zelenskyy said, adding that "Russia wants this meeting more than anyone," warning against handing Moscow "another major diplomatic advantage."

For years now, Russia has been seeking a new agreement with Washington on European security architecture, and in particular an end to what Putin considers NATO's aggressive expansion towards Russia.

Putin has falsely repeatedly said Ukraine war was an act of self-defense

Putin continues to cast the ongoing invasion of Ukraine as a response to such a NATO threat – a position widely rejected in Kyiv and the rest of Europe.

Zelenskyy's warning came ahead of planned talks between Ukrainian, Russian and US envoys in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) next month.

No specific date has been set for the Abu Dhabi meeting, but Kyiv is keen for it to take place before the potential Russia-China-US summit.

Before that, it was also confirmed on Wednesday that Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov will travel to the United States for a meeting with G20 counterparts in Atlanta on October 30-31.

Zelenskyy's comments were released as he traveled to the Netherlands for talks with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten Image: Remko de Waal/ANP/picture alliance

Zelenskyy in Netherlands

Zelenskyy's remarks were released as he traveled to the Netherlands for meetings with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten and Dutch King Willem-Alexander in The Hague.

The Dutch government said on Wednesday it would provide Ukraine with €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) in non-military support over the next ⁠years.

Zelenskyy also held a phone call with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham to thank him for an ​extra £10 ⁠billion ($13.29 billion/€11.94 billion) of support announced earlier ⁠on ​Wednesday.

"A truly ​strong very timely step coming right Russia needs to and ​feel that Ukraine will not be left ​alone to deal with the problems ⁠Russia ​is so ​eager to escalate," he wrote on social media.

But Ukraine's greatest assets in its defense against Russian aggression remain US Patriot air defense missiles, and Zelenskyy urged Washington to increase supplies.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine had been receiving 12 missiles a month this year but is being targeted with "150 ballistic missiles a month."

Oleshky truce holding for now, Zelenskyy says

Meanwhile on the battlefield, officials said a six-day ceasefire in a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine held for its first day and night.

The localized truce in the devastated town of Oleshky began on Tuesday and is due to last until Sunday, enabling a planned humanitarian operation to provide around 2,000 remaining residents with urgently needed food and medicine, and evacuate those who want to leave.

"We are grateful that they are organizing this possibility to evacuate people," said President Zelenskyy.

The plight of Oleshky in Ukraine's southern Kherson region caught the attention of US first lady Melania Trump, who the White House said helped broker the humanitarian mission.

If the ceasefire holds, it will be the first time in more than four-and-a-half years of fighting that both sides have observed a significant truce, with previous attempts quickly unraveling.

"This is the biggest de-escalation since 2022," said Ukraine's negotiator, Davyd ‌Arakhamia, on Tuesday, adding every step brings peace closer.

Oleshky ceasefire comes into effect in Ukraine war To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Drone attacks in Kharkiv, Belgorod — and off Bulgaria

Elsewhere, however, the war raged on with five people, including a four-year-old child, injured in a Russian drone strike on the northeastern Ukrainian city of Kharkiv overnight.

In Moscow, the Russian Defense Ministry said air defenses had downed 531 Ukrainian drones on Tuesday night and into Wednesday morning, but local authorities in the Belgorod border region said one person was killed in a drone attack.

And in Sofia, Bulgarian Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov said three maritime drones struck a container ship in the Black Sea off the coast of Bulgaria.

The crew evacuated the vessel and there were no immediate reports of casualties, according to Bulgarian state news agency BTA, but the incident took place as defense ministers from Bulgaria, Romania and Turkey were meeting in Sofia for trilateral talks focused on Black Sea security.

"We follow with concern the intense attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea ​and call on the sides to act with common sense, in line with the principle of navigational safety in open seas," said Turkish Defense Minister Yasar Guler.

"The necessary warnings are constantly being conveyed to both sides to keep commercial navigational out of the conflict zone and ​immediately halt attacks on civilian vessels."

A series of drone attacks have occurred this month off the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria. Russia has not taken responsibility, but suspicion has increasingly fallen on Moscow.

"The logic points in that direction," Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev told parliament earlier this month. "The problem is that we cannot prove it."

World.title: Los audios del accidente|El controlador de Atocha, al maquinista del AVE: “Desconecte y vuelva a conectar. Reanude con marcha normal”
World.content:
Lugar del accidente de dos trenes de alta velocidad, uno de Renfe y otro de Iryo, que han colisionado a primera hora de este miércoles a la altura de la estación de Urda (Toledo).

El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

Los audios muestran el error del responsable de Atocha. La maquinista del Iryo avisó a cinco minutos de la tragedia de que estaba detenida y no podía arrancar el tren. Y nadie frenó al AVE

Los tres audios clave de la tragedia, dos conexiones entre la maquinista del tren Iryo que estaba parado y el controlador de Atocha y uno del maquinista del AVE que venía por detrás y este mismo operador, demuestran con claridad los errores que se cometieron. El controlador da la orden al tren AVE, que estaba 25 kilómetros por detrás del Iryo, de que reinicie “la marcha normal”, y no a vista, como señalaba el protocolo, con una limitación de 40 kilómetros por hora. Y, además, lo hace sin comprobar que no hay ningún tren delante obstaculizando la vía. La maquinista del Iryo también recibe la misma orden, de reanudar “la marcha normal”, pero siete minutos después llama para decir que sigue detenida porque no puede reiniciar el tren con el sistema LZB y, sin embargo, nadie avisó al AVE ni siquiera ahí, a cinco minutos de la tragedia, de que tenía que frenar.

El controlador de Atocha, al maquinista del AVE: “Reanude con marcha normal”

El audio clave entre el centro de control de Atocha y el AVE, que dura más de cinco minutos, es muy confuso en el arranque, donde se ve al controlador con muchas dudas, pero termina con una orden clara que según el Gobierno contraviene claramente el protocolo y está en el origen del accidente: reanudar la marcha normal cuando aún no ha comprobado que el tren que estaba delante se haya alejado lo suficiente —más de 30 kilómetros— para evitar una colisión.

Los dos hombres al final de la conversación redactan una especie de acta de las órdenes que está recibiendo el maquinista, para que quede claro que ambos entienden lo mismo:

—CRC Atocha a maquinista de tren es 2080

—Sí

—A las 08.36.

—Sí

—Y esto dice: maquinista de tren 2080. Desconecte y vuelva a conectar el LZB. Reanude marcha. Y luego reanude la marcha al amparo del BSL con marcha normal

—¿Con marcha normal?

—Sí.

Ahí está el primer gran error, según el Ejecutivo, ordenar al AVE que reanude la marcha a las 8.36, cuando aún no ha comprobado que el Iryo se está alejando, y además hacerlo a marcha normal, sin el protocolo de seguridad de marcha “a vista”, que podría haber evitado el accidente.

Los otros dos audios también apuntan claramente a otros dos errores, puesto que la maquinista del Iryo avisó de que seguía detenida al no haber podido reanudar la marcha pese a haber recibido la autorización para ello.

02:11 Conversación Iryo - Adif Atocha (2) Vídeo: EPV

08.41: Primera llamada con el Iryo

—Buenos días, Atocha. He tenido una pérdida de transmisión circulando en BSL. El siguiente se ha de ir en el 113 a más de 200. Pero no he cogido transmisión. Estoy detenida. A la entrada de Urda.

Después de varios mensajes confusos, el controlador finalmente sigue el protocolo y se dispone a dar las órdenes y firmar esa especie de acta conjunta para que quede claro que ambos han entendido lo mismo:

—Vale, pues un momentito. Esto dice maquinista de tren 6076. Desconecte. Y vuelva a conectar.

—Y vuelva a conectar.

—Reanude la marcha, al amparo del BSL, con marcha normal.

De nuevo, el controlador vuelve a dar la orden de marcha normal, algo fuera de protocolo e incluso de la ley, también al Iryo. Pero lo hace cuatro minutos después de hablar con el AVE, a pesar de que está delante y muy cerca. Según el Ejecutivo, primero tendría que haberse asegurado de que el Iryo estaba fuera del alcance del AVE y después ordenarle reanudar.

Pero hay un tercer mensaje también desconcertante, tal vez el más evidente porque ahí aún se podía haber evitado la tragedia: el Iryo llama para decir que no puede arrancar porque no logra revisar el sistema LZB, y aparentemente el controlador no toma ninguna decisión drástica con esa información ni avisa al AVE de que se detenga, cuando aún estaba a tiempo.

00:53 Conversación Iryo - Adif Atocha (1) Vídeo: EPV

08.48: Segunda llamada con el Iryo

Maquinista: No me está permitiendo el tren reiniciar el sistema LZB. Y por eso estoy todavía detenida ante la señal de entrada.

Control: Vale. ¿Conforme? Pues nada, en cuanto pueda. Y si tiene problema, ahora nos llama.

Maquinista: Vale, perfecto. Ahora le digo.

Y ahí empieza una conversación interna que muestra un cierto caos en el centro de control:

—De verdad, tronco. De verdad. El 6071 está teniendo problemas con el equipo. Está avanzando hasta que se detenga. Tenía un Meta40 que continuara en BSL. No hemos cambiado. Un momento.

Cinco minutos después de esta conversación, se produjo el choque mortal del AVE con el Iryo sin que aparentemente nadie fuera consciente de que estaba a punto de llegar una de las mayores tragedias de la alta velocidad europea, y la segunda en España en un año y en la misma línea después de 35 años sin un solo siniestro mortal.

World.title: El “espectáculo inmoral de la feria de oportunidades de Franco” revienta las expectativas de recaudación
World.content:
El mayor éxito artístico para Isabel de Cubas, cuñada de Carmen Franco aficionada a pintar, llegó insospechadamente 18 años después de su muerte en 2008. La esposa de Andrés Martínez-Bordiú, conde de Morata de Jalón y hermano del marqués de Villaverde, reventó todos los pronósticos en la primera sesión de la subasta de suvenires del pazo de Meirás que se celebra esta semana en Madrid, cuando su pequeño cuadro —tasado por las expertas de Magna Art Auctions en 50 euros— desató la locura entre los postores. De un soplido, el óleo naíf (que representa toscamente la fachada del pazo que disfrutó la familia del dictador ocho décadas) disparó su cotización hasta los 6.000 euros. Para los nostálgicos, o fanáticos, esta pintura sobre tabla era importante pese a su técnica elemental; no solo por su temática, sino porque la autora había incluido por la parte trasera una dedicatoria: “Para mi querida Carmen Franco, con todo mi cariño”.

Los nietos del dictador Francisco Franco se deshacen desde el martes de un millar de objetos de Meirás que no tienen interés en conservar, agrupados en 689 lotes. Y el éxito de la puja es tal que ha sobrepasado las expectativas de la casa de subastas Magna Art. Las sesiones son maratonianas y se han visto obligados a alargar la tarea un día más (con horario ampliado), después de que el martes el equipo no lograse avanzar más que hasta el lote 250 (una lámpara de araña descoyuntada) cuando la jornada agónica se acercaba ya a la medianoche y los presentes en la sala empezaban a marchar, agotados, dejando sus paletas de puja en la entrada. Desde las 17 horas hasta casi las 22.30, cuando la casa de subastas acordó hacer un receso para ir al baño, el carrusel de recuerdos del pazo no dio ni una tregua. Con tanto frenesí pujador, cuando se llegó al lote 200 ya se había superado la valoración de partida del conjunto de 689 lotes: 207.700 euros. La primera sesión rozó el cuarto de millón de euros, todavía con la mayor parte de los fetiches más deseados sin subastar.

Óleo de Meirás, firmado por la condesa de Morata de Jalón. Lote 45, con precio de salida de 50 euros y adjudicado por 6.000. Catálogo de Magna Art Auctions

El colectivo que más ha peleado durante estos años para que los bienes muebles que pertenecían a la historia del pazo gallego propiedad del Estado se quedasen en él, la Comisión pola Recuperación da Memoria Histórica da Coruña (CRMH), ha esperado al segundo día de subasta para reiterar su “indignación” y su “asco”. “Queremos mostrar públicamente nuestra indignación ante el espectáculo inmoral de esa especie de feria de oportunidades del franquismo”, expresan en una nota de prensa difundida este miércoles. Se trata, dicen, de “una asquerosa apología muy lucrativa del régimen genocida, que tiene como únicos beneficiarios a los herederos del dictador Franco”.

El cuadrito de Isabel de Cubas y Gerdtzen no fue, ni mucho menos, la única sorpresa de este rastrillo de postín en una de las zonas más elitistas de Madrid. El tapiz repostero con el escudo franquista pasó en nada de 850 a 9.000 euros y la maza acabó adjudicándoselo a alguien que pujaba desde una plataforma internacional. Los alambicados relojes de mesa, las viejas maquetas de barcos, los numerosos albarelos de farmacia y la abundante porcelana china de la dinastía Qing también multiplicaron con creces su valor, como un par de jarrones Hu que se despacharon a 7.000 o la pecera que subió de 150 a 2.500 euros.

Jarra de Talavera, siglo XVII, correspondiente al lote 111 del catálogo de la subasta de Meirás. Con un precio de salida de 350 euros, acabó adjudicándose por 10.000 y se convirtió en la pieza más cotizada de la primera sesión de pujas. Catálogo Magna Art Auctions

El mobiliario de jardín, sillas y bancos de hierro que aún hace pocos años poblaban el césped de Meirás, llegaron a multiplicar por 10 su precio en la puja. Una foto coloreada del Generalísimo, su esposa y su hija pasó de 80 a 2.250 euros. Una pequeña escalera de la biblioteca de Franco pasó de 50 a 1.500 y la lámpara rústica de esa misma estancia se vendió a 2.000. Un misal de la capilla de Meirás, se revalorizó de 90 a 900. Dos vinajeras litúrgicas, de los 400 a los 2.250. Dos figuritas de “santos niños mártires” pasaron de 150 a 5.000 cuando daban las diez de la noche. Una jarra “rara” de Talavera batió todos los récords cuando se adjudicó por 10.000 euros tras una reñida puja.

Para la CRMH, “la puja evidencia que el Estado y la Xunta no defendieron debidamente estos bienes”. El colectivo que preside Carlos Babío —en cuyas investigaciones de décadas se basó la Abogacía del Estado para recuperar el pazo de la familia ocupante— recuerda que no se atendió su reivindicación para que las Administraciones inspeccionasen y “en caso de encontrar bienes de dominio público, impidiesen la enajenación”. Respecto a esto, la CRMH advierte a los posibles compradores de que, “con independencia de que figurasen o no en inventarios, los bienes de dominio público son imprescriptibles e inalienables”.

“Atenta contra la integridad del pazo”

Esta puja, tal y como informa la misma asociación, es consecuencia de un proceso en el que Estado y Xunta de Galicia encargaron inventarios e informes sobre los bienes que formaban parte del inmueble en las etapas anteriores a la muerte del dictador en 1975. Entre ellos estaban también los elementos de antes de llegar Franco en 1938 a Meirás, ligados a la familia Pardo Bazán. El catálogo de la “subasta especial” de Magna Art “ha dejado en evidencia que muchos de los objetos tienen como mínimo una aparente vinculación con bienes ligados a esas etapas históricas y con la consideración de bienes de dominio público”, insiste la CRMH de A Coruña. “Algunos incluso son de fácil identificación y demostración”, avisa el grupo que guarda un amplio archivo fotográfico de las distintas etapas del pazo. Los memorialistas piden explicaciones de “por qué no fueron incorporados a los inventarios” que sí acordó defender la Abogacía del Estado en su día.

Tapiz repostero heráldico correspondiente al lote 129, con precio de salida de 850 euros y vendido a un postor internacional tras una reñida puja por 9.000. Catálogo Magna Art Auctions

“El abandono en la defensa de estos bienes atenta contra la integridad patrimonial del pazo”, que “queda vacío en parte de contenido”, lamenta la asociación gallega. Por extensión, la CRMH entiende que esta última peripecia de los herederos del dictador con luz verde del Gobierno de España es un golpe para la “memoria y el respeto que una sociedad democrática debe ofrecer y garantizar a las víctimas del franquismo”.

Para la Comisión de A Coruña es “inaceptable que, a más de 50 años de la muerte de Franco, sus descendientes continúen apropiándose de bienes que tienen su origen en la dictadura”. La reciente declaración del pazo de Meirás como Lugar de Memoria afirmaba: “Meirás ha dejado de ser únicamente un símbolo de la apropiación y del poder franquista para convertirse también en un referente de la defensa de los valores democráticos y de la construcción de una memoria colectiva basada en la verdad, la justicia, la reparación y la preservación del patrimonio común”.

World.title: La visita de Gabriel Rufián e Irene Montero da a ‘La Revuelta’ el tercer programa más visto de su historia
World.content:
El espacio de La 1 obtuvo un 21,7% de cuota de pantalla y una media de 2,7 millones de espectadores, casi 10 puntos por encima de ‘El hormiguero’

La visita de los candidatos a las elecciones generales de noviembre ha vuelto a dar un gran dato de audiencia a La Revuelta. Tras el récord histórico obtenido la semana pasada con su encuentro con Pedro Sánchez, la llegada este martes de Irene Montero (Podemos) y Gabriel Rufián (ERC) ha otorgado al programa presentado por David Broncano su tercera mejor marca de siempre: 21,7% de cuota de pantalla y una media de 2.654.000 espectadores, apunta el informe de Dos 30′ con datos recopilados por Fifty5Blue.

La Revuelta firmó la semana pasada con Pedro Sánchez un 33,9% de cuota de pantalla y una audiencia media de 4.387.000 espectadores. La visita de Rosalía en noviembre de 2025, le dio 20,4% y 2.706.000 espectadores de media. Por lo que la emisión de este martes logra el segundo mejor share histórico del programa, pero con unos 50.000 espectadores de media menos que la emisión con la cantante.

Con estos registros, el espacio de La 1 lideró su franja de emisión este martes, superando en casi 10 puntos a El hormiguero (1.539.000 espectadores de media y un 12,3% de cuota de pantalla), en la que ha sido una de las pocas ocasiones en las que el programa de Antena 3 queda por detrás del de la cadena pública esta temporada.

La Revuelta asegura que ha invitado a todos los líderes de las principales formaciones, pero que dos de ellos no han confirmado todavía su asistencia, así que habrá que ver si nuevos candidatos se pasan por el teatro de Broncano antes del 29-N.

Durante su paso por La Revuelta, los dos candidatos hablaron del problema de la vivienda, de sexo (durante el momento de las preguntas clásicas que finalmente no contestaron a título personal) y de la controvertida figura de Íñigo Errejón.

“Bajaríamos el precio del alquiler en un 40% y prohibiríamos la especulación. Prohibido comprar casas para hacer negocio”, apuntaba Montero sobre las medidas que aplicarían. “Una familia, una casa. Es un derecho”, ampliaba Rufián.

Broncano preguntó a los dos invitados cuánto les habían sorprendido las acusaciones que hicieron dimitir a Errejón. “Me sorprendió 10”, respondió Rufián. A Montero no: dijo que lo sabía bastante gente. “Es el poder de los tíos moviéndose con impunidad. Lo hemos criticado mucho las feministas”, dijo ella.

World.title: De Sitges a Montserrat: cuatro escapadas en los alrededores de Barcelona
World.content:
La capital catalana es mucho más que el territorio por el que se pierden cada año 26 millones de turistas. La arquitectura de referencia, el patrimonio cultural, natural y gastronómico han superado de sobra las fronteras urbanas

Las curiosidades alrededor de Barcelona se desperdigan por toda la provincia. Están presentes en ese Gaudí y modernismo tan típicos de la zona, pero también reúne otros característicos atributos, como la fuerza de la montaña, la genética de los viñedos y las bodegas y la singularidad de las poblaciones costeras. Barcelona confunde, pero es mucho más que la ciudad por la que se pierden cada año 26 millones de turistas. Ofrecemos aquí cuatro recomendaciones para quienes se acercan a la capital catalana, pero también quieren alejarse un poco de ella.

La Colònia Güell y la cripta de Gaudí

A apenas 20 minutos en tren desde la ciudad hay un enclave que merece una visita. Se trata de la Colònia Güell, con la cripta que construyó aquí Antoni Gaudí, el autor de la Sagrada Familia. La colonia industrial (con las viviendas de los obreros junto a la fábrica) está en el municipio de Santa Coloma de Cervelló (8.200 habitantes). La construyó en 1890 el industrial Eusebi Güell para trasladar la fábrica textil que tenía en Barcelona y alejarla de los conflictos sociales y laborales. Güell veló porque sus trabajadores gozaran de mejoras sociales y culturales, y construyó un núcleo racionalista con escuela en un edificio donde también estaba la casa del maestro, el ambulatorio y otros equipamientos como el Ateneu Unió, con teatro, una cooperativa de consumo y la iglesia. Eso sí, como en todas las colonias fabriles, la vida social y económica se desarrollaba bajo la tutela del empresario.

Más información Pedaleando por el barrio de Poblenou en Barcelona hasta el mar

Gaudí, a quien el industrial encargaría posteriormente el Park Güell, comenzó las obras en 1908, pero el proyecto quedó inacabado después de construir la nave inferior, la cripta, un porche y parte del campanario. El edificio incluye buena parte de las innovaciones que aplicaría en el futuro, como el ladrillo, formas naturales o 200 arcos y nervios para prescindir de contrafuertes y arbotantes. El resultado es una construcción asombrosamente gaudiniana, con coloridos vitrales y, además, incluye mobiliario modernista de madera ideado por el arquitecto. La industria, colectivizada durante la Guerra Civil, pero que la familia recuperó posteriormente, fue vendida en 1945 y cerró en 1973.

La inacabada cripta de la Colònia Güell, obra modernista de Antoni Gaudí. Albert Garcia

La colonia conserva el ambiente de pueblo tranquilo con media docena de calles con casas unifamiliares con patio delantero y trasero, cuyos propietarios, en algunos casos, parecen competir por quién tiene el jardín más bonito. Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya (FCG) tiene un billete de ida y vuelta a la Colònia Güell desde Barcelona que incluye la entrada a la cripta y audioguía para recorrer el recinto. Todo por 15,8 euros.

Montserrat, símbolo físico y del imaginario de Cataluña

También con acceso directo desde Barcelona en transporte público (encadenando trayectos en FCG y trenes turísticos), la montaña de Montserrat, reconocible por su silueta y símbolo físico y del imaginario de Cataluña, recibe cada año más de dos millones de visitantes. Es un enclave singular porque reúne, en poco espacio, una espectacular geografía y naturaleza, arte y cultura de primera magnitud (¡en el museo hay un caravaggio!) y espiritualidad: aquí fundaron los monjes benedictinos el Monasterio de Montserrat hace 1.001 años, cuya basílica preside la Virgen de la Moreneta, patrona de Cataluña, y donde, a excepción de los sábados, canta la Escolanía. En clave local, Montserrat es lugar también de peregrinación y celebración para familias e instituciones catalanas.

El Monasterio de Montserrat, con la montaña de fondo. Lorena Sopena (Europa Press / Getty Images)

Con un paisaje de agujas y montículos redondeados de piedra gris formado por rocas que eran los sedimentos de la cuenca del Ebro, ofrece desde exigentes zonas de escalada hasta senderos aptos para toda la familia. La altitud máxima del macizo es de 1.200 metros. En el plano cultural, el Museo de Montserrat reúne desde obra antigua hasta arte contemporáneo de artistas españoles de primer nivel. La basílica también merece una visita, para escuchar a la Escolanía, bajar a la impresionante cripta (donde reposan los monjes que murieron durante la Guerra Civil) u observar las capillas laterales, con obra firmada por escultores de la talla de Josep Maria Subirachs, autor de la Fachada de la Pasión de la Sagrada Familia.

Vale mucho la pena quedarse a dormir, porque el silencio y el ambiente cuando se marchan los visitantes es impresionante. Las opciones son variadas. Hay un solo hotel con restaurante, el Abat Cisneros; están los apartamentos del edificio Cel·les Abat Marcet, evolución de las antiguas celdas en las que durante siglos se alojaron los peregrinos cuando la hospedería del monasterio se quedaba pequeña; y la otra opción es el albergue Abat Oliva, con habitaciones compartidas o familiares.

El Penedès, viñas y más

Puede sonar contraintuitivo en un territorio de viñedos y bodegas, pero el Penedès no renuncia a nada, como Carlos Rodríguez y Montse Virgili tampoco lo hicieron cuando empezaron a cocinar cerveza artesana en su casa y acabaron montando una microcervecería en la Masia Agullons, buen lugar para iniciar una ruta por la zona. De allí sale la cerveza de la marca Ales Agullons, que hace años recibió un reconocimiento internacional por elaborar la mejor cerveza artesana hecha en barrica. Signo o no de que el vino lo impregna todo en esta comarca, Masia Agullons se encuentra en Sant Joan de Mediona, rodeada de tierras de vides y cebada, y a unos pocos kilómetros en carretera siempre serpeante del municipio hermano de Sant Quintí de Mediona. Allí, mucho más exclusiva, se ubica la Bodega Can Sala o Can Freixeneda, el lugar donde nació uno de los gigantes del Penedès, el productor de cava Freixenet. Hoy van por caminos muy diferentes: Freixenet, en manos de un gran productor alemán y enfocado a las grandes producciones, y Can Sala, atesorado por la familia Ferrer y centrado en su cava de paraje cualificado.

Viñas de la bodega Gramona, en Sant Sadurni d'Anoia. Vicens Gimenez

No son pocos los cellers, grandes y pequeños, que han creado su propio museo, si bien quienes quieran dar un paso adelante en el campo del conocimiento deben acercarse a Vilafranca del Penedès o a Sant Sadurní d’Anoia para visitar sus museos del vino y del vinum titillum, el vino que hace cosquillas, que decían los romanos de los espumosos. Quienes prefieran hacer un alto en el camino y disfrutar de la calma natural pueden acercarse a ver los denominados pèlags, masas de agua que surgieron de las explotaciones mineras que se explotaron en tiempo de los romanos; es el caso de los cuatro que hay en el Parc dels Talls, en Vilobí del Penedès. Una visita para caminar, como la que ofrecen (otra vez) multitud de bodegas entre sus viñedos, con cata de vinos incluida.

Perderse en Sitges

Desde que Santiago Rusiñol lo puso de moda entre sus coetáneos modernistas, Sitges se convirtió en un contrapunto de las colonias de veraneo de la burguesía que se expandieron por el litoral al norte de Barcelona y hoy es un éxito turístico rotundo. La mejor forma de entenderlo es seguir el paseo marítimo hasta la escalinata bajo la fachada de la iglesia de Sant Bartomeu y Santa Tecla, subirla y desde la plaza del Baluard volver a otear el mar para girar de nuevo y adentrarse a recorrer sus callejuelas de edificios encalados en blanco. Allí están el Palau de Terramar (solo visitable los domingos, con entrada previa), el Museo de Maricel (excepcional balcón al Mediterráneo) y el del Cau Ferrat, casa-taller de Rusiñol y templo del modernismo desde entonces, convertido en museo desde 1933. Recomendable también es buscar la calle más antigua del municipio, la d’En Bosc, muestra de su pasado medieval y donde se encuentra el gótico del Palau del Moro.

El Palau de Maricel, junto al mar Mediterráneo en la localidad de Sitges, en la provincia de Barcelona. juan orihuela (GETTY IMAGES)

Desde esa zona se puede continuar, según gustos, hacia el paseo que continúa hacia la playa de San Sebastián u optar por el casco urbano hacia la Plaça de la Vila. Sitios para tomar algo en un lugar donde en verano se multiplica la población no es difícil. Como tampoco lo es toparse con las casas que se construyeron los americanos locales, los hombres que se fueron a hacer fortuna a Cuba y volvieron con los bolsillos llenos. Y si la ruta quiere ser más larga, los Jardines de Terramar, de 1919, son los vestigios de una historia a medio construir: la idea de crear una ciudad jardín que pretendía contar también con casino propio. Hoy son solo un parque, muy entretenido para los niños, que linda con un campo de golf y un resort hotelero.

Hoy el municipio es referente del turismo familiar y LGTBIQ+ al albur de sus playas y su centro histórico, y se ha convertido también en punto de reunión festivo, gracias a su carnaval, y cultural, por el legado que dejó el mismo Rusiñol o el que reúne cada año el Festival de Cine Fantástico de Sitges. Para conocer la Blanca Subur, lo mejor es adentrarse por las callejuelas.

World.title: Vídeos de ajedrez | Arte con la luz de un candil
World.content:
No sólo es arte. Además, es artesano. Lo produjo, en los primeros años del siglo XX, uno de los mejores compositores de finales artísticos de todos los tiempos, el francés Henri Rinck (1870-1952). Hoy, las dos maravillas de este vídeo serían relativamente fáciles de elaborar, porque ambas constan de muy pocas piezas, con ayuda de programas informáticos muy potentes que corren en un teléfono móvil y juegan mejor que el campeón del mundo.

Hace más de cien años, no sólo eran impensables los módulos digitales, sino que Rinck ni siquiera se dedicaba profesionalmente al ajedrez -era químico especializado en el aceite de oliva- y sólo podía producir su arte al atardecer, a la luz de un candil, en su domicilio de Barcelona. Y así creó estas dos joyitas, cuyo factor común, además de las pocas piezas, es que requieren pensar fuera de la caja. La imaginación convertida en arte artesanal.

World.title: Jetten calls for tougher sanctions against Russia ahead of talks
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has called for Europe to present a united front and step up sanctions against Russia in order to force Vladimir Putin to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine.

Jetten told reporters at a joint president with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy in The Hague that economic pressure was needed to persuade Putin to give ground.

His remarks came after Polish president Donald Tusk said the US, Ukraine and Russia had provisionally agreed to hold ceasefire talks in Abu Dhabi on November 4.

European leaders will not be present, but Tusk said Finnish president Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre had held a call with Putin after consulting Zelenskyy and the American side.

Zelenskyy told reporters in The Hague that it was “very important” for Europe to show unity “because Russia is focusing on how to divide us”.

“Russia is losing,” he said. “The American side is asking to find a balance and a compromise. If they need a compromise, we say: Russia is not winning. But what is very clear is they are not ending the war.

No Russian gas

“That is the problem. That’s why we need to work step by step and move Russia to end this war.”

Jetten also ruled out restarting supplies of Russian gas to Europe, an idea reportedly raised by Donald Trump’s peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff during talks with Zelenskyy at the weekend.

“It is clear that we need to push Putin to take the negotiations seriously,” he said.

“The way forward for Europeans, but also for Americans and others, is to put more sanctions on the Russian regime, not less. So buying Russian energy is a very stupid idea. I can assure you that there is no European leader who is willing to buy Russian gas in the next few years.

“What we want is for Russia to stop this war, and as long as they don’t we will hit them hard in their pockets with sanctions.”

Aid packages

The Dutch government announced on Wednesday it was spending another €1.2 billion on non-military aid to Ukraine over the next three years, as well as €500 million on military support in the form of air defence and drones.

The non-military aid, announced by foreign trade minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma on a visit to Kyiv, will address “the most urgent needs” such as energy, drinking water, humanitarian aid, healthcare and medicine, as well as operations to clear landmines.

“Russia is hoping to break Ukraine’s morale, its society and its economy,” Jetten said.

“But they will not succeed. Firstly because of the great courage and resilience of the Ukrainians themselves, but also because we as allies realise that we must not let up on giving our support.”

World.title: Booking can compel staff to spend two days in the office: court
World.content:
A court has ruled that travel website Booking.com can compel its staff to spend at least two days a week in the office, settling a dispute with the company’s works council.

The decision was widely expected after the judge remarked at an earlier hearing that requiring employees to spend 40% of their contracted hours on site was “very normal”.

Just over a quarter of Booking.com’s 7,000 staff currently travel to its head office in Amsterdam twice a week. The company had advised its workers to spend two days in the office to promote better workplace relations, training and efficient working practices.

But when bosses tried to make the two-day guideline a mandatory requirement, the works council objected. It said the impact on people’s work-life balance, commuting times and travel costs was too great and questioned whether it would lead to improved performance.

The judge said the company had taken employees’ concerns into account and responded by introducing a six-month transition period and deciding to set the minimum office time at 40% rather than 50% or 60%.

Booking said it welcomed the judgment, pointing out that the two-day rule was not a new measure but a “strengthening of our current policy”.

“We value the relationship with our works council and will continue to hold constructive dialogue with them and our employees as we roll this policy out further,” a spokesman said.

Employment lawyer Pascal Besselink told RTL Nieuws other companies that wanted staff to spend more time in the office would be studying the judgment closely.

“They will always strive to maintain a good relationship with their employees and works council and consult thoroughly on arrangements about home working,” he said.

Two explosives from the Second World War have been discovered at Eindhoven Airport during renovation groundwork next to one of the airport’s runways.

A spokesperson for the Royal Marechaussee, a branch of the military police, said the explosives were found on Wednesday morning on the military side of the airport, which shares the runway with civilian planes, Brabants Dagblad reported.

One of the items is a mortar shell, and the other has not yet been identified, the spokesperson told broadcaster NOS.

No air traffic was disrupted by the discovery and no civilians were at any harm.

World.title: “Strict” Dutch border controls lead to 650 refusals in 21 months
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Fewer than 700 people were turned away at the Dutch border in 21 months of extra border controls that were introduced as part of the “strictest asylum policy ever”.

Border police stopped 43,210 vehicles and checked 182,700 people crossing land borders into Belgium and Germany after the last government reintroduced border controls in December 2024.

A total of 650 people were refused entry while trying to cross the border by road during the period until the checks, introduced by former asylum minister Marjolein Faber of the far-right PVV party, ended in September.

Police arrested 300 people, of whom 40 were suspected of involvement in human trafficking. The government also said 140 people claimed asylum after being stopped at the border.

Some 70% of people stopped at the land borders were EU citizens, asylum minister Bart van den Brink said in a letter to parliament. Border police also checked 398,000 people travelling on flights within the Schengen zone, 85% of whom had EU passports.

Van den Brink said the checks were stepped up to deal with the “significant impact of the continued influx of irregular migration”.

According to Frontex figures, the number of irregular border crossings is down by 26% since 2024. In the same period there has been a 25% drop in first-time asylum applications in the Netherlands.

Schengen zone rules allow member states to reinstate border checks as a temporary measure if there is a threat to security or public order, but they must keep the EU updated on progress.

World.title: Police seize dozens of servers in Limburg over cybercrime
World.content:
The police have seized dozens of servers from a data centre in Limburg that were allegedly used to distribute child pornography, as well as carry out cyberattacks and phishing scams.

The seizures are part of an investigation into an unnamed company, a so-called bulletproof hoster, which provides web space and server access to criminal groups.

Police say they have now gained information on over 3,000 customers who used the servers, and that the hunt for those people is now underway.

At the same time, the FBI and German police also acted against suspects revealed in the investigation, seizing cryptocurrency and shutting down online infrastructure.

The location of the data centre has not yet been made public since the servers in question were housed alongside legal ones, local broadcaster L1 reported.

Police confirmed around 50 servers were taken on Tuesday. The US department of justice announced at the same time that the FBI had taken action against a site called Virtualine, with assistance from Dutch, British and German authorities. The connection between these cases has not yet been confirmed.

The seizure follows a raid in July on the hosting company used by Motherless, a porn website which contained huge amounts of abusive material. NOS later reported that the site’s own employees had uploaded child pornography.

World.title: Free as a bird? New law for freelancers goes into consultation
World.content:
If you work as a freelancer or have your own business, you should be aware of a new law that the Dutch government has just proposed.

The Zelfstandigenwet, or freelance law, aims to create more “peace and clarity” for people who want to work on their own, according to employment minister Thierry Aartsen.

There has already been an exodus of freelancers due to a crackdown on “sham” self-employment, but tax advisers believe people should not panic.

“Don’t get scared,” said an adviser for Blue Umbrella tax service. “Believe in your business, believe in being self-supporting and go for it! Economic growth comes from small and medium-sized enterprises and the government knows that.”

Tests

The new law proposal, which could come into force in 2028 if the minority government manages to find support, will make it clearer what you need to do to be considered a freelancer, or “zzp’er”.

In the past, this group could get a special document from the tax office confirming their freelance status but instead of this formal recognition, there will be a series of tests.

You will need to be registered with the Chamber of Commerce (Kamer van Koophandel) – which is true for most businesses, in any case. You will also need a VAT number and a business bank account, and you must have worked for at least three different clients in two years. Freelancers may also need a specific financial buffer, insurance and pension savings.

Another test will examine how independently you work, including whether you can organise your working hours and take financial risks.

Portfolio

Blue Umbrella recommends making it clear to your potential customers that you will meet the requirements. “Make a portfolio of your clients and what you did in the past year,” the advisor said. “Show that you have a substantial business with multiple clients and you are developing yourself. That gives them trust that they can hire you.”

There is currently an internet consultation running for all freelancers and interested parties until October 29. When the law comes in, however, it may be tested in court: it is not clear why someone with three clients could objectively be called freelance as opposed to someone with two.

Reduction

Under pressure from unions and the European Commission, which has linked some of the compensation for the Netherlands during corona to reducing “fake freelancing”, the number of Dutch self-employed workers has already gone down.

A report last week from the DNB central bank found that there were 131,000 fewer freelancers halfway through 2026 than there were at the end of 2024. The peak came in 2024, when almost 1.3 million people worked for themselves.

According to the report, a third of those who stopped found a permanent job or one that could become a fixed contract. But 40% of the people who stopped freelancing switched to work in a completely different occupation, and 7% became unemployed.

Complex

Blue Umbrella has seen some clients close their businesses too, but stressed that people should not despair: this issue has been around for a long time and, in practice, it is complex. The proposed law aims to help people prove they are genuinely self-employed in future but it would not necessarily stop people who are currently freelancing, under the current rules.

“If you talk about whether someone can make their own decisions as one of the factors to judge whether they are self-employed, it’s a hard question,” said the adviser. “Even as a contractor, you always follow the instructions of the client. You can’t just do your own thing because you think it’s your decision. That would be absurd!”

That said, it’s a good idea to be careful with your finances and consider what extra investments you might want to make, if there are uncertainties in the future of self-employment in the Netherlands.

But do not give up! “The biggest tax revenue comes from small businesses and they are our economic drivers, not the big companies,” he said. “The world will change, and at the end of the day, you have to do it yourself, not rely on the government!”

Find out more about Blue Umbrella’s cost-efficient scheme for businesses and tax services for internationals

World.title: PostNL worker faces 10 years over deadly fake pill webshop
World.content:
The public prosecution service (OM) is demanding prison sentences of 10 and 6.5 years for two suspects accused of involvement in a counterfeit medicine webshop, whose products appear to have led to the deaths of three people.

The pair are alleged to have worked for an organisation that set up dozens of online sites offering prescription pills like sedatives, painkillers and sleeping aids. The sites were shutdown last week and three people arrested for orchestrating the operation.

People bought the pills online without knowing what was actually in them. Some contained powerful synthetic opioids like nitazenes, which can be far more deadly than fentanyl.

The two suspects were not the main players in the case; one is accused of storing and packing the orders, and the other of using his role in the postal service to ensure deliveries were made.

The PostNL employee is also suspected of importing and dealing in large quantities of cocaine, according to broadcaster NOS.

Both suspects say they had no idea they were helping distribute contaminated pills. A lawyer for one of the defendants described his client as a “glorified assembly-line worker”.

World.title: King sees challenges and successes on visit to asylum centre
World.content:
King Willem-Alexander has visited one of the Netherlands’ longest running accommodation centres for asylum seekers to talk to refugees and local residents.

The king received an enthusiastic reception from the 530 people living in the centre in Leersum, Utrecht province, which has been operational for 35 years.

He said he wanted to see how a refugee centre “can be integrated into a local community”, but also gain an insight into the challenges for people living in the area.

During his visit he was shown the facilities in the centre such as a women’s café with yoga and cooking workshops, a bicycle repair shop and support for refugees looking for work or training.

“We all know what the problems are and we see them a lot,” the king said. “But it is also good to be able to show, by being here and bringing lots of journalists along, that things can go very well.”

He was handed a bundle of letters from primary school children, in which they told their personal stories and described how they missed their parents.

The head of the school, Bea, who has been teaching refugee children for 16 years, told AD.nl that the outlook was bleaker than at any time she could remember because of the length of time it is taking for asylum claims to be processed.

“A large group of children are still waiting for their parents, whom they haven’t seen for two or three years in some cases, to be given residency permits,” she said. “We have to deal with that as well as teaching classes.”

World.title: Turkish engineer creates live 3D pixel map of adopted hometown Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
