World.title: Estonian defense forces uniform sold online, but unauthorized public wear illegal
World.content:
While wearing Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) uniforms and insignia without the right to do so is illegal, they can still be bought freely online.

Under the Defense Forces Service Act, using the EDF uniform or insignia without authorization is banned, and illegal use is a misdemeanor offense the EDF itself can pursue.

This is in order to avoid for instance "false flag" efforts during times of crises, as well as cases of "stolen valor".

The regulation is set by a defense minister directive outlining each uniform element. Items like a regular officer's beret, sold by the volunteer Defense League (Kaitseliit) shop, meet that description. Online stores also offer various camouflage items: a summer scout cap, raincoat, shirt, vests and more. Reports have come in of uniforms worn in public by those lacking the right to do so.

The Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) can also verify, in public, whether an individual wearing EDF uniform is entitled to do so. The EDF can open misdemeanor proceedings where there is reason to believe the rules have been breached — for example based on information received, or where there is reasonable doubt about whether the wearer has the right.

There is no direct legal ban on buying or selling such products in civilian circulation, for instance via military surplus outlets, however, while retailing or producing them does not require a Defense Ministry permit.

At the same time, if a uniform was directly issued by the EDF, which makes it state property, selling or otherwise transferring it without authorization is prohibited, and the buyer of a standard EDF uniform or insignia is still liable if they wear it in public, even if the seller lacked the permit to sell.

In 2021 the Defense Ministry clarified that civilian wearing of the uniform was being banned due to its being official clothing worn in the course of service duties, including in combat. The ministry said it was vital a person wearing uniform, or clothing resembling it who was not a member of the military did not get confused with a service member carrying out duties.

The EDF considered this particularly important during any crisis or unrest, where illegal wearing of such clothing could, either inadvertently or deliberately, create a false impression of the actions of the EDF, the Defense League or the state. The concern also echoes what is often called "stolen valor" in the U.S. — the false impression created by wearing military uniform without entitlement.

World.title: Patient healthcare compensation claims on the rise, but many rejected
World.content:
Claims against healthcare providers have grown steadily in the nearly two years since the patient insurance system came into force, and so has the number of rejections.

"Looking at recent developments, the positive thing is that healthcare providers have adapted to the new regulation and everyone who must have patient insurance has signed a contract," Kairi Ruhno, service manager at the Health Board's (Terviseamet) healthcare services department, said.

Statistics also show patients are increasingly aware of patient insurance and are better able to use it.

"Whereas the previous healthcare quality expert committee got around 200 applications a year, in the first full year of the patient insurance system more than 400 compensation claims were filed with insurers. In the first ten months of this year, more than 660 applications have already been submitted," Ruhno said.

Ruhno stressed it is important to understand that not every treatment outcome that falls short of expectations automatically means a medical error occurred or an insurance claim can or should be made; simply that patients must have a clear and workable route to claim compensation for actual harm.

"Going forward, we see the greatest need for development in raising awareness. On the one hand it is important that healthcare providers understand the broader purpose of patient safety and the insurance system. On the other, patients' awareness of their rights and of how patient insurance works must increase, including which cases constitute an insured event and which do not," Ruhno went on.

Insurance market opening up

When liability insurance was introduced in Estonia over 20 years ago, in November 2004, there was only one option on the market, from insurers PZU. Now a PZU product and a new provider have been added, while market participants believe new insurers and products will ease the burden on healthcare providers and offer more flexible choices.

Liisi Murde-Parvell, a patient insurance expert at broker IIZI, said significant shifts have taken place, with Lloyd's entering alongside PZU and its terms now fully brought into line with the law. The arrival of new providers has ended PZU's monopoly, and brought prices down, though the market will take time to settle. "Pricing is difficult at the moment. The healthcare provider liability insurance product is entirely new, and there is very little earlier statistics to rely on. It is more other countries' practice," Murde-Parvell said.

Although premiums in the early years were high because of how the products were structured, she is optimistic. "This year the situation is already certainly considerably better and I believe next year it will be better still. There will probably be more new entrants by next year," Murde-Parvell said.

Because the statutory liability period is ten years, full statistics and clarity will take time to accumulate. "Complete knowledge of how many claims come and how many of them are actually justified will develop over years. And once it has developed, pricing will certainly be more transparent and easier to understand, and perhaps fairer too," she said.

Statistics: 75 percent of claims rejected

The Health Board publishes real-time statistics on its website on the application of patient insurance and the processing of claims.

From November 1, 2024 to October 27, 2026, a total of 1,148 compensation claims were submitted to insurers. Completed proceedings account for three-quarters: 863 claims have been reviewed, or 75.2 percent of all applications, while 285, or 24.8 percent, are still in progress.

Most claims are rejected. Of the 863 processed, 226 qualified as insured events, or 26.2 percent, while 637, or 73.8 percent, were not upheld. Across all claims submitted, upheld cases account for 19.7 percent and rejected ones 55.5 percent.

As many as 84.16 percent of compensated cases stem from direct medical error in diagnosis or treatment. Second among compensated cases are healthcare-associated infections at 9.5 percent, and wrong or unsuitable medicine or wrong dose at about 4.5 percent.

Nearly 59 percent of compensated cases fall into the middle damage category. Serious, irreversible or life-threatening harm accounts for about a third, 32.2 percent, of recognized claims. Minor harm accounts for under a tenth, 9.5 percent, suggesting claims are often not filed for lighter consequences or fall below the statutory compensation threshold.

A total of €1,077,228 has been paid out to patients. The average per compensated case is €5,886, and the largest single payout is €32,652.

The most claims were filed against emergency medicine departments, 180, which also produced the highest absolute number of insured events, 46. Family medicine is second by number of claims at 159, but its approval rate is exceptionally low: of 121 completed proceedings, only 12, or 9.9 percent, were recognized as insured events.

In orthopaedics, 34.6 percent, general surgery, 35.1 percent, obstetrics, 29.8 percent, and maxillofacial surgery, 31.6 percent, the approval rate remains steadily around a third.

More claims in 2026

As of 11 months into 2026, 664 compensation claims have been filed with insurers, exceeding the whole of 2025, 469 claims, by more than 41 percent.

Where only 29 claims, 6.2 percent, were unresolved in 2025, 256, or 38.55 percent of all applications, are in proceedings in 2026 — pointing to a multiplied workload for processors and to the fact that the speed of decisions cannot keep pace with the inflow.

Where family medicine was second by number of claims in 2025 with 56, in 2026 it has risen to first with 103. At the same time its approval rate has remained marginal.

The Health Insurance Fund (Tervisekassa) paid healthcare providers €6 million in 2025 to cover patient insurance costs, and €6 million is planned for 2026. Providers must add the same amount again from their own budgets each year, because the Health Insurance Fund covers up to 50 percent of the premium. That made last year's total insurance cost to the Estonian healthcare system an estimated €12 million.

World.title: Minister replaces Eesti 200 defector on Integration Foundation board
World.content:
Jašin was formerly a member of the coalition Eesti 200 party, but left it earlier this month to join the Social Democrats (SDE), who are in opposition.

According to the minister's directive, the proposal to recall Jašin, once touted as a possible future party leader, was made by Eesti 200 itself on October 15, the day after he left the party.

The party's letter is classified in the ministry's document register as being for internal use only, under a provision covering information containing personal data whose disclosure could significantly harm the data subject's privacy.

The replacement is not in itself unexpected: the foundation's board traditionally includes representatives of the relevant ministries, parties represented at the Riigikogu, and experts in the field, and Jašin had been from the second of these categories.

Via the same directive, Purga appointed Nikita Lumijõe to the same position for a three-year term. Lumijõe has been an Eesti 200 member since 2018 and works as an adviser to Education Minister Kristina Kallas, who is also Eesti 200's leader. SDE was in office with Reform and Eesti 200 until spring last year and has a representative on the XXX board in Henri Kaselo, formerly Kohtla-Järve's mayor.

Jašin was a member of Eesti 200 from November 19, 2018 until October 2, 2026, and joined SDE on October 14. Before the switch he had been discussed as a possible new leader of Eesti 200, and is a former Tallinn deputy mayor.

The Integration Foundation (Integratsiooni Sihtasutus) supports the development of an integrated and cohesive society as a competence center in the field, with both foreign residents of Estonia and Estonians living outside the country being in its target groups, the organization says on its website.

World.title: Iraqi PM visits Sayyida Zaynab shrine in Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited on Wednesday the holy Sayyida Zaynab shrine in the Syrian capital, Damascus, as part of his first official visit to the neighboring country.

Al-Zaidi’s trip to Syria is significant, as it marks the first visit by an Iraqi prime minister since the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024.

Al-Zaidi was accompanied by Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and visited Islamic sites in Damascus, where he also engaged in religious and financial diplomacy.

The prime minister offered prayers at the prominent Shia pilgrimage site, which is widely believed to house the tomb of Zainab bint Ali, the granddaughter of Prophet Muhammad.

Al-Zaidi also toured the historic Umayyad Mosque located in the heart of the Syrian capital.

The prime minister contributed $10 million from his personal finances, allocating $5 million to the Umayyad Mosque and $5 million to the Sayyida Zaynab shrine.

Beyond his religious visits, al-Zaidi held high-level discussions with Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa. The two leaders discussed building a mutually beneficial partnership that goes beyond religious differences.

The two sides discussed the possible revival of the Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline to export Iraqi oil via Syrian Mediterranean ports, offering Iraq a strategic alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

The two leaders also discussed approaches to enhance intelligence sharing, border controls, and counter-terrorism coordination, as well as protocols to safely receive Iraqi pilgrims heading to sacred sites in Syria.

World.title: Turkey welcomes Iraqi security measures in Sinjar as crucial step for stability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ankara officially welcomed recent military and security measures undertaken by the Iraqi federal government to consolidate state authority and establish full sovereign control over Sinjar District in Nineveh Governorate, characterizing the assumption of security command by official Iraqi security forces as a pivotal step toward achieving lasting regional stability.

Speaking during a weekly press briefing, Spokesperson for the Turkish Ministry of National Defense, Rear Admiral Zeki Aktürk, stated that Turkey welcomes Baghdad’s focused efforts to normalize conditions in Sinjar and eliminate non-state armed threats.

Aktürk emphasized that ending the illicit presence of terrorist networks and transferring territorial security administration directly to Iraq’s official federal security institutions represent an essential milestone for securing permanent peace across the border area, adding that Turkish authorities continue to track developments on the ground in close coordination with Iraqi counterparts.

World.title: Iraq’s Development Road will provide 100,000 job opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Transport announced on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, that engineering designs for the strategic Iraq Development Road project have entered their final phases and will be fully completed before the end of the current year, clearing the path for ground-level execution to commence in 2027.

The ministry noted that the transit corridor will generate over one million jobs across its lifespan, including 100,000 opportunities during Phase 1.

Speaking to Al Iraqiya News in remarks monitored by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Ministry of Transport Spokesperson Ali Al-Khalidi stated that technical designs for the high-speed railway network have surpassed a 95% completion rate, while engineering blueprints for the parallel motorway stand at 92%.

Al-Khalidi characterized the multi-billion-dollar transit corridor as a generational economic artery connecting the Gulf to Europe, with the project’s first operational phase slated for completion by 2033.

The dual-track road and railway network originates at the Grand Faw Port in Basra and traverses ten governorates and districts—passing through Dhi Qar, Al-Muthanna, Al-Diwaniyah, Najaf, Karbala, southern Anbar, Abu Ghraib in Baghdad, Samarra, and Mosul, before terminating at Fishkhabur on the Iraq–Turkey border.

Al-Khalidi noted that technical and commercial negotiations remain underway with international infrastructure consortiums, alongside ongoing coordination with the Turkish government through bilateral working committees, affirming that final contracts for primary engineering procurement and construction (EPC) packages have not yet been awarded.

Beyond direct transit capacity, the corridor’s master plan integrates modern passenger stations, logistical logistics hubs, smart communities, and dedicated industrial and residential zones along the route, forming an integrated economic spine designed to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

World.title: Iraq to host Baghdad International Energy Forum in January
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil has announced on Wednesday that it is planning to organize the next Baghdad International Energy Forum entitled “Towards the Optimal Investment in Oil and Gas” in Baghdad on January 20–21, 2027.

The organizing committee has announced the completion of all logistical and technical preparations for the launch of the forum, which will be held under the auspices of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and will be attended by energy ministers from around the world, as well as heads of major corporations and specialized international organizations.

The strategic event aims to highlight the latest and most significant investment opportunities in Iraq’s oil and gas sectors, in line with the government’s vision to establish Baghdad as an important hub in regional and global energy markets, according to a statement released by the Oil Ministry.

The organizing committee has extended formal invitations to ministers of energy and petroleum, heads of international agencies, and business executives.

The forum aims to provide a high-level dialogue platform that facilitates the creation of sustainable international partnerships, attracts cutting-edge technological solutions, and supports infrastructure development efforts.

The event is part of the Iraqi government’s initiatives to guarantee the most effective use of the country’s resources.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate remains steady in Baghdad, rises in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar remained stable on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and rose in the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate remained stable in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,678 Iraqi dinars throughout the day.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,682.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,672.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate rose, fluctuating between 1,677 and 1,676 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following a cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraq seeks cooperation with Russia in oil, gas industries
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Deputy Minister of Oil for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber emphasized on Tuesday Iraq’s interest in developing cooperation with Russia in the oil and gas sectors.

Saber’s remarks took place during his meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of their participation in the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF), held between October 25 and 27 in Moscow.

According to Saber, Iraq seeks to leverage Russia’s advanced expertise and foster partnerships and joint ventures that optimally utilize natural resources and advance the energy sector.

Saber conveyed the Iraqi president’s and the prime minister’s greetings to Putin, emphasizing their commitment to promoting bilateral relations and broadening the scope of cooperation to serve the interests of the two countries.

The GECF addressed developments in the world’s gas markets and approaches to enhance cooperation among producing countries.

The forum also discussed strategies to attract investments and develop infrastructure to guarantee supply security and meet the growing demand for energy throughout the world.

World.title: Iraqi PM arrives in Damascus for an official visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived in Damascus on Wednesday for an official visit to Syria, where he will meet President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

The trip marks the first high-profile visit by an Iraqi premier to Syria since the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024 and the establishment of al-Sharaa’s administration.

Al-Zaidi is accompanied by a high-level ministerial delegation aiming to strengthen economic, political, and security connections with the neighboring country.

The Iraqi prime minister’s agenda in Syria includes expanding commercial partnerships in trade, transport, agriculture, and water.

The two leaders are expected to focus on expanding oil export routes, following a memorandum of understanding signed earlier to revive a pipeline linking Iraq’s oil output to the port of Baniyas on the Mediterranean.

The discussions are expected to cover tightening control over shared borders and aligning counter-terrorism efforts. Al-Sharaa noted ahead of the visit that the border is secure and that intelligence and military coordination are actively underway.

The two leaders’ meeting is the second after they met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Syria signals a broader strategy by both nations to transition neighborhood ties into sustainable developmental and security frameworks.

World.title: Trump tamed after US midterms? Europe doubts it
World.content:
Brussels – President Donald Trump may be facing a political pounding at the US midterm elections next month — but in Europe expectations are low that a big Democrat win would change much.

From the battlefields of Ukraine to the boardrooms of Europe, Trump has sent multiple shockwaves across the continent since returning to power last year.

During a head-spinning 22 months, the mercurial leader has turned spectacularly on Kyiv, imposed tariffs on allies and threatened to take Greenland.

Ahead of the November 3 polls it looks like American voters could punish Trump’s Republican party and hand control of one or both of the US House of Representatives or Senate to the Democrats.

But while the hope may be that Trump could be reined in by a hostile Congress, multiple officials at the EU and NATO told AFP they doubt a big loss would muzzle him on the international stage.

“We don’t think the unpredictability is going to change,” said one senior EU diplomat.

Publicly the European Union is keeping its cards close to its chest.

“We will not comment on any elections in the EU or abroad. Let’s wait for those and we’ll see where it goes,” said European Commission spokeswoman Paula Pinho.

Behind closed doors as well, officials say that the midterms are not featuring much in the bloc’s internal discussions.

“I suspect because a) it is difficult to really predict the result, b) one wouldn’t want to get too high hopes for change and c) not sure how much even a Democratic wave would impact foreign policy issues,” said a second senior EU diplomat.

– Ukraine, tariffs –

Ahead of the midterms, Trump has rattled Europe by yet again lashing out at Ukraine and cosying up to Russia as Washington has renewed its push to end the fighting.

While a Democrat win could usher in a more vocal pro-Kyiv majority in Congress, the EU is not expecting US support for Ukraine to ramp up again.

Officials in Brussels say they are focused on plugging a 70-billion-euro hole in Kyiv’s finances next year.

And while they’re pushing other countries like Britain, Canada and Japan to do more, they are certainly not counting on the United States.

Meanwhile, there is equally little optimism for any major reversal on the tariffs Trump has slapped on Europe.

Diplomats and officials point out that it took months to get Democrat President Joe Biden to roll back tariffs on EU steel after Trump’s first term — and even then limitations remained.

In a recent poll from the Washington-based Council on Foreign Relations, only one quarter of Americans backed removing all the tariffs on the EU.

– US forces in Europe? –

At NATO the story is much the same.

European allies are nervously waiting for the results of a Pentagon review of US forces on the continent that looks set to be unveiled in December.

The widespread expectation is that it will see the United States scale back its deployments, although the hope is the cuts will not be too severe.

Multiple diplomats at NATO said they didn’t envision the midterms having an impact on the review.

While a changed Congress could see US lawmakers more outspoken in support of the alliance, the direction of travel is already set with Europe stepping up efforts to take more responsibility for its defence.

“Whatever the outcome, we’ll keep going,” said one European diplomat.

– Trump unleashed? –

There is also a nagging fear that things could get worse after the midterms.

If Republicans cling on it could embolden Trump, meanwhile if they lose, he could seek to distract from his woes at home by stirring up things abroad.

“We have a history in America of presidents who get in trouble domestically turning more to the international stage,” said Bruce Stokes, a visiting fellow at the German Marshall Fund think tank.

From an escalation in the Iran war to a more concerted push on Ukraine, there are numerous ways the White House can keep worrying Europe.

“Trump has demonstrated they can’t stand not to be the centre of attention,” said Stokes.

“If that means he needs to do more on the world stage, positively or negatively, that may be what ends up happening.”

World.title: ‘Unwavering commitment’: Rajnath Singh backs ASEAN centrality, calls for stronger defence ties
World.content:
Defence minister

on Thursday reaffirmed Indiaâs commitment to ASEAN centrality and called for stronger defence cooperation and mutual trust at the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministersâ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines.

He said the forum was important for maintaining a resilient, secure and prosperous region, adding that the discussions should help address emerging disruptions and strengthen cooperation among participating countries.

âI look forward to constructive deliberations and concrete outcomes from this meeting,â Singh said.

Philippine defence secretary Gilberto C Teodoro Jr, meanwhile, said two documents were signed at the ADMM the previous day â a joint statement commemorating the 50th anniversary of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia and the Manila Joint Declaration marking the 20th anniversary of the ADMM.

Teodoro said the documents reaffirmed the participating countriesâ commitment to shared principles, ASEAN unity and centrality.





He outlined three priorities for the meeting: ensuring cooperation is guided by mutual respect and international law, sustaining progress under the ADMM-Plus framework, and addressing the wider impact of global disruptions.

Highlighting the importance of food and energy security amid supply chain challenges and overseas conflicts, Teodoro also called for greater cooperation to protect migrant workers and seafarers, particularly those from smaller countries caught in conflict zones.

World.title: MEA says 22 Indians killed during West Asia conflict

Twenty-two Indians, including 14 seafarers, have so far lost their lives in the West Asia conflict, said govt, expressing deep concern over the situation in the region. âWe are deeply concerned about the ongoing conflict in West Asia.

World.title: Supreme Court removes October 30 deadline for additions to Delhi electoral roll
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a relief to over 43 lakh voters excluded from Delhiâs draft electoral rolls for âpermanently shifting outâ, Supreme Court on Wednesday asked Election Commission not to stop adding names in the voter list by the Oct 30 deadline and told it to continue distributing and receiving enumeration forms, and Forms 6 (new voters), 7 (for deletion) and 8 (for those who shifted from one constituency to another).

A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also questioned EC on why voters whose names were there on earlier electoral rolls but were deleted from the draft rolls were asked to file Form 6, which is meant for enrolment of first-time voters.

Without passing any order, the bench said, âWe will examine the issue after two weeks. The effort should be to reduce the 43 lakh (who have been deleted from draft rolls).

One suggestion â publish the list of those who are deleted and specify the reason for deletion against each name. Request them to contact the nearest BLO and fill Form 8. You can give them enumeration forms. Tell them that they are welcome to fill either Form 6 or 8.

â

How can you insist on Form 6 for person who was voter earlier: SC

During the proceedings on a PIL filed by activist Anjali Bhardwaj, the bench heard advocate Prashant Bhushanâs complaints against EC for insisting on filling Form 6 by those whose names got excluded and, thereby, compelling them to give a false declaration that they were first-time voters.





The bench said, âRight to vote is a vital right. If a person has shifted out from Vasant Kunj to Dwarka, or had gone out of station for a month or so and for some other reason could not respond to the EC notice or could not file the claim for inclusion of name, or did not get enumeration form because of change of address, should EC permanently disable him from voting by striking his name off the voter list?

âHow can you insist on Form 6 for a person who was a voter earlier? If a person has shifted from one constituency to another within Delhi, it is erroneous to ask him/her to fill Form 6.

You must allow similarly placed persons, whose names are deleted on the ground of âpermanently shiftedâ, to fill Form 8.â

Appearing for EC, senior advocate D S Naidu said the commission had conducted over one lakh camps in Delhi to spread awareness among people on how to re-enter their names in the voter list.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âThe situation on the ground is very different. Not a single person has come to fill Form 8. The petitioner is creating a scare on paper in the courtroom.

Any person can seek inclusion of his/her name in the voter list of a constituency till the date of filing of nominations,â Naidu said, and clarified that no one has been prosecuted for using Form 6 to restore names in voter lists across states.

But EC relented to keep the window open for inclusion of names in Delhi as SC insisted that the Oct 30 deadline for filing claims and objections need not be set in stone as elections were not imminent in Delhi to warrant urgent completion of the SIR exercise.

World.title: Isro to launch NVS-03 on Oct 30, but NavIC has a long way to go
World.content:
BENGALURU: Isro will launch its next navigation satellite, NVS-03, aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket on Friday (Oct 30) at 11.51 pm from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

GSLV-F18 is the 20th flight of Indiaâs Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV). The mission is a crucial attempt to rebuild Indiaâs ailing NavIC navigation constellation, which currently lacks enough operational satellites to provide standalone positioning services.

The roughly 50-metre rocket, with a lift-off mass of about 420 tonnes, will place the approximately 2,250-kg NVS-03 into a geosynchronous transfer orbit with a perigee (closest point to Earth) of 170 km, apogee (farthest point from Earth) of 37,023 km and inclination of 20.75Â°.

Why the launch matters

NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isroâs next-generation navigation series, designed to ensure continuity of the services of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, now called Navigation with Indian Constellation, or NavIC.

NavIC is intended to provide Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) services across India and up to about 1,500 km beyond the countryâs landmass, reducing dependence on foreign navigation systems.





âNVS-03 carries an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured clocks and introduces the L1 signal, in addition to the existing L5 and S signals,â Isro said. The addition is expected to widen compatibility with more user devices and strengthen NavICâs civilian and strategic utility.

But the launch comes at a time when NavIC is operating below its minimum requirement. Earlier this year, union minister Jitendra Singh told Parliament: âAfter completion of mission life (10 years) of IRNSS-1F, presently the NavIC constellation has three satellites â IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 â for providing PNT services.

To provide basic positioning service, a minimum of four operational satellites are required in orbit.â The govt acknowledged that, as a result, âthe NavIC constellation cannot provide standalone positioning service, however timing service is functional.â

A troubled programme

NavICâs difficulties stem from a combination of ageing satellites, atomic-clock failures and a failed replenishment mission. IRNSS-1F completed its 10-year mission life in March 2026; soon after, Isro said its procured onboard atomic clock stopped functioning, removing the satellite from navigation service.

The more immediate setback was NVS-02, launched on Jan 29, 2025 aboard GSLV-F15. Although the satellite separated successfully and deployed its solar panels, it could not perform the orbit-raising manoeuvres needed to move from its elliptical transfer orbit to its designated circular orbit.

An Isro apex committee traced the anomaly to the spacecraftâs pyro system. It found that the drive signal did not reach the pyro valve in the oxidiser line of the orbit-raising engine, preventing the engine from firing.

The committee concluded that the most likely cause was disengagement of at least one contact in each of the main and redundant connector paths.

Isro said the panel recommended corrective measures to enhance redundancy and improve the reliability of pyro-system operations, and that these recommendations have already been implemented.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Still a long road

NVS-03âs successful launch would raise the number of navigation-capable satellites, but it will not by itself restore NavIC to full operational strength.

The spacecraft must first complete orbit-raising manoeuvres, reach its designated orbit and be validated for service.

The govt has said NVS-04 and NVS-05 are in an advanced stage of realisation, meaning further launches will be needed before NavIC regains a robust, redundant constellation.

NavICâs return to standalone positioning service depends not only on NVS-03 reaching orbit, but on Isro executing the post-launch operations that failed for NVS-02, and on the timely induction of the satellites that follow.

World.title: IN-SPACe picks 6 AI space projects for grants of up to Rs 1-cr each
World.content:
BENGALURU: Space regulator-cum-promoter Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected six private space-sector entities for seed-fund grants under its AI INSPIRED programme, which aims to encourage the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in space technology.

The projects span precision landing, space situational awareness, debris detection, satellite servicing and refuelling, automated target recognition, and spacecraft autonomy. Two other entities have been selected for mentorship and technical support, including access to Isro facilities for technology validation.

The programme, announced in Feb 2026 under IN-SPACeâs Seed Fund Scheme, has a total outlay of up to Rs 6 crore, with each selected entity eligible for a grant of up to Rs 1 crore.

The funding is intended to help start-ups and micro and small enterprises develop AI-based solutions for space applications.

Among the selected projects, Agnikul Cosmos will develop an edge AI-enabled vision-based terminal navigation module for precision landing. The technology is aimed at improving navigation during the final stages of a landing manoeuvre.

Digantara has been selected for its Agentic RSO Evaluation Suite (ARES), while EON Space Labs will develop an intelligent optical payload using field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based edge AI.





The latter project aims to enable real-time space situational awareness and detection of space debris.

OrbitAid Aerospace will work on machine-learning-assisted pose estimation algorithms for on-orbit servicing and refuelling. Such algorithms can help spacecraft determine their relative positions and orientations, an important requirement for operations involving approaching, docking with or servicing another spacecraft.

Omnipresent Robot Technologies has been selected for an automated target recognition project covering applications such as defence and docking. TakeMeToSpace will work on adaptive spacecraft autonomy through an AI modernisation programme for attitude determination and control systems (ADCS), which help establish a spacecraft's orientation and maintain its intended direction.

IN-SPACe has also selected Foucault Private Limited and AkashaVeda Technologies for mentorship and technical support, although they are not listed among the six seed-fund grantees.

Foucault will work on an autonomous collision avoidance system for spacecraft using AI and machine learning. AkashaVedaâs project focuses on AI-based mission management, covering both onboard and ground operations. The two entities will receive opportunities to use IN-SPACe and Isro facilities to validate their technologies. They will also be considered for technology transfer from the Department of Space.

As per IN-SPACe, the initiative is part of its efforts to expand private participation in Indiaâs space sector by supporting the development of indigenous technologies and products.

World.title: The Madras Warp explores culture and memory through 16 artists at Lalit Kala Akademi
World.content:
Like threads woven together to create a fabric, 16 contemporary artists come together in The Madras Warp, an upcoming exhibition at Lalit Kala Akademi that explores the many ways art engages with culture, identity, memory and place. Opening on November 1, the exhibition brings together artists from Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Kerala. Spanning painting, photography, printmaking, mixed media and installation art, it offers a glimpse into the diverse perspectives shaping contemporary art today.

Tangible forms

Take, for instance, artist Rishi Sasi’s work, which uses collage as his visual language; his artworks begin with a question, conflict, or circumstance and gradually transform into a visual dialogue. “My work explores the subtle interplay between memory, thought and time. It is essentially a desire to translate intangible things into tangible forms, such as dreams, memories and impressions,” says Rishi.

Two of his works are inspired by photographs from his trip to Lwani village in Uttarakhand, made using photographs, overlapping papers, paper boards, and found objects to create collage-like visuals; the works create dreamlike visuals that call for careful observation. “Through this exploration, I aim to evoke a sense of timelessness and complexity, where personal experiences and shared memories interact,” he adds.

In another work, artist and photographer Hemant Kumar uses printmaking to create awareness about the endangered species around us. Each print, he says, “is carved from wood layer by layer, capturing the beauty of the wildlife we can no longer take for granted.” The three artworks made from woodcut prints showcase species like the vanishing green slender loris, the Malabar large-spotted civet, and the green Nilgiri marten. His works also remind us of how rapid urbanisation and canopy loss have driven some of these species to extinction.

Artist Manimaran Rajapandian connects his work to a childhood habit of finding faces in everyday things. “There are mountains, plains and rivers, each with its own form and flow. It reminds me of how our emotions and moods keep changing, taking different forms and flowing differently at different times,” says Manimaran. Two of his artworks relate cartographic features on maps to human emotions.

Landscapes of belonging

“An artwork begins with the artist, but its story continues with everyone who encounters it,” says curator and participating artist Nivetha Mailasini.

For the exhibition, her works explore landscapes as “collective drawings made by people over time”. From afar, the artworks look like a block of colours red, crimson, and green but look closer and reveal more. “The roads, settlements, and agricultural fields become visible traces of culture, memory, labour, and belonging. I explore how the land holds the presence of human life, even when individual stories remain unseen,” says Nivetha.

Stories of resilience and grief also find expression in the exhibition. Artist Selin Sabashini takes a multidisciplinary approach, working with acrylics, paper-mâché, wood and interactive installations to explore patriarchal structures, the stages of grief following her mother’s death, and the challenges of living with chronic, invisible pain.

Artist Vidya Lalgudi Jaishankar’s Artwork titled Recovering -1, made with watercolour, ink and gouache on watercolour paper, was painted during a period of physical recovery following ear surgery. “It emerged from a time of vulnerability, when my usual rhythms had been interrupted,” says Vidya. Her practice began with an exploration of the spaces between verbal and non-verbal communication, gradually expanding into a broader inquiry into how information and experiences shift as they move between forms.

“My work engages with the relationships between perception, memory, the body and time, investigating how experiences take on new meanings when encountered through different mediums,” says Vidya.

Symbolic Expressionism

“I have always been drawn to old walls, abandoned places, eroded surfaces, and the unusual patterns that emerge through wear and tear. To me, these surfaces are not merely damaged or forgotten; they hold traces of time, memory, and human presence,” says artist Helen Jenifer. Her works belong to the genre of Symbolic Expressionism, a fusion of abstract figuration, emotional expression, and philosophical storytelling.

One of her artworks The Eye of Perception, made with mixed media on canvas, brings forth a divine messenger, the goddess of empathy, who offers humanity the ability to truly see one another. “Her outstretched hand presents the symbolic eye of perception, inviting us to perceive not with judgment, but with compassion. Through this act, she grants viewers the power to understand the emotions and struggles of others, a gift that leads to harmony and kindness,” says Helen.

The Madras Warp will be on at Lalit Kala Akademi, Greams Road from November 1 to 7. Entry is free and open to all.

World.title: Maharashtra MLC election: Congress trumps BJP in Nagpur, MVA leads 3-2 in State
World.content:
Congress trumped the Bharatiya Janata Party in Nagpur during the Legislative Council elections in Maharashtra. Of the five graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies which went to the polls, theOpposition alliance of Maha Vikas Aghadi won three seats.

In the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA), Sharad Pawar’s NCP SP won two of the three seats, while Congress won the prestigious battle of Nagpur. The ruling Mahayuti alliance secured two seats. This is the second time the Congress has defeated the BJP on its home turf of Nagpur, the seat of the RSS headquarters. The party had guarded the seat for 58 years before losing it to Congress for the first time in the year 2020.

While the NCP SP called for going back to ballot papers for holding elections, the BJP called for introspection among the alliance partners. The election results have caused an embarrassment for the ruling alliance of Mahayuti.

Congress’ sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari secured 67,231 votes, while the BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale secured 63,960 votes. “It is not always the strength which helps you win you elections. Sometimes, an idea works better. Shaktipeksha yukti shreshtha (An idea is stronger than might). We strategised well,” Mr. Wanjari said after being elected.

“The illusionary bubble of Modi and Fadnavis has burst. MVA has registered a resounding victory in three seats in the Legislative Council elections,” Maharashtra Congress president Harshawardhan Sapkal posted. He said that despite having money and muscle power, the BJP stood defeated.

“In the city of RSS headquarters Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, the Congress has defeated the BJP for the second consecutive term,” he said.

NCP SP leader Supriya Sule congratulated the party’s victorious candidate Harshada Deshmukh Jadhav by performing a ceremonial blessing by waving aarti lamp around her.

On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the opposition hit out at the BJP over its “arrogance” and “overconfidence”. It targeted Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis over a deleted post on X, which had responded to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s post asking how many seats Congress had won in the elections held on ballot paper.

“Since the ballot paper has shown what the Honourable Prime Minister says, then our country should now move back to the voting system of using ballot papers. Requesting PM Modi ji must make a move in that direction,” NCP SP national spokesperson Clyde Crasto said.

NCP SP leaders Rohit Pawar and Mr. Crastro shared screenshots of the allegedly deleted post of Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, saying it reeked of arrogance. “Our party wins two, and Congress wins one MLC seat in Maharashtra. MVA gets three of five; arrogance and overconfidence caused Mr. Devendra Fadnavis and Mahayuti grave embarrassment. Reminder to BJP leaders, these elections were held using ‘Ballot Papers’,” posted Mr. Crasto.

NCP SP MLA Rohit Pawar said it was sad that the CM had to delete his post. He said there was a message for the BJP in these election results, particularly in Nagpur. “You had personally paid attention to the Nagpur graduates’ constituency election. You had gone door-to-door to convince rebels to withdraw from the polls. This is in Nagpur, in the headquarters of the RSS that the BJP had to see defeat,” he said, adding that the “ego of power” in CM’s deleted post did not reflect well.

World.title: Traders seek action against street vendors, encroachments in Dharwad
World.content:
The traders’ association has urged the authorities to curb unregulated street vending and remove encroachments on public spaces in Dharwad, alleging that they were affecting local businesses and causing inconvenience to pedestrians.

Speaking at a press conference on October 28, association representative Deepak Rege said street vending had increased along Subhash Road, around Lakshmi Narayan temple, and near Basel Mission School. The presence of street vendors is affecting the movement of customers, and hurting the business of local shopkeepers and hotel owners who pay rent, taxes, and licence fees, he said.

Mr. Rege said encroachments had made roads unsafe for pedestrians, schoolchildren, senior citizens, and persons with disabilities. He called on food safety officials to test food sold by street vendors for possible contamination and take appropriate action based on the findings.

He said temporary vending arrangements made for nine days during the Lakshmi Narayan temple fair had continued for nearly a month. Claiming that many vendors had come from outside Dharwad, he urged the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation to clarify the duration, locations, and conditions of the permissions granted to them.

The association was not opposed to street vendors earning a livelihood, Mr. Rege said, adding that they should be provided designated vending zones and suitable rehabilitation. However, their activities should not inconvenience established traders or other people, he said, urging elected representatives to co-operate with the authorities in finding a permanent solution.
